title: 10  Shared options
text:
10.1 Charts
Option groups taken by several charts, builders or data functions, documented once here. A chart’s page lists the groups it takes and which of their keys (a chart may take only part of a group); builder tables mark the rows of a group with its title.
Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

title: 10  Shared options
text:
10.1.1 Common options
Every chart may read its own rows and merge its own mapping over the plot’s - e.g. a reference curve beside the data (Data and mapping chapter) - and leave its key glyph out of the legends.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:data
a sequence of rows (maps) or a map of columns (sequences) or nil
the plot's :data
the chart's own data instead of the plot's


:mapping
a mapping: key -> accessor (a keyword or a function of a row)

the chart's mapping, merged over the plot's mapping (a key set to nil removes it)


:legend
true or false or nil
true
draw the chart's key glyph in the legends (false - the chart adds none, a legend no chart keys is dropped; its aesthetics still scale)






(plot/render-image {:data wave
                    :mapping {:x :t :y :v}
                    :charts [(chart/scatter)
                             (chart/line {:data (for [t (range 0 30 0.5)] {:t t :v (m/sin (m/* 0.3 t))})})]}
                   {:width 500 :height 250})




:legend false keeps a chart’s glyph out of the legend while its colours still follow the scale: the rug’s ticks would otherwise be drawn over the scatter’s dots in every key (left). A legend no chart draws a key into is dropped.

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange (for [legend [true false]]
                                   {:data wave
                                    :mapping {:x :t :y :v :color #(if (m/pos? (double (:v %))) "up" "down")}
                                    :charts [(chart/scatter) (chart/rug {:mapping {:y nil} :legend legend})]
                                    :labels {:title (str "rug :legend " legend)}})
                                 {:columns 2})
                   {:width 800 :height 250})






10.1.2 Annotation options
The rule, rect and text charts mark literal positions. By default their positions count for the scales (the axis reaches them); :extent false leaves them out - the rule at y = 2 is then off the panel (right).





Option
Type
Default
Description




:extent
true or false or nil
true
include the positions in the scale extents






(plot/render-image (plot/arrange (for [extent [true false]]
                                   {:data wave
                                    :mapping {:x :t :y :v}
                                    :charts [(chart/line) (chart/rule {:y 2 :extent extent :dash :dashed})]
                                    :labels {:title (str ":extent " extent)}})
                                 {:columns 2})
                   {:width 800 :height 250})






10.1.3 Line style
Colour, width and dash of the lines of line-like charts (line, rule, segment, smooth, density, ecdf …); a mapped aesthetic wins over the fixed value.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:color
a clojure2d color or :none

line colour (a mapped :color wins)


:line-width
a non-negative number

line width in pixels


:dash
:none, a dash style (:dashed :dot-dash :dot-dot-dash :dotted :long-dash :loose-dot :solid :two-dash) or a sequence of positive numbers or nil

dash style of the line (a mapped :dash wins)






(plot/render-image {:data wave
                    :mapping {:x :t :y :v}
                    :charts [(chart/line {:color [178 34 34] :line-width 3 :dash [6 2]})]}
                   {:width 500 :height 250})




Every built-in dash style (a dash may also be a vector of dash and gap lengths, as above):

(plot/render-image {:charts (vec (mapcat (fn [i d]
                                           [(chart/rule {:y i :dash d :line-width 2})
                                            (chart/text {:x 0 :y i :text (str d) :anchor [:left :bottom]})])
                                         (range 1 100) (:dash describe/attribute-values)))
                    :scales {:x {:domain [0 1] :axis false} :y {:domain [0 9] :reverse true :axis false}}}
                   {:width 500 :height 320})






10.1.4 Curves
The line between data points of lines and ribbons: straight, a fastmath interpolation or a step, sampled for drawing.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:interpolator
a fastmath 1D interpolation method keyword or a function (fn [xs ys & params] f)

interpolation of the line between data points (none - straight segments)


:interpolator-params
vector of any value

extra parameters passed to the interpolation method


:curve
one of :parametric :bezier

path curve instead of a function of x: :parametric (x(t), y(t) over the chord length) or :bezier


:sample-step
a positive number of pixels or {:count n}, n >= 2
1.0
distance between evaluated positions: pixels or {:count n} per run






(def points (for [x (range 8)] {:x x :y (nth [1 3 2 5 4 4.5 2 3] x)}))






x
y




0
1


1
3


2
2


3
5


4
4


5
4.5


6
2


7
3






(plot/render-image (plot/arrange (for [interpolator [:linear :monotone :cubic :step]]
                                   {:data points
                                    :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
                                    :charts [(chart/line {:interpolator interpolator}) (chart/scatter)]
                                    :labels {:title (str ":interpolator " interpolator)}})
                                 {:columns 4})
                   {:width 1000 :height 260})




Every interpolation method (schema/interpolation-methods) through the same points, with default parameters - most pass through them or smooth them; :pava and :cir fit a monotone curve - :pava flat runs joined by a step, :cir flat, then sloping; :kriging stays near a constant (its variogram is fitted to the points, by a seeded search, so every render draws the same curve), and :gp / :rbf use a kernel too narrow for points this far apart:

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange (for [interpolator (sort schema/interpolation-methods)]
                                   {:data points
                                    :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
                                    :charts [(chart/line {:interpolator interpolator}) (chart/scatter {:size 4})]
                                    :labels {:title (str interpolator)}})
                                 {:columns 4})
                   {:width 1000 :height 800})




:interpolator-params are the method’s arguments after the points - for :gp and :rbf a fastmath kernel. A curve is fitted in pixels along the line’s horizontal axis, so the kernel’s width is in pixels: here 60, a bit more than the gap between the points:

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data points
                                   :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
                                   :charts [(chart/line {:interpolator :gp :interpolator-params [(k/kernel :gaussian {:sigma 60.0})]})
                                            (chart/scatter {:size 4})]
                                   :labels {:title ":gp, gaussian kernel sigma 60"}}
                                  {:data points
                                   :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
                                   :charts [(chart/line {:interpolator :rbf :interpolator-params [(k/rbf :gaussian {:scale 60.0})]})
                                            (chart/scatter {:size 4})]
                                   :labels {:title ":rbf, gaussian scale 60"}}]
                                 {:columns 2})
                   {:width 800 :height 280})




Without an interpolator, :curve draws a smooth path through the points in their order - also a closed or looping one (:parametric, a Catmull-Rom curve; :bezier, bezier pieces); :sample-step sets how densely a curve is sampled (here coarse, to show the samples):

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange (for [[title opts] [[":curve :parametric" {:curve :parametric}]
                                                     [":curve :bezier" {:curve :bezier}]
                                                     [":sample-step 25 (cubic)" {:interpolator :cubic :sample-step 25}]]]
                                   {:data points
                                    :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
                                    :charts [(chart/line opts) (chart/scatter {:size 4})]
                                    :labels {:title title}})
                                 {:columns 3})
                   {:width 1000 :height 260})






10.1.5 Fill patterns
A pattern drawn over filled marks (bars, areas, boxes, tiles of hierarchies …), in its own colour.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:pattern
a pattern name (:back-hatch :cross :dense-dots :diagonal-cross :dots :hatch :horizontal :solid :vertical) or a pattern map

pattern drawn over the fill (a mapped :pattern wins)


:pattern-color
:darker or a clojure2d color or :none

pattern ink: a colour, :none or :darker (the darkened fill)






(plot/render-image {:data (for [[i p] (map-indexed vector [:hatch :back-hatch :cross :dots])] {:p (name p) :v (+ 3 i)})
                    :mapping {:x :p :y :v :pattern :p}
                    :charts [(chart/bar {:color :white :stroke-color :black :pattern-color :black})]
                    :legend false}
                   {:width 500 :height 260})






10.1.6 Rounded corners
Rounded bar corners: all of them, or only the end away from the baseline.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:corner-radius
a non-negative number
0
radius in pixels of every corner of a bar or rect


:corner-radius-end
a non-negative number

radius in pixels of the corners at the bar's value end only (wins over :corner-radius)






(plot/render-image {:data counts
                    :mapping {:x :k :y :v :color :g}
                    :charts [(chart/bar {:corner-radius-end 8})]}
                   {:width 500 :height 260})






10.1.7 Strip options
Strip charts (bar, box, violin, stripplot, beeswarm, dotplot, rug, bullet, extent) draw one item per level of a categorical axis.

10.1.7.1 Placement
Where the items sit across the value axis, how wide, and which axis holds the levels:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:place
{:at a finite number} or one of :band :bottom :center :edge
:band with a level mapping, else the chart's own (:center for most, :edge for the rug)
where the items sit across the value axis: :band (one band per level), {:at v} (centred on v of a numeric scale), :center, :edge or :bottom (between the panel edge and 0)


:width
a non-negative number
0.8
fraction an item spans across the value axis: of the level's band, of the panel for :center, of the room between the panel edge and 0 for :bottom


:thickness
a non-negative number
20 pixels for {:at v}, 8 for :edge
item thickness in pixels for :place {:at v} and :edge


:bottom-share
a number in [0 1]
0.15 with :place :bottom
padding below the data asked for with :place :bottom (only there), a fraction of the y data span


:level-axis
one of :x :y
the categorical axis of the mapping; with neither, :x when only :y is mapped, else :y
the mapping axis holding the levels (decides when both or neither of :x and :y are categorical)






(plot/render-image {:data iris
                    :mapping {:x :species :y :sepal-length}
                    :charts [(chart/violin {:width 0.9}) (chart/box {:width 0.15})]}
                   {:width 500 :height 280})




Without levels an item sits by :place: across the panel’s middle (:width a fraction of the panel), below the data (:bottom - the y axis reaches below zero, :width a fraction of the room under zero), at the panel’s edge or at a value of the other axis ({:at v}) - those two :thickness pixels thick. Here a box of the eruption times over the scatter:

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange (for [[place opts] [[:center {:width 0.15}] [:bottom {:width 0.8}]
                                                     [:edge {:thickness 12}] [{:at 60} {:thickness 20}]]]
                                   {:data faithful
                                    :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting}
                                    :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 4}) (chart/box (merge {:place place :mapping {:y nil}} opts))]
                                    :labels {:title (str ":place " place " " opts)}})
                                 {:columns 2})
                   {:width 900 :height 600})




:level-axis names the axis of the levels - needed when both axes or neither are categorical; here the rounded petal widths on y (0 to 3), declared categorical, are the levels, a strip of sepal lengths at each (points spread across the band by the stripplot’s seeded :jitter):

(plot/render-image {:data iris
                    :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y (levels/categorical #(m/round (:petal-width %)))}
                    :charts [(chart/stripplot {:level-axis :y :jitter 0.3 :rng (r/rng :mersenne 5)})]
                    :labels {:x "sepal length" :y "petal width, rounded"}}
                   {:width 500 :height 280})






10.1.7.2 Groups
Groups of one level share its band: side by side (:dodge, with a gap), on top of each other, or one half each (:mirror).





Option
Type
Default
Description




:position
one of :dodge :mirror :overlay
:dodge when a level holds two or more groups, else :overlay (dotplot: always :overlay)
how groups of one level share its band: :dodge (side by side), :overlay (on top of each other) or :mirror (two groups, one half each)


:dodge-gap
a number in [0 1]
0.1
gap between dodged groups, a fraction of a group's part of the band






(plot/render-image {:data counts
                    :mapping {:x :k :y :v :color :g}
                    :charts [(chart/bar {:position :dodge :dodge-gap 0.3})]}
                   {:width 500 :height 260})






10.1.7.3 Counts
Each item’s row count written past its largest value.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:n-label
true or false or nil
false
draw each item's row count just past its largest value


:n-format
a count format string or a function
"n=%d"
text of the n labels: a format string or a function of the count






(plot/render-image {:data iris
                    :mapping {:x :species :y :petal-length}
                    :charts [(chart/box {:n-label true :n-format "%d flowers"})]}
                   {:width 500 :height 280})







10.1.8 Mirrored strips
Two groups on the two sides of the value axis, e.g. a population pyramid.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:mirror
one of :color :shape :size :dash :pattern :group

a grouping dimension with exactly two levels; the second level's items are drawn on the negative side






(plot/render-image {:data counts
                    :mapping {:x :k :y :v :color :g}
                    :charts [(chart/bar {:mirror :color})]
                    :flip true
                    :scales {:x {:reverse true}}}
                   {:width 500 :height 260})




The same mirroring upright, and on a range chart (the second group’s intervals below the axis):

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data counts
                                   :mapping {:x :k :y :v :color :g}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:mirror :color})]
                                   :labels {:title "bar, :mirror :color"}}
                                  {:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :species :y :sepal-length :color #(if (< (:petal-width %) 1.3) "narrow" "wide")}
                                   :charts [(chart/extent {:mirror :color})]
                                   :labels {:title "extent, :mirror :color"}}]
                                 {:columns 2})
                   {:width 900 :height 300})






10.1.9 Ridgelines
Histograms and densities over a categorical axis - one row per level, overlapping by :overlap rows.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:overlap
a non-negative number
0.9
height of the tallest ridge in band steps (above 1 - ridges overlap the next level)






(plot/render-image {:data iris
                    :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :species :color :species}
                    :charts [(chart/density {:overlap 1.8 :fill :color :alpha 0.7})]
                    :scales {:y {:reverse true}}
                    :legend false}
                   {:width 500 :height 300})






10.1.10 Cell style
The cell shape and outline of grid-cell charts (tile, bin2d): any fastmath grid type, scaled. Every cell type binning the same points:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:cell
one of :square :shifted-square :triangle :rhombus :flat-hex :pointy-hex

cell shape of the grid (a fastmath grid cell type)


:cell-scale
a finite number, > 0, <= 1

cell polygon size relative to its grid cell, in (0 1]


:stroke-color
:darker or a clojure2d color or :none

cell outline: a colour, :none or :darker (the darkened fill)


:stroke-width
a non-negative number

cell outline width in pixels


:alpha-factor
a number in [0 1]

factor multiplying the fill colours' alpha






(plot/render-image (plot/arrange (for [cell (:cell describe/attribute-values)]
                                   {:data iris
                                    :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width}
                                    :charts [(chart/bin2d {:cell cell :stroke-color :white})]
                                    :labels {:title (str ":cell " cell)}
                                    :legend false})
                                 {:columns 3})
                   {:width 900 :height 560})






10.1.11 Fields
Raster and contour charts draw a scalar field.

10.1.11.1 A function
The field as a function of a point over a domain …





Option
Type
Default
Description
Group




:f
a function

the field as a function of a point [x y] returning a number (instead of mapped data)
Fields


:domain
map
the plot's explicit :x and :y scale domains
the domain of a function field
Fields


:domain :x (required)
[a finite number, a finite number]

x domain [lo hi]



:domain :y (required)
[a finite number, a finite number]

y domain [lo hi]







(plot/render-image {:charts [(chart/contour {:f (fn [[x y]] (+ (* x x) (* 2 y y))) :domain {:x [-2 2] :y [-2 2]}})]}
                   {:width 450 :height 350})






10.1.11.2 A density estimate
… or the kernel density estimate of mapped points …





Option
Type
Default
Description




:kernel
keyword
:gaussian
fastmath kernel of the 2D density estimate of mapped points


:bandwidth
a positive finite number or one of :nrd :nrd0 :nrd-adjust :sj :sj-dpi :rlcv :lcv :lscv :scott or [a positive finite number or one of :nrd :nrd0 :nrd-adjust :sj :sj-dpi :rlcv :lcv :lscv :scott, a positive finite number or one of :nrd :nrd0 :nrd-adjust :sj :sj-dpi :rlcv :lcv :lscv :scott]
:nrd per axis (MASS::kde2d, as ggplot2)
bandwidth of the density estimate: a number, a fastmath selector or :scott, or a pair [hx hy] of them


:binned
true or false
false
estimate the density from binned points (faster for many points)


:cut
a non-negative finite number
3
how many bandwidths the density domain extends past the points on each side






(plot/render-image {:data iris
                    :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width}
                    :charts [(chart/field {:kernel :epanechnikov :bandwidth 0.4}) (chart/scatter {:size 3})]}
                   {:width 450 :height 350})






10.1.11.3 The grid
… sampled on a grid of :n points per axis (interpolating gridded data with :interpolation).





Option
Type
Default
Description




:interpolation
one of :bilinear :bicubic :cubic-2d
:bilinear
interpolation of gridded data (mapped :x, :y, :value on a full lattice)


:n
integer (2..2000) or [integer (2..2000), integer (2..2000)]
100
grid size: values sampled along each axis, or [nx ny]






(plot/render-image {:charts [(chart/field {:f (fn [[x y]] (m/sin (m/* x y))) :domain {:x [0 3] :y [0 3]} :n 12})]}
                   {:width 450 :height 350})







10.1.12 Hierarchy labels
Group and leaf labels of treemaps, partitions and circle packings: off, on, or a function writing them.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:group-labels
true or false or a function or nil
true
group labels: true - the node's name, false - none, or a function of the node info {:name :value :depth :path :share :parent-share} returning the text


:leaf-labels
true or false or a function or nil
true
leaf labels: as :group-labels, for the leaves






(def budget [{:dept "science" :team "physics" :cost 40} {:dept "science" :team "biology" :cost 25}
             {:dept "arts" :team "music" :cost 15} {:dept "arts" :team "theatre" :cost 10}

                    :charts [(chart/treemap {:group-labels false :leaf-labels #(str (:name %) " " (:value %))})]}
                   {:width 500 :height 300})






10.1.13 3D frame
3D charts (cloud, surface) draw their data in a box seen in perspective.

10.1.13.1 View
The eye sits at an azimuth and elevation, at a perspective distance; the box has proportions and may mirror axes.





Option
Type
Default
Description
Group




:view
map

the eye's position: azimuth, elevation and perspective distance
3D frame


:view :azimuth
a finite number
40.0
rotation around the vertical axis, degrees



:view :elevation
a finite number, >= -90, <= 90
30.0

:view :distance
a non-negative finite number
0.0

:aspect
[a positive number, a positive number, a positive number]
[1 1 1]
box proportions [ax ay az]
3D frame


:reverse
set of one of :x :y :z

axes running the other way (mirrors the scene)
3D frame






(plot/render-image {:data iris
                    :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width :z :petal-length :color :species}
                    :charts [(chart/cloud {:view {:azimuth 60 :elevation 20 :distance 0.3} :aspect [1 1 0.6]})]}
                   {:width 500 :height 400})

The box, the ticks and the axis titles.





Option
Type
Default
Description
Group

true or false or nil
true
draw the box: hidden edges dashed and a floor grid behind the data, visible edges over it
3D frame


:axes
true or false or nil
true
draw ticks, tick labels and axis titles
3D frame


:axis-titles
map
the mapped column names
axis titles (nil - none)
3D frame

any value

any value

y axis title



:axis-titles :z
any value

z axis title







(plot/render-image {:data iris
                    :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width :z :petal-length}
                    :charts [(chart/cloud {:box false :axis-titles {:x "sepal L" :y "sepal W" :z "petal L"}})]}
                   {:width 500 :height 400})






10.1.13.3 Domains
Explicit domains - needed when several 3D charts share a plot.





Option
Type
Default
Description
Group




:domain
map
the data's domains
explicit data domains (needed for each of several 3D charts in one plot)
3D frame


:domain :x
[a finite number, a finite number]

explicit x domain [a b] (a > b reverses the axis)

[a finite number, a finite number]

explicit y domain [a b] (a > b reverses the axis)

[a finite number, a finite number]

explicit z domain [a b] (a > b reverses the axis)







(plot/render-image {:data iris
                    :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width :z :petal-length}

                   {:width 500 :height 400})







10.1.14 3D shading
Shaded 3D faces (surface quads, cloud bars) are lit by Lambert’s law: an ambient share of the colour plus the rest by the face’s angle to the light, whose direction is given in view coordinates (x right, y up, z away from the eye).





Option
Type
Default
Description




:ambient
a number in [0 1]
0.4
share of a shaded face's colour independent of the light (0 - light only, 1 - no shading)


:light
[a finite number, a finite number, a finite number]
[-0.5 0.6 -1.0]
direction toward the light [x y z] in view coordinates (x right, y up, z away from the eye), normalized





The default shading beside a darker ambient share lit from the right.

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:charts [(chart/surface {:f (fn [[x y]] (m/sin (m/* x y)))
                                                            :domain {:x [-2 2] :y [-2 2]} :color [120 160 220]})]
                                   :labels {:title "default shading"}}
                                  {:charts [(chart/surface {:f (fn [[x y]] (m/sin (m/* x y)))
                                                            :domain {:x [-2 2] :y [-2 2]} :color [120 160 220]
                                                            :ambient 0.2 :light [1.0 1.0 -0.5]})]
                                   :labels {:title ":ambient 0.2 :light [1 1 -0.5]"}}]
                                 {:columns 2})
                   {:width 800 :height 400})






10.1.15 Text style
Font, size, colour, padding, alignment and background of the text chart - also the style of every theme text role (Theme chapter).





Option
Type
Default
Description




:font
a bundled, installed or logical font name, or a java.awt.Font

font name (bundled, installed or logical) or a java.awt.Font


:size
a positive number

title: 11  Errors
text:
11.1 Error data
Invalid input fails before anything is computed. plot/build (and render, render-image) validates in two rounds, each throwing one ex-info listing all its errors:
Builders and data functions check their options before reading their data.
ex-data of the error: :key - the first offending key, :in - its path, :value - the value, :errors - every problem as {:in path :value v :message text}; the exception message lists the same problems as text. A misspelled key gets a spelling suggestion.
With the scale fixed the plot keys hold, and the chart’s misspelled option is reported:
Fixed:

title: 11  Errors
text:
(def bad-plot
  {:data [{:x 1 :y 2} {:x 2 :y 3}]
   :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
   :charts [(chart/scatter {:szie 4})]
   :scales {:x {:kind :logarithmic}}})


(try (plot/build bad-plot)
     (catch clojure.lang.ExceptionInfo e {:message (ex-message e) :data (ex-data e)}))


{:message
 "Invalid input: [:scales :x :kind] should be either :bands, :datetime, :interpolated, :linear, :log, :pow, :radial or :symlog, got :logarithmic",
 :data
 {:key :kind,
  :in [:scales :x :kind],
  :value :logarithmic,
  :errors
  [{:in [:scales :x :kind],
    :value :logarithmic,
    :message
    "should be either :bands, :datetime, :interpolated, :linear, :log, :pow, :radial or :symlog"}]}}



(try (plot/build (assoc-in bad-plot [:scales :x :kind] :log))
     (catch clojure.lang.ExceptionInfo e (ex-data e)))


{:key :szie,
 :in [:charts 0 :options :szie],
 :value 4,
 :errors
 [{:in [:charts 0 :options :szie],
   :value 4,
   :message "unknown key, should be spelled :size"}]}



(plot/render-image (-> bad-plot
                       (assoc :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 4})])
                       (assoc-in [:scales :x :kind] :log))
                   {:width 500 :height 300})

title: 11  Errors
text:
11.2 Builders and data functions
Options are checked against the builder’s schema before its data is read:

(try (plot/sankey [{:from "a" :to "b" :value 1}] {:node-widht 10})
     (catch clojure.lang.ExceptionInfo e (ex-data e)))


{:key :node-widht,
 :in [:node-widht],
 :value 10,
 :errors
 [{:in [:node-widht],
   :value 10,
   :message "unknown key, should be spelled :node-width"}]}

Checks of the data itself (missing columns, wrong shapes) throw the same kind of error, keyed by the option or argument at fault.

12.1 Output
What cljplot2 doesn’t do, and the nearest way around it.

title: 12  Limits
text: Static raster images only (BufferedImage, a clojure2d raster canvas) - no interactivity, no SVG or PDF; plot/save writes the formats Java’s ImageIO knows (png, jpg, bmp, gif, tiff …; Render chapter).

title: 12  Limits
text:
12.2 Layout

Legends sit right of the panels; there is no placement option. A legend can go elsewhere as its own plot: :legend-only true in an :arrange cell (and :legend false on the plot beside it).
No subtitle or caption: write them with the text chart in panel units, or as a title of an :arrange.
:margins need a single panel (no facets, :arrange or :custom-grid); :aspect :iso and :flip need the generated grid; free or sliced facet scales don’t combine with explicit domains or :aspect :iso.

12.3 Coordinates

Polar coordinates only with the charts declaring them (Scales, axes and coordinates chapter); no polar :aspect :iso, :margins or :custom-grid.
3D charts (cloud, surface) only with other 3D charts, without :flip, :aspect :iso, :margins, polar coordinates or free facet scales.

12.4 Data

Dates are java.time values; date strings stay levels.

title: 13  Charts: points and paths
text:
13.1 scatter
Marks placed at data positions: points (scatter), lines through them (line), straight pieces between two positions (segment) and filled shapes (polygon). Each chart lists the mapping keys it reads, its own options and the shared option groups it takes (documented once in the Shared options chapter).
Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
Data: Monthly stock prices for five companies, vega-datasets 3.3.1 stocks.csv (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/vega-datasets@3.3.1/data/stocks.csv); licence: none listed - see vega-datasets (cite Vega as the source).
A point per row at its x and y; colour, shape and size may come from the data, and :order sets which points are drawn on top.
Its options: the point style used when nothing is mapped, the draw order of a mapped :order, and jitter - random offsets separating points on a grid of values (seeded here, so the image is the same on every build):
A mapped :order draws points by its values, later ones on top: the most powerful cars over the others (ascending) or under them (descending); :padding is the room around the data, here none on x:
:alpha sets the opacity of every point colour, mapped or not - overlapping bubbles stay visible; the white outline keeps its own colour:
Shared options: Common options (:data :mapping :legend); Named theme styles (:theme-style).

title: 14  Charts: series
text:
14.1 ribbon
Charts of values along x: a band between two bounds (ribbon), a fitted curve with its uncertainty band (smooth) and price candles (candlestick). Each chart lists the mapping keys it reads, its own options and the shared option groups it takes (documented once in the Shared options chapter).
Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
Data: VIX daily open, high, low and close values, vega-datasets 3.3.1 ohlc.json (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/vega-datasets@3.3.1/data/ohlc.json); original: Yahoo Finance VIX Data, CBOE - VIX Historical Data; licence: none listed - see vega-datasets (cite Vega as the source).
A band per group between a lower and an upper bound at each x - an interval, a range of values, an envelope.
Its options: the band’s colour and fill, its edges, and a gradient instead of a flat fill:
A gradient along x instead (over the x scale’s range), and the padding of the data span - none on x, a third of the span on y:
Shared options: Fill patterns (:pattern :pattern-color); Common options (:data :mapping :legend); Named theme styles (:theme-style); Curves (:interpolator :interpolator-params :sample-step).

title: 15  Charts: annotations
text:
15.1 rule
Marks placed by literal positions rather than by data: reference lines (rule), intervals (rect), labels (text), a picture (image) and curves of functions (function). Rule, rect and text also take data and a mapping - one mark per row. Each chart lists the mapping keys it reads, its own options and the shared option groups it takes (documented once in the Shared options chapter).
Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).
Straight lines across the panel: vertical at an x, horizontal at a y, or sloped y = intercept + slope · x - one per row of data, or at literal positions.
Its options: literal positions - one or a vector of them, across x (:x) or along it (:y) - and sloped lines:
Shared options: Line style (:color :line-width :dash); Common options (:data :mapping :legend); Named theme styles (:theme-style); Annotation options (:extent).

Option
Type
Default
Description




:overlapping-labels
one of :keep :drop :repel
:keep
labels overlapping one drawn before them (groups, then rows in data order): :keep (all drawn), :drop (not drawn) or :repel (moved to a free place within :repel-distance, else not drawn)


:repel-distance
a positive finite number or nil
60
with :overlapping-labels :repel: the farthest a label moves from its place, pixels


:label-leader
true or false or nil
false
with :overlapping-labels :repel: draw a line from the point of a label moved more than 6 pixels to its box





:overlapping-labels :drop leaves out each label overlapping one drawn before it - the rows’ order is the priority (here the larger cities first). A mapped :x-span gives each label a room along x in x units (here up to the next city east of it at about its latitude, else the panel’s edge): a longer label shrinks, down to its text role’s :min-size (the :annotation role’s 6 points by default; a role without one doesn’t shrink): on the right the labels with room keep their size, while Vienna (next to Bratislava) and Budapest (near the panel’s edge) are drawn smaller to fit their room. Only labels running along x are fitted - unrotated, in an unflipped cartesian plot. Builders use both for their node labels:

:overlapping-labels :repel moves such a label instead, in the same priority order: to the nearest free place within :repel-distance pixels (default 60) - inside the panel, off the labels placed before it and off the other labels’ points (not other charts’ marks) - and leaves out only a label with no free place there (a label larger than the panel stays where it is). It works in pixels on the drawn boxes, the same in flipped, polar and faceted plots and for rotated labels. :label-leader true joins a label moved more than 6 pixels to its point with a thin line in its colour, ending on the edge of its (turned) box; a place whose leader would cross another label, or whose box would cross another label’s leader, isn’t free - leaders never run through labels. Labels in boxes (:background, :inset) are repelled by their whole box - the text with its inset - and kept inside the panel with it (right). 0.5
with :along-path: where on the path the text sits, a fraction of its length from its first position (:anchor h - the text's start, middle or end there)





:along-path true lays each label text along the polyline of the positions of its group with that text, in data order, glyph by glyph turned to the path, upright: data rows of one group and label (a line’s own rows - left), or literal positions with one text (a fitted trend line - middle; a curve - right). :path-position is where on the path (a fraction of its length; default 0.5), :anchor places the text there (h: start, centre or end) and on a side of the path (v: :bottom - above it, :middle - on it, :top - below it), :offset [dx dy] moves it along and up from the path in pixels. The glyphs follow one another along the path shifted to the text’s baseline, so they keep their spacing through bends; the text reads upright by the whole path’s direction (a vertical path - bottom to top). A :background (inline or the text role’s) fills a band under the glyphs, :inset past them (right). A text longer than its path isn’t drawn.

(let [eruptions (map :eruptions faithful)
      waiting (map :waiting faithful)
      slope (/ (stats/covariance eruptions waiting) (stats/variance eruptions))
      intercept (- (stats/mean waiting) (* slope (stats/mean eruptions)))
      xs [1.5 5.2]
      ys (mapv #(+ intercept (* slope %)) xs)
      wave (m/slice-range 0.0 m/TWO_PI 60)]
  (plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data growth :mapping {:x :t :y :v :color :g}
                                     :charts [(chart/line)
                                              (chart/text {:mapping {:x :t :y :v :color :g :label :g} :along-path true
                                                           :path-position 0.7 :anchor [:center :bottom] :offset [0 2]})]
                                     :labels {:title "data: along each line"}
                                     :theme {:palette {:color :set1}}
                                     :legend false}
                                    {:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting}
                                     :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 4})
                                              (chart/function {:f #(+ intercept (* slope %)) :domain [1.5 5.2]})
                                              (chart/text {:x xs :y ys :text (format "waiting = %.1f + %.1f eruptions" intercept slope)
                                                           :along-path true :path-position 0.6 :anchor [:center :bottom]})]
                                     :labels {:title "literal: along a trend line"}}
                                    {:data (map (fn [x] {:x x :y (m/sin x)}) wave) :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
                                     :charts [(chart/line)
                                              (chart/text {:x (vec wave) :y (mapv m/sin wave) :text "a text along a sine wave"
                                                           :along-path true :path-position 0.0 :anchor [:left :bottom] :offset [0 2]})
                                              (chart/text {:x (vec wave) :y (mapv m/sin wave) :text "below the trough" :along-path true
                                                           :path-position 0.75 :anchor [:center :top]
                                                           :background [255 240 160] :inset 2})]
                                     :labels {:title "[:left :bottom], [:center :top]"}}]
                                   {:columns 3})
                     {:width 1000 :height 330}))




Shared options: Text style (:font :size :font-style :color :inset :background); Common options (:data :mapping :legend); Annotation options (:extent).

title: 15  Charts: annotations
text:
15.4 image
A picture drawn into the panel: a function gets the panel’s scales, domains and pixel size and returns an image; it reads no mapping. Here a radial gradient covering the data range [-1 1] × [-1 1]:

(plot/render-image {:charts [(chart/image {:domain {:x [-1 1] :y [-1 1]}
                                           :f (fn [{[w h] :size}]
                                                (let [w (int w) h (int h)
                                                      img (BufferedImage. w h BufferedImage/TYPE_INT_RGB)]
                                                  (doseq [i (range w) j (range h)
                                                          :let [d (m/hypot (- (/ (* 2.0 i) w) 1) (- (/ (* 2.0 j) h) 1))
                                                                c (int (* 255 (max 0.0 (- 1.0 (* 0.7 d)))))]]
                                                    (.setRGB img i j (+ (* 65536 c) (* 256 (quot c 2)) 80)))
                                                  img))})]}
                   {:width 450 :height 350})




Its options: the function and the data range the image covers - without :domain the image follows the other charts’ domains (here a scatter’s), drawn below them:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:f (required)
a function

callback of {:x-scale :y-scale :x-domain :y-domain :facet :size} returning the panel's image (a BufferedImage, clojure2d canvas or pixels; nil - nothing)


:domain
map
the image follows the other charts' domains
the data range the image covers, added to the extents without padding or nice ends


:domain :x (required)
[a finite number, a finite number]

x range [lo hi] (data units)


:domain :y (required)
[a finite number, a finite number]

y range [lo hi] (data units)






(plot/render-image {:data faithful
                    :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting}
                    :charts [(chart/image {:f (fn [{[w h] :size}]
                                                (let [w (int w) h (int h)
                                                      img (BufferedImage. w h BufferedImage/TYPE_INT_RGB)]
                                                  (doseq [i (range w) j (range h)
                                                          :let [c (int (+ 180 (* 60 (/ (double i) w))))]]
                                                    (.setRGB img i j (+ (* 65536 c) (* 256 c) 235)))
                                                  img))})
                             (chart/scatter)]}
                   {:width 550 :height 340})

title: 15  Charts: annotations
text:
15.5 function
Curves of functions y = f(x), or parametric [x y] = f(t), sampled at drawing; several functions are labelled and may be mapped to colour or dash by the chart’s own mapping.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:color
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

line colour per function label (e.g. :function)


:dash
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

dash style per function label


:group
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

groups without a visual aesthetic, each its own function






(plot/render-image {:charts [(chart/function {:f {"sin" #(m/sin %) "cos" #(m/cos %)}
                                              :domain [0 m/TWO_PI]
                                              :mapping {:color :function :dash :function}})]}
                   {:width 600 :height 320})





15.5.1 Curve
The functions, their domain (or :t range of a parametric curve), the sampling step, the fill and the chart’s own mapping:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:fill
a clojure2d color or :none
:none
fill colour (or :none) of the area to y = 0 (:f) or of the polygon the curve closes (:parametric)


:mapping
a mapping: key -> accessor (a keyword or a function of a row)

the chart's own mapping of the function labels (e.g. {:color :function}); only facet keys come from the plot


:f
a function, a non-empty vector of functions or of [label function] pairs, or a non-empty map label -> function

y = f(x): a function, a vector of functions or of [label function] pairs, or a map label -> function (this or :parametric)


:parametric
a function, a non-empty vector of functions or of [label function] pairs, or a non-empty map label -> function

[x y] = f(t): functions given as for :f (this or :f)


:domain
[lo hi]: finite numbers lo < hi, or two different java.time values
the plot's explicit x domain, else the x scale's domain at drawing
x span [lo hi] the :f functions are sampled over: numbers or java.time values


:t
[lo hi]: finite numbers lo < hi, or two different java.time values

t span [lo hi] of :parametric (required there): numbers or java.time values


:sample-step
a positive number of pixels or {:count n}, n >= 2
1 pixel for :f, {:count 500} for :parametric
distance between samples: pixels along x or {:count n} (:parametric - only {:count n})






(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:charts [(chart/function {:f #(* % % 0.5) :domain [-2 2] :fill [69 117 180 60]})]
                                   :labels {:title ":f, :fill"}}
                                  {:charts [(chart/function {:parametric (fn [t] [(m/sin (* 3 t)) (m/sin (* 4 t))])
                                                             :t [0 m/TWO_PI] :fill [200 80 40 60]})]
                                   :aspect :iso
                                   :labels {:title ":parametric (Lissajous)"}}
                                  {:charts [(chart/function {:f #(m/sin %) :domain [0 10] :sample-step 25})]
                                   :labels {:title ":sample-step 25 px"}}]
                                 {:columns 3})
                   {:width 1000 :height 320})






15.5.2 Gaps
A nil or non-finite result breaks the curve, or a faint segment bridges the gap:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:bridge
map
{:alpha-factor 0.3}
style of the segments bridging gaps with :gaps :bridge: :alpha-factor (a fraction of the line alpha), optional :line-width and :dash


:bridge :alpha-factor (required)
a number in [0 1]
0.3 in the theme's :bridge (a given :bridge replaces it whole)
bridge opacity, a fraction of the line's alpha


:bridge :line-width
a non-negative number
the line's width
bridge line width in pixels


:bridge :dash
:none, a dash style (:dashed :dot-dash :dot-dot-dash :dotted :long-dash :loose-dot :solid :two-dash) or a sequence of positive numbers or nil
the line's dash
dash style of the bridge


:gaps
one of :break :bridge
:break
nil or non-finite results break the curve: :break (empty space) or :bridge (a straight segment in the :bridge style)






(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:charts [(chart/function {:f #(m/sqrt (- 1 (* % %))) :domain [-2 2]})]
                                   :labels {:title ":gaps :break (default)"}}
                                  {:charts [(chart/function {:f #(when-not (< 1 % 2) (m/sin %)) :domain [0 6]
                                                             :gaps :bridge :bridge {:alpha-factor 0.6 :dash :dotted}})]
                                   :labels {:title ":gaps :bridge"}}]
                                 {:columns 2})
                   {:width 800 :height 300})






15.5.3 Extent
Which samples count for the y axis: the 1% - 99% quantiles by default (a pole doesn’t stretch the axis), all of them, or those within :y-limits:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:y-limits
[lo hi], finite numbers, lo < hi

[lo hi] - samples outside don't count for the y extent (the curve is only clipped)


:y-extent
:quantiles, :min-max, :none or {:quantiles [p q]}, 0 <= p < q <= 1
:quantiles
y extent of the samples without :y-limits or an explicit y domain: :quantiles (1% and 99%), {:quantiles [p q]}, :min-max or :none


:padding
map of one of :x :y to [lo hi], non-negative numbers
0.05 on every side
padding of the data span per position axis, {:x [lo hi] :y [lo hi]} fractions of the span






(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:charts [(chart/function {:f #(m/tan %) :domain [0 3]})]
                                   :labels {:title ":y-extent :quantiles (default)"}}
                                  {:charts [(chart/function {:f #(m/tan %) :domain [0 3] :y-extent :min-max})]
                                   :labels {:title ":y-extent :min-max"}}
                                  {:charts [(chart/function {:f #(m/tan %) :domain [0 3] :y-limits [-5 5]})]
                                   :labels {:title ":y-limits [-5 5]"}}]
                                 {:columns 3})
                   {:width 1000 :height 300})




The padding of the sampled span: none on x (the curve meets the panel’s sides), a quarter of the span on y:

(plot/render-image {:charts [(chart/function {:f #(m/sin %) :domain [0 6.3] :padding {:x [0 0] :y [0.25 0.25]}})]
                    :labels {:title ":padding {:x [0 0] :y [0.25 0.25]}"}}
                   {:width 500 :height 280})




Shared options: Line style (:color :line-width :dash); Named theme styles (:theme-style); Common options (:legend).

title: 16  Charts: bars and ranges
text:
16.1 bar
Strip charts drawing one item per level of a categorical axis: a bar of a summary (bar), an interval with its centre (extent) and a bullet - a measure over qualitative ranges with markers (bullet). Each chart lists the mapping keys it reads, its own options and the shared option groups it takes.
Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
A bar per level (and group) whose length summarises the item’s rows - their sum by default, or a count of them; vertical bars take the levels on x, horizontal ones on y.

title: 16  Charts: bars and ranges
text:
Option
Type
Default
Description




:x
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

x position: the levels (categorical) of vertical bars or the values of horizontal ones


:y
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

y position: the values of vertical bars or the levels (categorical) of horizontal ones


:color
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

fill colour: categorical values group the bars (legend keys), numeric ones colour each bar by its value (a colour bar)


:pattern
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

fill pattern per group (gives legend keys)


:group
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

groups without a visual aesthetic (dodged, stacked or mirrored as other groups)






(plot/render-image {:data sales
                    :mapping {:x :quarter :y :amount :color :product}
                    :charts [(chart/bar)]
                    :labels {:y "amount"}}

[69 117 180]
bar fill colour (a mapped :color wins)

                                   :labels {:title ":overlay, :alpha 0.35"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data pyramid
                                   :mapping {:x :people :y :age :color :sex}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:mirror :color :zero-line-color :red :zero-line-width 3})]
                                   :scales {:y {:reverse true}}
                                   :labels {:title "mirrored, red 0 line"}}]
                                 {:columns 3 :widths [1 1 1.3]})
                   {:width 1000 :height 320})






16.1.2 Bars
What a bar’s length is (:stat), how the groups of one level share its band, widths by the item’s size, the order of negative stacked parts, and the padding:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:stat
one of :count :mean :median :percent :pmf :sum or a function
:sum
bar length from the item's rows: :sum, :mean, :median or a function of the values, or a count measure :count, :percent, :pmf (no values needed)


:color-stat
one of :mean :median :sum or a function or nil
the :stat of value stats, :mean for count stats
a bar's colour value from its rows' values of a linear or binned :color: :sum, :mean, :median or a function of the values


:position
one of :dodge :normalize :overlay :stack
:dodge when a level holds two or more groups, else :overlay
how groups of one level share its band: :dodge (side by side), :overlay (on top of each other), :stack or :normalize (stacked, each level summing to 1)


:zero-line
true or false or nil
true
draw the 0 line on top of mirrored bars (with :mirror only)


:varwidth
true or false or a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil
false
bar widths relative to the widest: true - by the square root of the count, a keyword or function of a row - by the item's sum of it


:negative-order
one of :forward :reverse
:forward
order of the groups below 0 with :stack: :forward (group order) or :reverse (the last group nearest 0)


:padding
map of one of :x :y to [lo hi], non-negative numbers
values 0.05, 0 at the baseline side the bars grow from, 0 for :normalize
padding of the data span per position axis, {:x [lo hi] :y [lo hi]} fractions of the span (strip frame: :x the values)






(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :species :y :sepal-length}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:stat :mean})]
                                   :labels {:title ":stat :mean"}}
                                  {:data sales
                                   :mapping {:x :quarter :y :amount :color :product}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack})]
                                   :labels {:title ":position :stack"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data sales
                                   :mapping {:x :quarter :y :amount}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:varwidth :amount})]
                                   :labels {:title ":varwidth :amount"}}]
                                 {:columns 3})
                   {:width 1000 :height 320})




Every :stat: summaries of the mapped values (:sum - the default, :mean, :median) and counts of the rows, needing no values (:count, :percent of the panel’s rows, :pmf - shares summing to 1):

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :species :y :sepal-length}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar)]
                                   :labels {:title ":sum (default)"}}
                                  {:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :species :y :sepal-length}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:stat :median})]
                                   :labels {:title ":stat :median"}}
                                  {:data mtcars-cyl
                                   :mapping {:x (levels/categorical :cyl)}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:stat :count})]
                                   :labels {:title ":stat :count"}}
                                  {:data mtcars-cyl
                                   :mapping {:x (levels/categorical :cyl)}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:stat :percent})]
                                   :labels {:title ":stat :percent"}}
                                  {:data mtcars-cyl
                                   :mapping {:x (levels/categorical :cyl)}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:stat :pmf})]
                                   :labels {:title ":stat :pmf"}}]
                                 {:columns 5})
                   {:width 1000 :height 280})




Groups side by side (:dodge, the default for several groups of a level) or stacked; with negative values a stack grows both ways from 0 - :negative-order :reverse puts the last group nearest 0 below it. Mirrored bars drop their 0 line with :zero-line false, and :padding widens the value axis (here 30% past the longest bar):

(def balance [{:month "Jan" :item "sales" :eur 40} {:month "Jan" :item "costs" :eur -25} {:month "Jan" :item "tax" :eur -8}
              {:month "Feb" :item "sales" :eur 55} {:month "Feb" :item "costs" :eur -30} {:month "Feb" :item "tax" :eur -12}
              {:month "Mar" :item "sales" :eur 35} {:month "Mar" :item "costs" :eur -20} {:month "Mar" :item "tax" :eur -6}])

                                   :mapping {:x :month :y :eur :color :item}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:position :dodge})]
                                   :labels {:title ":position :dodge"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data balance
                                   :mapping {:x :month :y :eur :color :item}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack :negative-order :forward})]
                                   :labels {:title ":stack, :negative-order :forward"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data balance
                                   :mapping {:x :month :y :eur :color :item}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack :negative-order :reverse})]
                                   :labels {:title ":negative-order :reverse"}}]
                                 {:columns 3 :widths [1 1 1.3]})
                   {:width 1000 :height 320})





(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data pyramid
                                   :mapping {:x :people :y :age :color :sex}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:mirror :color :zero-line false})]
                                   :scales {:y {:reverse true}}
                                   :labels {:title ":zero-line false"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data sales
                                   :mapping {:x :quarter :y :amount}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:padding {:y [0 0.3]}})]
                                   :labels {:title ":padding {:y [0 0.3]}"}}]
                                 {:columns 2})
                   {:width 900 :height 300})




A numeric :color doesn’t group the bars: each bar is filled by its own colour value - :color-stat over its rows’ colour values (default the bar’s :stat, :mean for counts) - with a colour bar. Mapped to the values with :sum it colours each bar by its length; stacked segments (groups from :group or a categorical aesthetic) take their own colours; a count can be coloured by a summary of another column:

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data sales
                                   :mapping {:x :quarter :y :amount :color :amount}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:color-stat :sum})]
                                   :labels {:title ":color-stat :sum"}}
                                  {:data sales
                                   :mapping {:x :quarter :y :amount :group :product :color :amount}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack :color-stat :mean})]
                                   :labels {:title "stacked, :mean"}}
                                  {:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :species :color :petal-length}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:stat :count :color-stat :median})]
                                   :labels {:title ":count, :median"}}]
                                 {:columns 3})
                   {:width 1000 :height 320})




An explicit colour :domain never drops rows: every bar keeps its length, and a bar whose colour value lies outside the domain is drawn in the NA colour (Q4’s mean, 45.7, is above 40). A :value-label function reads the bar’s colour value as :color-value:

(plot/render-image {:data sales
                    :mapping {:x :quarter :y :amount :color :amount}
                    :charts [(chart/bar {:color-stat :mean :value-label #(format "mean %.1f" (:color-value %))})]
                    :scales {:color {:domain [15 40]}}
                    :labels {:title "colour :domain [15 40]"}}
                   {:width 500 :height 320})






16.1.3 Labels
Each bar’s length written past its end or in its middle, formatted or as the text a function returns:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:label-stack
one of :horizontal :vertical
along the bars: :horizontal for horizontal bars, :vertical for vertical ones
how the value and n texts of one label are joined: :horizontal (side by side) or :vertical (one above the other)


:value-label
true or false or a function or nil
false
write each bar's length (true) or the text a function of {:value :n :share :level :group} returns


:label-position
one of :end :center :base :outer
:center for :stack / :normalize, else :end
where labels sit: :end (past the bar's end), :center (in the bar), :base (in the bar at its base) or :outer (polar only: past the outer radius)


:label-leader
true or false or nil
false
draw a line from the bar's outer edge to its :outer label


:value-format
a number format string or a function
whole numbers as integers, else the fewest digits telling the labels apart
text of the value labels: a format string or a function of the number






(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data sales
                                   :mapping {:x :quarter :y :amount :color :product}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:value-label true})]
                                   :labels {:title ":value-label true"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data sales
                                   :mapping {:x :quarter :y :amount :color :product}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:position :normalize :value-label #(format "%.0f%%" (* 100 (:share %)))})]
                                   :labels {:title ":normalize, shares in %"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :species :y :petal-length}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:stat :mean :value-label true :value-format "%.2f cm"})]
                                   :labels {:title ":value-format"}}]
                                 {:columns 3})
                   {:width 1000 :height 320})




Where labels sit: past the bar’s end (:end, the default unstacked) or inside it (:center, the default stacked; :base - at its base, shown further down); with the value and the row count (:n-label) the two texts join side by side or one above the other (:label-stack):

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :species :y :sepal-length}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:stat :mean :value-label true :label-position :end})]
                                   :labels {:title ":label-position :end"}}
                                  {:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :species :y :sepal-length}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:stat :mean :value-label true :label-position :center})]
                                   :labels {:title ":label-position :center"}}
                                  {:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :species :y :sepal-length}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:stat :mean :value-label true :n-label true
                                                        :label-stack :horizontal})]
                                   :labels {:title ":label-stack :horizontal"}}
                                  {:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :species :y :sepal-length}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:stat :mean :value-label true :n-label true
                                                        :label-stack :vertical})]
                                   :labels {:title ":label-stack :vertical"}}]
                                 {:columns 2})
                   {:width 900 :height 560})




:base writes the label inside the bar at its base (the end nearer 0), reading from the axis - each segment’s own base when stacked. With 0 outside the value domain (e.g. :scales {:x {:domain [4 nil]}}) the label sits at the visible end nearest 0; in a polar plot with the values on the radius the bases meet at the centre, where labels rarely fit their wedge and are skipped:

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:stat :mean :value-label true :label-position :base})]
                                   :labels {:title ":label-position :base"}}
                                  {:data sales
                                   :mapping {:x :quarter :y :amount :color :product}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack :value-label true :label-position :base})]
                                   :labels {:title ":stack, :label-position :base"}}]
                                 {:columns 2 :widths [1 1.3]})
                   {:width 900 :height 320})




In a polar plot :outer puts the labels past the outer radius, with a leader line from each bar (:label-leader):

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data sales
                                   :mapping {:x :quarter :y :amount}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:value-label true :label-position :outer})]
                                   :coord {:kind :polar}
                                   :labels {:title ":label-position :outer"}}
                                  {:data sales
                                   :mapping {:x :quarter :y :amount}
                                   :charts [(chart/bar {:value-label true :label-position :outer :label-leader true})]
                                   :coord {:kind :polar}
                                   :labels {:title ":label-leader true"}}]
                                 {:columns 2})
                   {:width 800 :height 400})

title: 17  Charts: strip distributions
text:
17.1 box
Strip charts showing the distribution of each level’s values: summaries (box, violin) and the values themselves (stripplot, beeswarm, dotplot, rug). Placement, width and grouping across the strip are the Strip options group every one of them takes. Each chart lists the mapping keys it reads, its own options and the shared option groups it takes.
Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
A box per level (and group): the quartiles, the median, whiskers to the most extreme values within 1.5 IQR of the box and the outliers past them - computed from the values …
… or read from rows of precomputed statistics, one row per level and group, with :stat :identity:
Its options: the box and outlier style, the statistics, outliers on or off, the mean marker, widths by count and the Tufte variant (whisker lines and a median point) - here on rear axle ratios, with outliers in the 4- and 8-cylinder groups:
:padding - space past the values along the value axis, fractions of their span (default 5% each side):
Shared options: Fill patterns (:pattern :pattern-color); Common options (:data :mapping :legend); Named theme styles (:theme-style); Strip options (:place :width :thickness :position :dodge-gap :bottom-share :n-label :n-format :level-axis).

title: 18  Charts: distribution statistics
text:
18.1 histogram
Charts computing a statistic of the values on one axis: binned counts (histogram), kernel density curves (density), the empirical distribution function (ecdf) and the comparison of two distributions by quantiles (qq) or probabilities (pp).
Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
Random log-normal values (seeded) - skewed in data units, even on a log axis:
Two species only - for the charts drawing two groups against each other:
Bars counting the values falling into each bin; groups overlay, dodge, stack or mirror, and a categorical :y gives one histogram per level (ridgelines).

title: 18  Charts: distribution statistics
text:
Option
Type
Default
Description




:x (required)
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one

values to bin (data units)


:y
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

ridgeline levels: categorical or on a :bands scale, one histogram per level (a numeric :y otherwise is ignored)


:color
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

groups, each with its own bar fill colour


:pattern
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

groups, each with its own fill pattern


:group
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

groups without a visual aesthetic






(plot/render-image {:data iris
                    :mapping {:x :petal-length :color :species}
                    :charts [(chart/histogram)]
                    :labels {:x "petal length [cm]"}}
                   {:width 600 :height 350})





18.1.1 Bins
The bins (a method, a count or breaks), what a bar’s height measures and the space the bins are made in:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:bins
keyword or vector of a finite number (at least 2) or quantile bins {:quantiles q :estimation e}: q a positive count or a vector of increasing probabilities strictly between 0 and 1, e one of [:legacy :r1 :r2 :r3 :r4 :r5 :r6 :r7 :r8 :r9] or a positive integer
:sturges
bins (per panel under free or sliced facet x scales): an estimation method (:sturges :sqrt :rice :doane :scott :freedman-diaconis), a bin count or increasing breaks (shared, values outside dropped)


:y
one of :cumulative :percent :count :pmf :density
:percent
bar height: :percent (of the panel's or group's total), :count, :pmf (shares summing to 1), :density (area 1) or :cumulative (count of the bin and every bin before it)


:stat-space
one of :data :scale or nil
:data
space the bins are made in: :data (data units) or :scale (the x scale's coordinates - equal-width log10 bins on a :log axis, values it can't place dropped; :density per transformed unit)






(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data faithful
                                   :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                                   :charts [(chart/histogram {:bins 30 :y :count :stroke-color :none})]
                                   :labels {:title ":bins 30 :y :count"}}
                                  {:data faithful
                                   :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                                   :charts [(chart/histogram {:bins [1.5 2 2.5 3 3.5 4 4.5 5 5.5] :y :density
                                                              :color [120 160 90] :stroke-color :white})]
                                   :labels {:title "breaks, :y :density"}}
                                  {:data two-species
                                   :mapping {:x :sepal-length :color :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/histogram {:position :mirror :bins 12 :zero-line-color :red
                                                              :zero-line-width 2})]
                                   :labels {:title ":position :mirror"}
                                   :legend false}]
                                 {:columns 3})
                   {:width 1000 :height 320})




What a bar’s height measures - the same bins as shares summing to 1 (:pmf, the default :percent scaled to 100), and the running count (:cumulative):

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data faithful
                                   :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                                   :charts [(chart/histogram {:bins 20 :y :pmf})]
                                   :labels {:title ":y :pmf"}}
                                  {:data faithful
                                   :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                                   :charts [(chart/histogram {:bins 20 :y :cumulative})]
                                   :labels {:title ":y :cumulative"}}]
                                 {:columns 2})
                   {:width 900 :height 300})




On a log axis bins of equal width in data units crowd into the last decades; :stat-space :scale makes them in the axis’s log10 coordinates - equal-width on screen, :density per log10 unit (values a log axis can’t place, 0 and negatives, are dropped and counted). In either space the values are numbers: histogram and density take no dates.

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data skewed
                                   :mapping {:x :value}
                                   :scales {:x {:kind :log}}
                                   :charts [(chart/histogram {:bins 20 :y :count :stat-space :data})]
                                   :labels {:title ":stat-space :data"}}
                                  {:data skewed
                                   :mapping {:x :value}
                                   :scales {:x {:kind :log}}
                                   :charts [(chart/histogram {:bins 20 :y :count :stat-space :scale})]
                                   :labels {:title ":stat-space :scale"}}]
                                 {:columns 2})
                   {:width 900 :height 300})




Bins are shared by every facet panel, so panels compare bar by bar. Under a free (or sliced) facet x scale each panel gets bins over its own range instead - a count of bins (here 8) or a method applies per panel, so the bars fill each panel’s own axis; explicit breaks stay shared. Margin histograms follow their panel’s scale the same way.

(plot/render-image {:data iris
                    :mapping {:x :petal-length :facet :species}
                    :facets {:scales {:x :free}}
                    :charts [(chart/histogram {:bins 8 :y :count})]
                    :labels {:x "petal length [cm]"}}
                   {:width 900 :height 300})






18.1.2 Invalid values
Rows whose x is missing, NaN or not a number (or a value the stat space can’t place) are dropped and counted; :invalid :show draws their count as a bar in a band beside the x axis’s start, outside the axis line, on the same y scale, in the chart’s own fill (or the mapped one), labelled by :invalid-label (which needs :invalid :show). Shares (:percent, :pmf) are then of all rows, the invalid ones included; groups stack or dodge in the band as in the bins, every facet panel has its own band and a flipped plot puts it under the panel. Only the main charts of a generated grid draw a band: :invalid :show in a margin chart or a :custom-grid plot is an error.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:invalid
one of :drop :show or nil
:drop
rows with a missing, NaN, non-numeric or unplaceable x: :drop (counted in :dropped) or :show (a bar of their count in a band beside the x axis's start)


:invalid-label
string or nil

18.1.3 Position
How groups combine and the zero line and y range of mirrored groups:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:position
one of :dodge :mirror :normalize :overlay :stack
:overlay
grouped bars: :overlay (translucent), :dodge, :stack, :normalize (stacked to 1) or :mirror (two groups, the second downward); ridgelines: :overlay or :mirror


:symmetric
true or false or nil
false
with :position :mirror, tie both halves to one y range [-M M], M the tallest bar over all panels


:zero-line
true or false or nil
true
with :position :mirror, draw the y = 0 line over the bars


:padding
map of one of :x :y to [lo hi], non-negative numbers
{:x [0.05 0.05] :y [0 0.05]} (bars stand on the panel's bottom edge); y [0.05 0.05] with :position :mirror
padding of the data span per position axis, {:x [lo hi] :y [lo hi]} fractions of the span





How groups share the bins: translucent over each other (:alpha of :overlay), side by side, stacked, or stacked to 1 - the share of each species in every bin:

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :petal-length :color :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/histogram {:position :overlay :alpha 0.4 :bins 20})]
                                   :labels {:title ":position :overlay :alpha 0.4"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :petal-length :color :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/histogram {:position :dodge :bins 12})]
                                   :labels {:title ":position :dodge"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :petal-length :color :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/histogram {:position :stack :bins 20})]
                                   :labels {:title ":position :stack"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :petal-length :color :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/histogram {:position :normalize :bins 20})]
                                   :labels {:title ":position :normalize"}
                                   :legend false}]
                                 {:columns 2})
                   {:width 900 :height 560})




Mirrored groups: halves tied to one y range [-M M] (:symmetric) or each fitted to its own tallest bar, the zero line off; thick outlines and no padding above the bars:

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data two-species
                                   :mapping {:x :sepal-length :color :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/histogram {:position :mirror :bins 12 :symmetric true})]
                                   :labels {:title ":symmetric true"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data two-species
                                   :mapping {:x :sepal-length :color :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/histogram {:position :mirror :bins 12 :symmetric false :zero-line false})]
                                   :labels {:title ":symmetric false :zero-line false"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data faithful
                                   :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                                   :charts [(chart/histogram {:bins 15 :stroke-color :black :stroke-width 2
                                                              :padding {:y [0 0]}})]
                                   :labels {:title ":stroke-width 2 :padding {:y [0 0]}"}}]
                                 {:columns 3})
                   {:width 1000 :height 320})

Option
Type
Default
Description




:color
a clojure2d color
[69 117 180]

:stroke-color
:darker or a clojure2d color or :none
:darker
outline colour: a colour, :none or :darker (the darkened fill)


:stroke-width
a non-negative number
1
outline width in pixels


:alpha
a number in [0 1]
0.6
fill opacity of grouped bars with :position :overlay (other bars are opaque)


:zero-line-color
a clojure2d color or :none
:black
colour of the y = 0 line drawn with :position :mirror


:zero-line-width
a non-negative number
1
width in pixels of the y = 0 line drawn with :position :mirror






(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data faithful
                                   :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                                   :charts [(chart/histogram {:bins 20 :color [200 120 60] :stroke-color :none})]
                                   :labels {:title ":color, :stroke-color :none"}}

                                   :mapping {:x :sepal-length :color :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/histogram {:bins 12 :alpha 0.3 :stroke-color :darker :stroke-width 1.5})]
                                   :labels {:title ":alpha 0.3 :stroke-width 1.5"}
                                   :legend false}]
