title: 18  Charts: distribution statistics
text:
18.2 density
A kernel density estimate per group drawn as a curve, optionally filled; groups overlay, stack or mirror, and a categorical :y gives ridgelines.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:x (required)
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one

values whose density is estimated (data units)


:y
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

ridgeline levels: categorical or on a :bands scale, one curve per level (a numeric :y otherwise is ignored)


:color
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

groups, each a curve in its own colour


:dash
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

groups, each a curve with its own dash style


:pattern
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

groups, each area with its own fill pattern


:group
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

groups without a visual aesthetic, each its own curve






(plot/render-image {:data iris
                    :mapping {:x :petal-length :color :species}
                    :charts [(chart/density)]
                    :labels {:x "petal length [cm]"}}
                   {:width 600 :height 350})





18.2.1 Style
The area under a curve, its opacity, a gradient fill of ridgelines and the zero line of mirrored curves:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:fill
:color or a clojure2d color or :none
:none
area under the curve: a colour, :color (the curve's colour, its own alpha times :alpha) or :none; stacked positions and ridgelines fill with the curve's colour unless set


:alpha
a number in [0 1]
0.6
factor of the curve colour's alpha filling areas in the curve's colour


:zero-line-color
a clojure2d color or :none
:black
colour of the y = 0 line drawn with :position :mirror


:zero-line-width
a non-negative number
1
width in pixels of the y = 0 line drawn with :position :mirror


:fill-gradient
a clojure2d gradient: a preset keyword, a colour list or a function

ridgelines only: fill colour along :fill-gradient-axis, a clojure2d gradient (preset keyword, colour list or function of t in [0 1]) (wins over :fill)


:fill-gradient-axis
one of :x :y
:x; only with ridgelines and :fill-gradient
axis of the :fill-gradient: :x (over the x scale's domain) or :y (from each ridge's baseline to the top of the tallest curve)






(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :petal-length :color :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/density {:fill :color :alpha 0.3})]
                                   :labels {:title ":fill :color :alpha 0.3"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/density {:fill-gradient :mpl/viridis})]
                                   :scales {:y {:reverse true}}
                                   :labels {:title "ridgelines, :fill-gradient"}}
                                  {:data two-species
                                   :mapping {:x :sepal-length :color :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/density {:position :mirror :fill :color
                                                            :zero-line-color :red :zero-line-width 2})]
                                   :labels {:title ":zero-line-color :red"}
                                   :legend false}]
                                 {:columns 3})
                   {:width 1000 :height 320})




The ridgelines’ gradient along x (over the x domain) or along y (from each ridge’s baseline up):

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/density {:fill-gradient :mpl/plasma :fill-gradient-axis :x})]
                                   :scales {:y {:reverse true}}
                                   :labels {:title ":fill-gradient-axis :x"}}
                                  {:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/density {:fill-gradient :mpl/plasma :fill-gradient-axis :y})]
                                   :scales {:y {:reverse true}}
                                   :labels {:title ":fill-gradient-axis :y"}}]
                                 {:columns 2})
                   {:width 900 :height 320})






18.2.2 Estimate
The kernel, its bandwidth (in data units or a selector), the number of evaluation points and how far a curve reaches past the data:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:kernel
keyword
:gaussian
fastmath KDE kernel


:bandwidth
a positive number or keyword
:nrd0
kernel bandwidth in data units, or a fastmath bandwidth selector


:n
integer, >= 2 or nil
512
number of evaluation points of each curve


:cut
a non-negative number or nil
3
how many bandwidths the curve extends past the extreme values on each side


:stat-space
one of :data :scale or nil
:data
space the density is estimated in: :data (data units) or :scale (the x scale's coordinates - log10 on a :log axis, values it can't place dropped; a numeric :bandwidth in those units)






(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data faithful
                                   :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                                   :charts [(chart/density)]
                                   :labels {:title "default (:gaussian, :nrd0)"}}
                                  {:data faithful
                                   :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                                   :charts [(chart/density {:bandwidth 0.1})]
                                   :labels {:title ":bandwidth 0.1"}}
                                  {:data faithful
                                   :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                                   :charts [(chart/density {:kernel :uniform :cut 0})]
                                   :labels {:title ":kernel :uniform :cut 0"}}]
                                 {:columns 3})
                   {:width 1000 :height 300})




A bandwidth selector instead of a number, few evaluation points (the curve drawn through 8 points), and a curve reaching 1 bandwidth past the data (3 by default):

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data faithful
                                   :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                                   :charts [(chart/density {:bandwidth :sj})]
                                   :labels {:title ":bandwidth :sj"}}
                                  {:data faithful
                                   :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                                   :charts [(chart/density {:n 8})]
                                   :labels {:title ":n 8"}}
                                  {:data faithful
                                   :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                                   :charts [(chart/density {:cut 1})]
                                   :labels {:title ":cut 1"}}]
                                 {:columns 3})
                   {:width 1000 :height 300})




Skewed values: estimated in data units (the default) the curve is lopsided and its tail passes 0 - a log axis can’t show it; :stat-space :scale estimates the density of the log10 values on a log axis (per log10 unit, a numeric :bandwidth in log10 units) and draws it back on the axis:

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data skewed
                                   :mapping {:x :value}
                                   :charts [(chart/density {:stat-space :data :fill :color})]
                                   :labels {:title ":stat-space :data"}}
                                  {:data skewed
                                   :mapping {:x :value}
                                   :scales {:x {:kind :log}}
                                   :charts [(chart/density {:stat-space :scale :fill :color})]
                                   :labels {:title ":stat-space :scale, a log x axis"}}]
                                 {:columns 2})
                   {:width 900 :height 300})






18.2.3 Position
How groups combine (the Layering and position chapter shows the streamgraphs), a common y range of the mirrored halves and the padding:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:position
one of :mirror :normalize :overlay :silhouette :stack :wiggle
:overlay
grouped curves: :overlay, :stack, :normalize (stacked, summing to 1), streamgraphs :silhouette and :wiggle, or :mirror (two groups, the second drawn downward); ridgelines take :overlay or :mirror


:symmetric
true or false or nil
false
with :position :mirror, tie both halves to one y range [-M M], M the tallest curve over all panels


:zero-line
true or false or nil
true
with :position :mirror, draw the y = 0 line over the curves


:padding
map of one of :x :y to [lo hi], non-negative numbers
{:x [0.05 0.05] :y [0 0.05]} (curves stand on the panel's bottom edge); y [0.05 0.05] with :mirror, :silhouette and :wiggle
padding of the data span per position axis, {:x [lo hi] :y [lo hi]} fractions of the span






(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :petal-length :color :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/density {:position :stack})]
                                   :labels {:title ":position :stack"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data two-species
                                   :mapping {:x :petal-length :color :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/density {:position :mirror :fill :color})]
                                   :labels {:title ":position :mirror"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data two-species
                                   :mapping {:x :petal-length :color :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/density {:position :mirror :fill :color :symmetric true})]
                                   :labels {:title ":symmetric true"}}]
                                 {:columns 3 :widths [1 1 1.4]})
                   {:width 1000 :height 320})




Stacked to 1 (each species’ share of the density at every x), the streamgraphs, and a mirrored pair without the zero line and with no padding:

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :petal-length :color :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/density {:position :normalize})]
                                   :labels {:title ":position :normalize"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :petal-length :color :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/density {:position :silhouette})]
                                   :labels {:title ":position :silhouette"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data iris
                                   :mapping {:x :petal-length :color :species}

                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data two-species
                                   :mapping {:x :petal-length :color :species}

                                                            :padding {:x [0 0] :y [0 0]}})]

                   {:width 900 :height 560})

title: 18  Charts: distribution statistics

A step line per group: the share of values at or below each x.





Option
Type
Default
Description

title: 19  Charts: grids and fields
text:
19.1 tile
Charts colouring a plane: a cell per row (tile), a 2D histogram (bin2d), a scalar field drawn as a raster (field) or as level lines (contour), the correlation of two variables as one glyph (correlation), and any other statistic of two variables as one cell (pairwise).
Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
Data: Maunga Whau volcano topography, R datasets package volcano (Ross Ihaka); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
A cell per row at its x and y, filled by a mapped colour: numeric (a gradient) or categorical (a palette).
Its own option writes the value in each cell (black or white by the fill, the :tile-value text role); the cell shape and outline are the Cell style group:
A mapped :size shrinks each cell by its value; with the colour mapped to another variable the size legend’s keys have no colour of their own - their fill is a theme key of [:chart :tile], not an option:
Shared options: Cell style (:cell :cell-scale :stroke-color :stroke-width :alpha-factor); Common options (:data :mapping :legend); Named theme styles (:theme-style).

title: 19  Charts: grids and fields
text:
19.2 bin2d
A 2D histogram: points counted in rectangular cells, the count (or another measure) as the cell colour.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:x (required)
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one

point x positions (numbers)


:y (required)
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one

point y positions (numbers)


:color
nil

must be nil (the cell colour is the measure): set it so in the chart's mapping when the plot maps :color






(plot/render-image {:data faithful
                    :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting}
                    :charts [(chart/bin2d)]
                    :labels {:x "eruption [min]" :y "waiting [min]"}}
                   {:width 600 :height 400})




Its options: the number of cells (or a fastmath estimate), a cell width in data units, the cells’ height / width ratio and what the colour measures:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:bins
one of :scott-correlated :scott :freedman-diaconis :cross-validation :shimazaki-shinomoto or a positive integer
:scott-correlated
cells across the x range (a positive integer), or a fastmath estimate-grid-size method giving a cell area (:binwidth wins)


:binwidth
a positive finite number

cell size in x data units (log10 units on a :log axis); wins over :bins


:aspect
a positive finite number
the panel's height / width (y span / x span with :aspect :iso), estimated from the plot size and facet layout
height / width ratio of the normalized binning space (cells are regular in pixels when it matches the panel)


:measure
one of :count :percent :pmf :density
:count
the cell colour: :count, :percent (of the panel's points), :pmf (share of the panel's points) or :density (count / (n * cell area in data units))






(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data faithful
                                   :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting}
                                   :charts [(chart/bin2d {:bins 10})]
                                   :labels {:title ":bins 10"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data faithful
                                   :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting}
                                   :charts [(chart/bin2d {:binwidth 0.25 :aspect 0.5})]
                                   :labels {:title ":binwidth 0.25 :aspect 0.5"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data faithful
                                   :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting}
                                   :charts [(chart/bin2d {:measure :percent})]
                                   :labels {:title ":measure :percent"}}]
                                 {:columns 3 :widths [1 1 1.3]})
                   {:width 1000 :height 320})




The fastmath estimates of the grid (the default :scott-correlated above) - each picks its own cell count:

                                   :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting}
                                   :charts [(chart/bin2d {:bins :scott})]
                                   :labels {:title ":bins :scott"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data faithful
                                   :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting}
                                   :charts [(chart/bin2d {:bins :freedman-diaconis})]
                                   :labels {:title ":bins :freedman-diaconis"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data faithful
                                   :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting}
                                   :charts [(chart/bin2d {:bins :cross-validation})]
                                   :labels {:title ":bins :cross-validation"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data faithful
                                   :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting}
                                   :charts [(chart/bin2d {:bins :shimazaki-shinomoto})]
                                   :labels {:title ":bins :shimazaki-shinomoto"}
                                   :legend false}]
                                 {:columns 2})

                                   :labels {:title ":measure :pmf"}}
                                  {:data faithful
                                   :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting}

Option
Type
Default
Description

1.0

a function

                   {:width 900 :height 380})

Option
Type
Default
Description




:color
a clojure2d color or :none
[69 117 180]; the theme's, for grouped lines without a mapped colour; ungrouped lines are coloured by level, lines grouped by :color take their group's colour
one colour for every line instead of colouring by level (contour's own :color, not the line style's)


:alpha-factor
a number in [0 1]
1.0; the theme's; grouped filled contours take half of it
factor multiplying the colours' alpha


:levels
integer (1..1000) or vector of a finite number (at least 1)
10
contour levels: a count evenly spread over the range of every sampled value (the ends left out), or a vector of level values


:filled
true or false
false
fill the region at or above each level, each band coloured by its middle value, instead of drawing lines


:labels
true or false or a function or nil
false
line contours only: label each line with its level - true (the number) or a function of {:level v} returning the text (nil - no label)






(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data volcano
                                   :mapping {:x :column :y :row :value :height}
                                   :charts [(chart/contour {:levels [100 120 140 160 180] :labels true
                                                            :color [40 40 40]})]
                                   :labels {:title ":levels vector, :labels true"}}
                                  {:data volcano
                                   :mapping {:x :column :y :row :value :height}
                                   :charts [(chart/contour {:filled true :levels 8 :alpha-factor 0.8})]
                                   :labels {:title ":filled true :levels 8"}}]
                                 {:columns 2 :widths [1 1.25]})
                   {:width 1000 :height 380})





19.4.1 Contour sources
The same sources as field: a function over a domain (lines on a coarse grid are angular), interpolated gridded values and a density with its own bandwidth:

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:charts [(chart/contour {:f (fn [[x y]] (+ (* x x) (* 2 y y) (* x y)))
                                                            :domain {:x [-2 2] :y [-2 2]} :labels true})]
                                   :labels {:title ":f over :domain"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:charts [(chart/contour {:f (fn [[x y]] (+ (* x x) (* 2 y y) (* x y)))
                                                            :domain {:x [-2 2] :y [-2 2]} :n 6})]
                                   :labels {:title ":n 6"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data lattice
                                   :mapping {:x :x :y :y :value :z}
                                   :charts [(chart/contour {:interpolation :bicubic :levels 8})]
                                   :labels {:title "5 x 5 lattice, :bicubic"}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data faithful
                                   :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting}
                                   :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 3 :color [0 0 0 80]})
                                            (chart/contour {:bandwidth [0.15 3] :cut 1})]
                                   :labels {:title ":bandwidth [0.15 3] :cut 1"}}]
                                 {:columns 2 :widths [1 1.25]})
                   {:width 900 :height 640})




Shared options: Line style (:line-width :dash); Fields (:f :domain :kernel :bandwidth :binned :cut :interpolation :n); Common options (:data :mapping :legend); Named theme styles (:theme-style).

title: 19  Charts: grids and fields
text:
19.5 correlation
The correlation coefficient r of two variables drawn as one glyph filling the panel - a cell of a correlogram (plot/pairs). Alone it writes r, one line per group.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:x (required)
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one

first variable (numbers)


:y (required)
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one

second variable (numbers)


:color
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

categorical groups, each a line of the :number glyph in its colour


:group
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

groups without a visual aesthetic, each a line of the :number glyph






(plot/render-image {:data iris
                    :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :petal-length :color :species}
                    :charts [(chart/correlation)]}
                   {:width 450 :height 300})




Its options: the coefficient, the glyph and its colours (by default r on a diverging scale):





Option
Type
Default
Description




:color
a clojure2d color or :none
[69 117 180]; grouped shape glyphs: the theme's; ungrouped: r on a diverging scale; :number: the :correlation text role's colour, group lines mapped or black
one fixed glyph colour, the :number text's too


:stroke-color
:darker or a clojure2d color or :none
:darker
outline colour: a colour, :none or :darker (the darkened fill)


:stroke-width
a non-negative number
1
outline width in pixels


:method
one of :pearson :spearman :kendall
:pearson
correlation coefficient: :pearson, :spearman or :kendall


:glyph
one of :number :shade :square :circle :ellipse :pie
:number
how r is drawn: :number (text, a line per group), :shade (the panel in r's colour), :square / :circle (area ~ |r|), :ellipse (normal contour) or :pie (a disk filled |r|)


:glyph-size
a number in [0 1]
0.9
glyph side (:square, :circle, :ellipse, :pie) as a fraction of the panel's shorter side





Every glyph, for one pair of variables (r about 0.82):

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :petal-width}
                                   :charts [(chart/correlation {:glyph :number})] :labels {:title ":glyph :number"}}
                                  {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :petal-width}
                                   :charts [(chart/correlation {:glyph :shade})] :labels {:title ":glyph :shade"}}
                                  {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :petal-width}
                                   :charts [(chart/correlation {:glyph :square})] :labels {:title ":glyph :square"}}
                                  {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :petal-width}
                                   :charts [(chart/correlation {:glyph :circle})] :labels {:title ":glyph :circle"}}
                                  {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :petal-width}
                                   :charts [(chart/correlation {:glyph :ellipse})] :labels {:title ":glyph :ellipse"}}
                                  {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :petal-width}
                                   :charts [(chart/correlation {:glyph :pie})] :labels {:title ":glyph :pie"}}]
                                 {:columns 3})
                   {:width 900 :height 560})




The three coefficients of the same pair (Kendall’s tau, counting concordant pairs, is the lowest), and a smaller glyph in one fixed colour with a thick outline:

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :petal-width}
                                   :charts [(chart/correlation {:method :pearson})] :labels {:title ":method :pearson"}}
                                  {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :petal-width}
                                   :charts [(chart/correlation {:method :spearman})] :labels {:title ":method :spearman"}}
                                  {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :petal-width}
                                   :charts [(chart/correlation {:method :kendall})] :labels {:title ":method :kendall"}}
                                  {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :petal-width}
                                   :charts [(chart/correlation {:glyph :circle :glyph-size 0.6 :color [120 160 90]
                                                                :stroke-color :black :stroke-width 3})]
                                   :labels {:title ":glyph-size 0.6"}}]
                                 {:columns 4})
                   {:width 1000 :height 280})




In a correlogram - a plot/pairs matrix with correlation glyphs below (:lower) and above (:upper) the diagonal, and the variables’ names on it (:diagonal :names):

(plot/render-image (plot/pairs iris {:variables [:sepal-length :sepal-width :petal-length :petal-width]
                                     :lower (chart/correlation {:glyph :ellipse :stroke-color :none})
                                     :upper (chart/correlation {:glyph :square :method :spearman})
                                     :diagonal :names
                                     :title "ellipses (Pearson) below, squares (Spearman) above"})
                   {:width 700 :height 620})




Shared options: Common options (:data :mapping :legend); Named theme styles (:theme-style).

title: 19  Charts: grids and fields
text:
19.6 pairwise
Any statistic of two variables drawn as one cell filling the panel: an error, an association, an effect size, a distance (the keys of cljplot2.data.pairwise/statistics, listed with pairwise/matrix-rows in the Data functions part) or a function of the two samples - always of the x sample against the y sample. Unlike r the values have no fixed range. Alone it writes the value, one line per group.





Option
Type
Default
Description




:x (required)
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one

first sample, the statistic's xs (numbers)


:y (required)
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one

second sample, the statistic's ys (numbers)


:color
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

categorical groups, each a line of the :number glyph in its colour


:group
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

groups without a visual aesthetic, each a line of the :number glyph






(plot/render-image {:data iris
                    :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :petal-length :color :species}
                    :charts [(chart/pairwise {:method :cohens-d})]}
                   {:width 450 :height 300})




Its options: the statistic and its label, the glyph (by default :number - the text alone; a shade colours the value on the colour scale over the panels’ range, symmetric around 0 on a diverging palette for a signed statistic), and the number format:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:color
a clojure2d color or :none
[69 117 180]; ungrouped shades: the value on the colour scale; grouped shades: the theme's; :number: the :pairwise text role's colour, group lines mapped
one fixed colour: the shade's (text over it by contrast), the :number text's


:method
one of :ameasure :canberra :chebyshev :cliffs-delta :cohens-d :cosine :covariance :euclidean :glass-delta :hedges-g :kendall :mae :manhattan :mape :me :means-ratio :mse :pearson :r2 :rmse :spearman or a function
:pearson
the statistic: a key of pairwise/statistics or a function of two samples (f xs ys)


:label
string or nil
the statistic's label, value for a function
the statistic's label (text, colour bar title)


:glyph
one of :number :shade :shade-number
:number
how the value is drawn: :number (text, a line per group), :shade (the panel in the value's colour) or :shade-number (both)


:value-format
a number format string or a function or nil
at most 2 decimals, whole numbers without them
the text of a value: a format string or a function of the number (a throw or nil - NA)





The glyphs for one pair (sepal against petal length): the mean absolute error as text, shaded and both, the signed mean error shaded on the diverging palette, a user function with its label and format, and one fixed colour (the text over a shade is black or white by the fill):

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :petal-length}
                                   :charts [(chart/pairwise {:method :mae :glyph :number})] :labels {:title ":number"}}
                                  {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :petal-length}
                                   :charts [(chart/pairwise {:method :mae :glyph :shade})] :labels {:title ":shade"}}
                                  {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :petal-length}
                                   :charts [(chart/pairwise {:method :mae :glyph :shade-number})] :labels {:title ":shade-number"}}
                                  {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :petal-length}
                                   :charts [(chart/pairwise {:method :me :glyph :shade-number})] :labels {:title "signed :me"}}
                                  {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :petal-length}
                                   :charts [(chart/pairwise {:method (fn [xs ys] (- (apply max xs) (apply max ys)))
                                                             :label "max diff" :value-format #(format "%+.1f cm" %)})]
                                   :labels {:title "function, :value-format"}}
                                  {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :petal-length}
                                   :charts [(chart/pairwise {:method :rmse :glyph :shade-number :color [120 160 90]})]
                                   :labels {:title ":color"}}]
                                 {:columns 3})
                   {:width 1000 :height 520})




In a plot/pairs matrix every cell shows the statistic of its column variable against its row variable, so the mirrored cells of the asymmetric mean error have opposite signs - shaded below, as text above, the names on the diagonal (:diagonal :names). The statistic is computed once for the matrix: every shaded cell is coloured on its range (symmetric around 0 for the signed mean error) and the one colour bar agrees; the cells share one text size:

(plot/render-image (plot/pairs iris {:variables [:sepal-length :sepal-width :petal-length :petal-width]
                                     :lower (chart/pairwise {:method :me :glyph :shade-number})
                                     :upper (chart/pairwise {:method :me})
                                     :diagonal :names
                                     :title "mean error: shaded below, text above"})
                   {:width 700 :height 620})




Shared options: Common options (:data :mapping :legend); Named theme styles (:theme-style).

title: 20  Charts: part of a whole
text:
20.1 treemap
Shares of a total as areas: nested rectangles (treemap), adjacent bands or rings (partition), nested circles (pack), a grid of cells (waffle) and overlapping sets (venn). Each chart lists the mapping keys it reads, its own options and the shared option groups it takes (documented once in the Shared options chapter).
Each leaf a rectangle of area proportional to its value, nested inside the rectangle of its group; the levels come from :hierarchy, outer level first.
Its options: the gap inside a group, the cell borders and the layout - near-square cells or slices turning direction at each depth:
:order sets the siblings’ order, as in the partition: by descending value (the default of :squarify) or in data order (the default of :slice-dice) - slices ordered by size make a mosaic read largest first:
Shared options: Fill patterns (:pattern :pattern-color); Common options (:data :mapping :legend); Named theme styles (:theme-style); Hierarchy labels (:group-labels :leaf-labels).

text:
20.2 partition
The hierarchy as adjacent bands, one per level, each node as wide as its value - an icicle plot; in polar coordinates the bands become rings (a sunburst).





Option
Type
Default
Description




:value (required)
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one

node size: a positive finite number per row (other rows are dropped)


:hierarchy (required)
vector of a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one (at least 1)

the levels of the tree, outer level first (a row's path ends at its first nil or "")


:color
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

leaf colour (rows with the same path but different colours stay separate leaves)






(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data budget
                                   :mapping {:hierarchy [:dept :team] :value :cost}
                                   :charts [(chart/partition)]
                                   :labels {:title "cartesian: icicle"}}
                                  {:data budget
                                   :mapping {:hierarchy [:dept :team] :value :cost}
                                   :charts [(chart/partition)]
                                   :coord {:kind :polar}
                                   :labels {:title "polar: sunburst"}}]
                                 {:columns 2})
                   {:width 1000 :height 420})




Its options: borders, the order of siblings, how nodes are coloured (by their top-level node, lighter by depth, or each by its name) and whether the root is drawn. :order :data keeps the rows’ order - here the budget reversed, so sport comes first and the teams go from the cheapest up (by value, the default above, science leads):





Option
Type
Default
Description




:stroke-color
a clojure2d color or :none
:white
cell outline colour


:stroke-width
a non-negative number
1
cell outline width in pixels


:order
one of :value :data
:value
order of siblings: :value (descending) or :data (first appearance)


:color-by
one of :top :name
:top
node colours: :top - each top-level node's palette colour, lighter by depth; :name - every node by its name through the color scale


:root
true or false or nil
false
draw the root too, every level one up






(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data (reverse budget)
                                   :mapping {:hierarchy [:dept :team] :value :cost}
                                   :charts [(chart/partition {:order :data :root true})]
                                   :coord {:kind :polar}
                                   :labels {:title ":order :data, :root true"}}
                                  {:data budget
                                   :mapping {:hierarchy [:dept :team] :value :cost}
                                   :charts [(chart/partition {:color-by :name :stroke-width 2})]
                                   :coord {:kind :polar}
                                   :labels {:title ":color-by :name"}
                                   :legend false}]
                                 {:columns 2})
                   {:width 1000 :height 460})

                    :mapping {:hierarchy [:dept :team] :value :cost}

title: 21  Charts: multivariate and 3D
text:
21.1 parallel
Many variables at once: a line per row across one axis per variable (parallel, a radar in polar coordinates), points in a 3D box (cloud), surfaces over a grid (surface), and a matrix of plots of every pair of variables (scatter-plot matrix, at the end). Each chart lists the mapping keys it reads, its own options and the shared option groups it takes (documented once in the Shared options chapter).
Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
Data: Earthquakes off Fiji since 1964, R datasets package quakes (Harvard PRIM-H project); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
A line per row across one vertical axis per variable, each axis scaled on its own; the variables come from the :variables option, the mapping only groups the rows.

title: 21  Charts: multivariate and 3D
text:
Option
Type
Default
Description




:color
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

line colour, grouping the rows


:dash
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

line dash style, grouping the rows


:pattern
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

radar fill pattern, grouping the rows


:group
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one or nil

groups without a visual aesthetic






(plot/render-image {:data iris
                    :mapping {:color :species}
                    :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables [:sepal-length :sepal-width :petal-length :petal-width]})]
                    :labels {:x nil :y nil}}
                   {:width 700 :height 400})





21.1.1 Axes
Which variables and in what order (a [label accessor] pair renames one), how each is scaled - every axis to 0..1 (:uniminmax), to standard scores, robustly, centred, or all on one common range - explicit limits, the axes themselves and what a missing value does:





Option
Type
Default
Description




:variables (required)
vector of a keyword or a [label accessor] pair (a string and a keyword or function)

the variables in axis order: keywords or [label accessor] pairs (2 or more)


:scaling
one of :center :globalminmax :robust :std :uniminmax
:uniminmax
per variable scaling: :uniminmax (0..1), :std, :robust, :center or :globalminmax


:limits
map of any value to [lo hi], finite numbers, lo < hi
each variable's finite data range
explicit variable domains {key [lo hi]}, key - the keyword or the pair's label


:axes
true or false or nil
true
draw each variable's axis with ticks and labels


:missing
one of :break :drop
:break
a missing value: :break (the line breaks there) or :drop (the row is dropped)


:robust-center
one of :median :mean
:median (only with :scaling :robust)
centre of :scaling :robust: :median or :mean


:robust-spread
one of [:biweight :gini :iqr :mad :meanad :qn :sn :stddev :tukey] or a quantile p, 0 < p < 0.5
:mad (only with :scaling :robust)
spread of :scaling :robust: a fastmath.stats/robust-stddev estimator (:mad, :iqr, :sn, :qn, ...) or a quantile p in (0 0.5)


:padding
map

padding of the scaled values' span, {:y [lo hi]} fractions of the span


:padding :y
[lo hi], non-negative numbers
[0.05 0.05]
padding of the value axis [lo hi], fractions of the span






(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data iris
                                   :mapping {:color :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables [["petal L" :petal-length] ["petal W" :petal-width]
                                                                         ["sepal L" :sepal-length]]
                                                             :scaling :std})]
                                   :labels {:title ":scaling :std, labelled variables" :x nil :y nil}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data iris
                                   :mapping {:color :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables [:petal-length :petal-width :sepal-length]
                                                             :scaling :globalminmax :limits {:petal-width [0 8]}})]
                                   :labels {:title ":globalminmax, :limits {:petal-width [0 8]}" :x nil :y nil}}]
                                 {:columns 2 :widths [1 1.25]})
                   {:width 1000 :height 380})




The scalings side by side: centred values (:center, original units less each variable’s mean) and the robust scaling - values less a centre over a spread, the median over the median absolute deviation by default, here also the mean over a quantile spread (:robust-spread 0.25 - the interquartile half-range). Every variable name is drawn, also when the names collide; long names in narrow plots turn with the theme’s [:axis :x :label-rotation]:

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange [{:data iris
                                   :mapping {:color :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables [:sepal-length :sepal-width :petal-length :petal-width]
                                                             :scaling :center})]
                                   :labels {:title ":scaling :center" :x nil :y nil}
                                   :theme {:axis {:x {:label-rotation -30}}}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data iris
                                   :mapping {:color :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables [:sepal-length :sepal-width :petal-length :petal-width]
                                                             :scaling :robust :robust-center :median :robust-spread :mad})]
                                   :labels {:title ":robust, :median / :mad" :x nil :y nil}
                                   :theme {:axis {:x {:label-rotation -30}}}
                                   :legend false}
                                  {:data iris
                                   :mapping {:color :species}
                                   :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables [:sepal-length :sepal-width :petal-length :petal-width]
                                                             :scaling :robust :robust-center :mean :robust-spread 0.25})]
                                   :labels {:title ":robust, :mean / 0.25" :x nil :y nil}
                                   :theme {:axis {:x {:label-rotation -30}}}}]
                                 {:columns 3 :widths [1 1 1.3]})

title: 21  Charts: multivariate and 3D
text:
21.4 Scatter-plot matrix
Not a chart but a matrix of plots of the charts above and on the other pages: plot/pairs gives every pair of :variables a cell. By default a scatter plot below the diagonal (:lower), the correlation as text above it (:upper) and a density on it (:diagonal):

(plot/render-image (plot/pairs iris {:variables [:sepal-length :sepal-width :petal-length :petal-width]
                                     :mapping {:color :species}})
                   {:width 700 :height 620})




A slot takes one chart, a vector of charts (layered in each cell) or :none (empty cells; nil - the default); :diagonal :names writes the variable’s name in the diagonal cell instead:

(plot/render-image (plot/pairs iris {:variables [:sepal-length :sepal-width :petal-length]
                                     :lower [(chart/scatter {:size 4}) (chart/smooth {:method :lm})]
                                     :upper :none
                                     :diagonal :names
                                     :title "scatter and a linear fit below, empty above"})
                   {:width 600 :height 560})

title: 22  Builders: graphs
text:
22.1 network
Builders turn edge rows (or wide rows) into an ordinary plot map: they lay the graph out with the data functions of the Graphs and trees chapter and add the charts. Each builder lists its own options; the options it forwards to the layout functions and the builder options (title, scales, theme) are shared groups.
Data: Migration flows between world regions, data-to-viz example dataset 13_AdjacencyDirectedWeighted (long form; Yan Holtz, after Abel & Sander 2014); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).
Data: UK energy flows in 2050 (a DECC scenario), networkD3 JSONdata/energy.json (the d3 sankey example; UK Department of Energy & Climate Change 2050 Calculator); licence: networkD3 is GPL-3; the data’s licence isn’t stated.
Data: Titanic passengers and crew by class, sex, age and survival, R datasets package Titanic (Dawson 1995); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
A node-link diagram of edge rows (:from, :to, optional :value): nodes placed by a force-directed, circle or random layout (seeded here), edges as segments - with arrows for a directed graph.
Node aesthetics from the node rows or the computed degree (whole numbers: :integer-ticks through the builder’s :scales), labels beside the nodes (a label overlapping that of a larger node is left out):
The node and edge style merged over the defaults, a directed graph’s arrows in :edge-style (left); edge widths from the weights and labels from a node column (:labels :age, right) - an aesthetic maps either nodes or edges, not both:
The theme styles a network draws with - the nodes in [:chart :network-node] (a scatter style over [:chart :scatter]), the edges in [:chart :network-edge] (a segment style), the labels in the text role :network-label (see the Theme chapter); :node-style / :edge-style win over them per call:
A theme restyles every network of a plot - here square, dark nodes:
Dashed blue edges and larger labels through the theme:
Shared options: Graph (:from :to :value :nodes :id :directed); Graph layout (:layout :iterations :gravity :rng); Builder options (:title :scales :theme).

title: 23  Builders: trees
text:
23.1 dendrogram
Builders drawing a tree or using one: a dendrogram of a clustering or a hierarchy, a node-link tree, a heatmap ordered by clustering, edges bundled along a tree, and sequences as rings (a flow sunburst). Each takes its data and an options map and returns an ordinary plot map; the tree functions it forwards to are shared groups (Shared options), the trees themselves come from the tree data functions.
Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
The cars’ variables as z-scores, a row vector per car, clustered with complete linkage (fastmath hclust):
A small hierarchy as rows of levels:
A dendrogram of a clustering (an hclust result, its observations named by :leaf-names) or of a tree (levels or parents) - branches at their merge heights, leaves along one axis.
Horizontal, with thicker red branches (:line-style, merged over the default), and without leaf names (left); a hierarchy with its group names at their nodes (right):
The branches draw in the theme style [:chart :dendrogram-branch] (a line style - its colour, width and dash shown; the clustered heatmap’s trees too), the group names in the text role :dendrogram-group-label:
Thin blue branches through the theme:
Shared options: Dendrogram layout (:k :circular :span); Builder options (:title :scales :theme).

title: 23  Builders: trees
text:
23.3 clustered-heatmap
Tiles of a value per row and column, rows and columns ordered by hierarchical clustering, their dendrograms beside the tiles; the data are long rows (:row, :col, :value accessors).





Option
Type
Default
Description




:row (required)
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one

accessor of a row's tile row


:col (required)
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one

accessor of a row's tile column


:value (required)
a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one

accessor of a row's tile value, a finite number


:method
one of :single :complete :average :weighted :centroid :median :ward :ward-d :diana
:complete
fastmath hclust linkage of the rows and columns


:distance
one of :euclidean :chebyshev :manhattan :canberra :earth-movers or a function
:euclidean
fastmath hclust distance: a keyword or a function of two double arrays


:row-tree
true or false
true
the rows' dendrogram right of the tiles (false - order only)


:col-tree
true or false
true
the columns' dendrogram above the tiles (false - order only)


:tree-size
[a number in (0 1), a number in (0 1)]
[0.2 0.2]
[w h] - the dendrograms' share of the width (rows) and the height (columns), fractions in (0, 1)


:row-annotations
sequential of [a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one, an aesthetic scale spec or nil] or nil
no strips
[[accessor colour-scale-spec] ...]: in order, a strip per accessor between the tiles and the rows' tree, coloured by its values (categorical or continuous), with a legend


:col-annotations
sequential of [a keyword, a function or a categorical marker of one, an aesthetic scale spec or nil] or nil
no strips
[[accessor colour-scale-spec] ...]: in order, a strip per accessor between the columns' tree and the tiles, coloured by its values (categorical or continuous), with a legend


:annotation-size
a positive number or nil
16
thickness of an annotation strip in pixels (not a fraction, as :tree-size)


:legend-span
one of :row :matrix or nil
:matrix with annotations, else :row
height of the legend column: :row - beside the tiles' row; :matrix - one cell beside every row (the trees' and the strips' too), stacking the value legend over the annotations' legends

title: 23  Builders: trees
text:
23.4 bundle
Hierarchical edge bundling: edges between the leaves of a tree, each bent along the tree path between its ends, leaves around a circle. title: 24  Builders: series
text:
24.1 acf
Builders of time series plots: the autocorrelation correlogram of a series of values, and horizon charts of one or more series. Each takes its data and an options map and returns an ordinary plot map; the series functions it forwards to are shared groups (Shared options).
An autoregressive series AR(1) with coefficient 0.7, 200 values - fastmath r/ar over seeded white noise:
The autocorrelation (ACF) and partial autocorrelation (PACF) of a series of numbers by lag: a stem per lag, a significance band around zero, the lags outside it marked (lag 0, always 1, is not marked).
One correlogram - the ACF (:acf) or the PACF (:pacf) - and the band as a block per lag (:stepped); the default :both draws ACF above PACF, the band :smooth:
The colours of the stems, the band and the significant lags:
The lag points draw in the theme style [:chart :acf-point] (a scatter style over [:chart :scatter]; their colours are the :colors option):
Larger triangle points through the theme:
Shared options: Autocorrelation rows (:lags :level); Builder options (:title :scales :theme).

title: 25  Data functions: levels
text:
25.1 levels/bin
Functions turning values into levels before plotting: numbers binned into intervals, numbers or dates read as levels, levels ordered by a statistic, rows ranked within each x, and overlapping intervals (shingles) for conditioning. Each returns rows, a vector of levels (order-levels) or a mapping marker (categorical) for an ordinary plot; options are checked against the table shown.
Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
Adds the bin of a numeric value to every row - an interval [lo, hi) (the last one closed), printed like R’s cut; a missing or non-numeric value gets no bin.
The bins of the cars’ horsepower - five equal-width bins, bounds printed with 2 significant digits - as a new column:
Bins are levels: counted by a bar chart (:stat :count), in interval order. Explicit breaks (left), quantile bins of equal counts (middle), and the series name printed in every bin (right):

26.1 graph/graph
Functions turning edges, adjacency matrices, parent links, level columns or clusterings into graphs and trees, and laying them out as rows - node positions, edge paths, ring sectors, bands - that ordinary charts draw (the graph and tree builders are made of them). Flights between airports (counts), the airports as node rows, and the same flows as a matrix:
The graph of edge rows: nodes (the given node rows first, then ids seen only in edges) with their degrees, and edges with numeric weights. Undirected by default; directed graphs split degrees into in and out.
The flights as a directed graph with the airports as nodes - Krakow has no flights (degree 0):
The edges of the flights as an undirected graph, the weights from :n as numbers (:value):
Without a :value accessor every edge weighs 1:

27.1 sets/upset-rows
Functions turning set memberships and time series into rows for ordinary plots: the bars and dot matrix of an UpSet plot, lag pairs, autocorrelation rows, the folded bands of a horizon chart and the matrix of a pairwise statistic. The builders plot/acf and plot/horizon (Builders: series) draw autocorrelations and horizons directly, chart/pairwise one statistic per panel.
Set memberships: one row per item and set it belongs to (an item may be in several).
An autoregressive series (fastmath r/ar, coefficient 0.6) over a weekly sine plus seeded white noise:
The bars of an UpSet plot: every combination of sets that holds items exclusively - its sets, size and degree - by size descending. The mapping names the set and item keys; a third argument chooses (and orders) the sets.

title: 29  Specific cases
text:
29.1 cljplot2.data.probability
The functions behind some charts are ordinary public functions in internal namespaces: probability plot pairs, kernel density curves, smoothing fits, dot plot bins, circle packing, treemap rectangles and Venn circles. They are not part of the documented API - no option tables, no validation, and they may change - but they return plain data, so a computation a chart doesn’t offer can start from them and draw with ordinary charts. Each section shows the data and a chart drawn from it; then the lists of fastmath distributions and kernels the charts accept, a few recipes and links to the use cases and galleries.
Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).
Q-Q and P-P statistics (the qq and pp charts). The plotting positions (i - 0.5) / n of a data side:
The Q-Q pairs of a normal distribution (x side) and the sample (y side) - the normal quantiles at the sample’s plotting positions against its sorted values - and the quartile line through the first and third quartile pairs, [slope intercept]:
The pairs drawn by hand - points and the quartile line (a rule by :slope and :intercept) - match the qq chart; the skewed sample bends away from the line at both ends:

29.8 Recipes
Short compositions of the pieces documented in this part.
A reference curve over a histogram: the histogram on the density scale (:y :density) and the normal density with the data’s mean and standard deviation as a function chart:

(plot/render-image (let [xs (map :waiting faithful)
                         normal (r/distribution :normal {:mu (stats/mean xs) :sd (stats/stddev xs)})]
                     {:data faithful
                      :mapping {:x :waiting}
                      :charts [(chart/histogram {:y :density :bins 25})
                               (chart/function {:f #(r/pdf normal %) :domain [40 100] :color [200 50 50] :line-width 2})]
                      :labels {:x "waiting [min]" :title "a normal curve fails a bimodal sample"}})
                   {:width 600 :height 320})




A highlighted interval with an explanation: a band (rect over an x interval), a threshold (rule) and a note (text) layered over a scatter with a loess smooth:

(plot/render-image {:data faithful
                    :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting}
                    :charts [(chart/rect {:x [2.5 3.5] :fill [255 200 0 60]})
                             (chart/scatter {:size 4})
                             (chart/smooth {:method :loess})
                             (chart/rule {:y 68 :dash :dashed})
                             (chart/text {:x 3.0 :y 95 :text "few eruptions of 2.5-3.5 min"})]
                    :labels {:x "eruptions [min]" :y "waiting [min]"}}
                   {:width 600 :height 320})




Small multiples built in a loop - one plot per group with a shared domain, arranged in a row:

(plot/render-image (plot/arrange (for [[label pred] [["short" #(< (:eruptions %) 3)] ["long" #(>= (:eruptions %) 3)]]]
                                   {:data (filter pred faithful)
                                    :mapping {:x :waiting}
                                    :charts [(chart/density {:fill :color})]
                                    :scales {:x {:domain [40 100]}}
                                    :labels {:title (str label " eruptions")}})
                                 {:columns 2})
                   {:width 800 :height 260})




Rendering to a file - plot/save at the end of a render-image pipeline - is shown in Render - Saving.

title: 29  Specific cases
text:
29.9 Links
The use cases show the charts at work, one family per chapter: distribution, correlation, ranking, part of a whole, evolution, flow and colours. The galleries reproduce other libraries’ examples: cljplot extras, lattice and Vega-Lite.

source: notebooks/reference/specific_cases.clj

title: 30  Distribution
text:
30.1 Violin
Charts of how the values of one numeric variable spread: violins, densities, histograms, boxplots and ridgelines (the R Graph Gallery distribution family), then beeswarms, strip plots, rugs and ECDFs.
Distribution charts put the values on :x and the groups (if any) on :y, so they are horizontal by default. :flip true draws the same plot vertically.
A violin is a kernel density estimate mirrored around the centre line of its group, here with a small box inside (the default :inner).

title: 30  Distribution
text:
30.1.1 Basic violin
Source: R Graph Gallery - Violin plot. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data iris
  :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :species}
  :charts [(chart/violin)]
  :labels {:title "Sepal length by species" :x "sepal length [cm]" :y nil}}
 {:width 800 :height 450})






30.1.2 Ordered violins
levels/order-levels orders the levels by any statistic of a value; the result is the scale’s :domain, its first level at the bottom (y grows upward) - ascending medians put the largest on top (setosa, first in the data and at the bottom by default).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Violin plot (reorder). Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data iris
  :mapping {:x :sepal-width :y :species}
  :scales {:y {:domain (levels/order-levels iris :species :sepal-width stats/median)}}
  :charts [(chart/violin {:inner :quartiles})]
  :labels {:title "Sepal width, species by median (largest on top)" :x "sepal width [cm]" :y nil}}
 {:width 800 :height 450})






30.1.3 Horizontal and vertical
The R Graph Gallery draws violins and boxplots vertically; here that is :flip true on the same plot - values stay on :x, which is now drawn vertically.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Horizontal violin plot. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [p {:data iris
         :mapping {:x :sepal-width :y :species}
         :charts [(chart/violin)]
         :labels {:x "sepal width [cm]" :y nil}}]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(assoc-in p [:labels :title] "horizontal (default)")
                  (-> p (assoc :flip true) (assoc-in [:labels :title] ":flip true"))]
                 {:columns 2})
   {:width 900 :height 450}))






30.1.4 Violin with a box and sample sizes
Two strip charts share the bands: a violin without inner marks and a narrow box. :n-label writes each group’s count past its largest value.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Violin with boxplot and sample size. Data: Barley yields, Minnesota 1931-1932, R lattice package barley (Immer et al. 1934; Fisher 1971; Cleveland 1993); licence: GPL (>= 2) (lattice).

(plot/render-image
 {:data barley
  :mapping {:x :yield :y :site}
  :charts [(chart/violin {:inner :none :color [200 200 220]})
           (chart/box {:width 0.12 :outliers false :n-label true})]
  :labels {:title "Barley yield by site" :x "yield [bushels/acre]" :y nil}}
 {:width 800 :height 500})






30.1.5 Grouped violins
A second grouping (here the year, coloured) dodges the violins inside each band, in legend order; with exactly two groups :position :mirror draws split violins, one half per group. The year is a number, so :scales {:color {:type :categorical}} declares it categorical: one colour per year instead of a gradient.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Grouped violin plot. Data: Barley yields, Minnesota 1931-1932, R lattice package barley (Immer et al. 1934; Fisher 1971; Cleveland 1993); licence: GPL (>= 2) (lattice).

(let [p {:data barley
         :mapping {:x :yield :y :site :color :year}
         :scales {:color {:type :categorical}}
         :labels {:x "yield [bushels/acre]" :y nil}}]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(assoc p :charts [(chart/violin {:inner :none})] :labels {:title "dodged" :x "yield" :y nil})
                  (assoc p :charts [(chart/violin {:position :mirror :inner :quartiles})]
                         :labels {:title "split (:position :mirror)" :x "yield" :y nil})]
                 {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 550}))






30.1.6 Inner marks
:inner chooses what a violin shows inside: a box (default), quartile lines, a rug or the points. The data is a fixed 5% sample of chem97 (31022 rows), so the rug and the points stay readable.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Violin plot; seaborn violinplot (1, 2). Data: A-level chemistry scores, England 1997, R mlmRev package Chem97 (Yang et al. 2002); licence: GPL (>= 2) (mlmRev).

(def chem97-sample
  "A fixed 5% sample of chem97 (the full data has 31022 rows)."
  (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 3)] (filterv (fn [_] (< (r/drandom rng) 0.05)) chem97)))
