title: 30  Distribution
text:
30.2 Density
A kernel density estimate (fastmath) of the values, per panel and group.

30.2.1 Basic density
:bandwidth is a number or a fastmath rule (:nrd0 by default, as R); :kernel any fastmath kernel.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Density plot. Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange (for [[title opts] [["default (:nrd0)" {}]
                                   [":bandwidth 0.1" {:bandwidth 0.1}]
                                   [":bandwidth 0.6" {:bandwidth 0.6}]
                                   [":kernel :epanechnikov" {:kernel :epanechnikov}]]]
                 {:data faithful
                  :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                  :charts [(chart/density (assoc opts :fill [69 117 180 60]))]
                  :labels {:title title :x "eruption time [min]"}})
               {:columns 2})
 {:width 900 :height 600})






30.2.2 Mirror density
Two groups, the second drawn downward, with the y = 0 line (:zero-line, on by default). :symmetric puts both halves on one range so they compare by height.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Mirror density chart. Data: A-level chemistry scores, England 1997, R mlmRev package Chem97 (Yang et al. 2002); licence: GPL (>= 2) (mlmRev).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange [{:data chem97
                 :mapping {:x :gcsescore :color :gender}
                 :charts [(chart/density {:position :mirror :fill :color})]
                 :labels {:title "GCSE score: F up, M down" :x "GCSE score"}}
                {:data chem97
                 :mapping {:x :age :color :gender}
                 :charts [(chart/density {:position :mirror :symmetric true})]
                 :labels {:title "age, :symmetric" :x "age [months, centred]"}}]
               {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 450})






30.2.3 Several groups
Groups from a colour mapping, overlaid. The line takes the group colour; :fill :color fills each area with its group colour at opacity :alpha, a fixed :fill colour fills every area alike.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Density with multiple groups. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange [{:data iris
                 :mapping {:x :sepal-length :color :species}
                 :charts [(chart/density {:line-width 2})]
                 :labels {:title "lines" :x "sepal length [cm]"}}
                {:data iris
                 :mapping {:x :sepal-length :color :species}
                 :charts [(chart/density {:fill :color :alpha 0.4})]
                 :labels {:title ":fill :color, :alpha 0.4" :x "sepal length [cm]"}}
                {:data iris
                 :mapping {:x :petal-length :color :species}
                 :charts [(chart/density {:fill [0 0 0 30]})]
                 :labels {:title ":fill [0 0 0 30]" :x "petal length [cm]"}}]
               {:columns 3})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})






30.2.4 Annotated density
Annotation charts take literal positions: a rule at the mean, a text label and a band (chart/rect) over the central 50% of the values.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Density chart with annotation. Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [xs (map :eruptions faithful)
      mean (stats/mean xs)
      [q1 q3] (stats/quantiles xs [0.25 0.75])]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data faithful
    :mapping {:x :eruptions}
    :charts [(chart/rect {:x [q1 q3] :fill [69 117 180 40]})
             (chart/density)
             (chart/rule {:x mean :dash [5.0 3.0] :color :red})
             (chart/text {:x mean :y [:panel 0.95] :text (format "mean %.2f" mean) :anchor [:left :top]
                          :offset [4 0] :color :red})
             (chart/text {:x (* 0.5 (+ q1 q3)) :y [:panel 0.05] :text "IQR" :anchor [:center :bottom]})]
    :labels {:title "Old Faithful eruption times" :x "eruption time [min]"}}
   {:width 800 :height 450}))






30.2.5 Small multiples
A facet mapping gives one panel per level; the colour still groups inside each panel.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Density small multiples. Data: A-level chemistry scores, England 1997, R mlmRev package Chem97 (Yang et al. 2002); licence: GPL (>= 2) (mlmRev).

(plot/render-image
 {:data chem97
  :mapping {:x :gcsescore :facet :score :color :gender}
  :charts [(chart/density)]
  :labels {:title "GCSE score by A-level score and gender" :x "GCSE score"}}
 {:width 900 :height 600})






30.2.6 Stacked density
:position :stack piles the group densities on one common grid; :normalize shows each group’s share.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Stacked density chart. Data: Prices and attributes of round cut diamonds, R ggplot2 package diamonds (Wickham et al.); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(let [p {:data diamonds
         :mapping {:x :price :color :cut}
         :scales {:color {:domain ["Fair" "Good" "Very Good" "Premium" "Ideal"]}}}]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(assoc p :charts [(chart/density {:position :stack})] :labels {:title ":stack" :x "price [USD]"})
                  (assoc p :charts [(chart/density {:position :normalize})] :labels {:title ":normalize" :x "price [USD]"})]
                 {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 450}))






30.2.7 Marginal density
:margins adds charts beside the panel: the top margin shares the horizontal axis, the right margin the vertical one. Margin charts read the plot’s data and colour mapping, with :x mapped to the shared dimension for them; they have no axes of their own, so the scatter keeps the only x and y axes.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Marginal distribution. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data iris
  :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width :color :species}
  :charts [(chart/scatter)]
  :margins {:top (chart/density {:fill :color :alpha 0.4})
            :right (chart/density {:fill :color :alpha 0.4})}
  :labels {:title "Iris sepals with marginal densities" :x "sepal length [cm]" :y "sepal width [cm]"}}
 {:width 750 :height 650})

title: 30  Distribution
text:
30.3 Histogram
Counts of the values in bins shared by all panels and groups.

30.3.1 Basic histogram
:y chooses the bar height: percent of the total (default), count, density (area 1) or probability.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Histogram. Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange (for [y [:percent :count :density :pmf]]
                 {:data faithful
                  :mapping {:x :waiting}
                  :charts [(chart/histogram {:y y})]
                  :labels {:title (str ":y " y) :x "waiting [min]"}})
               {:columns 2})
 {:width 900 :height 600})






30.3.2 Bin size
:bins takes a fastmath estimation rule, a number of equal bins or explicit breaks.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Histogram bin size. Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange (for [bins [:sturges 5 40 [1.5 2.5 3.5 4 4.5 5.5]]]
                 {:data faithful
                  :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                  :charts [(chart/histogram {:bins bins})]
                  :labels {:title (str ":bins " bins) :x "eruption time [min]"}})
               {:columns 2})
 {:width 900 :height 600})






30.3.3 Mirror histogram
Two groups back to back. Bars are filled by the group colour and outlined by :stroke-color - a colour, :none or :darker (the darkened fill, default); :symmetric gives both halves one range.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Mirror histogram. Data: A-level chemistry scores, England 1997, R mlmRev package Chem97 (Yang et al. 2002); licence: GPL (>= 2) (mlmRev).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange [{:data chem97 :mapping {:x :gcsescore :color :gender}
                 :charts [(chart/histogram {:position :mirror :bins 30})]
                 :labels {:title "default outline" :x "GCSE score"}}
                {:data chem97 :mapping {:x :gcsescore :color :gender}
                 :charts [(chart/histogram {:position :mirror :bins 30 :stroke-color :white :symmetric true})]
                 :labels {:title "white outline, :symmetric" :x "GCSE score"}}]
               {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 450})






30.3.4 Groups on one axis
:position places the groups’ bars: over each other (translucent), side by side, stacked or normalized.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Histogram with several groups. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange (for [position [:overlay :dodge :stack :normalize]]
                 {:data iris
                  :mapping {:x :sepal-length :color :species}
                  :charts [(chart/histogram {:position position :bins 15})]
                  :labels {:title (str ":position " position) :x "sepal length [cm]"}})
               {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 650})






30.3.5 Small multiples
Source: R Graph Gallery - Histogram small multiples. Data: Prices and attributes of round cut diamonds, R ggplot2 package diamonds (Wickham et al.); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 {:data diamonds
  :mapping {:x :price :facet :cut}
  :scales {:facet {:domain ["Fair" "Good" "Very Good" "Premium" "Ideal"]}}
  :charts [(chart/histogram {:bins 30})]
  :labels {:title "Diamond prices by cut" :x "price [USD]"}}
 {:width 900 :height 600})






30.3.6 Marginal histogram
A margin may hold several charts, :size sets its thickness in pixels and :axis true shows the magnitude (count, density) of a histogram or density margin; strips (boxes, rugs, …) work in margins too.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Marginal histogram. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data iris
  :mapping {:x :petal-length :y :petal-width :color :species}
  :charts [(chart/scatter)]
  :margins {:top {:charts (chart/histogram {:bins 25 :position :stack :y :count}) :axis true}
            :right {:charts [(chart/box {:outliers false}) (chart/rug)] :size 70}}
  :labels {:title "Iris petals: stacked histogram on top, boxes and a rug on the right"
           :x "petal length [cm]" :y "petal width [cm]"}}
 {:width 750 :height 650})






30.3.7 Strips on a histogram
Any strip chart (box, violin, rug, stripplot, beeswarm, extent) layers on a histogram or density: {:at v} centres it on y = v; :place :bottom draws it below y = 0 in room the chart asks for.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Histogram with boxplot on top; lattice Fig 3.1 (1, 2). Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange [{:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                 :charts [(chart/histogram {:bins 20}) (chart/box {:place {:at 14.5} :thickness 16})]
                 :labels {:title "box above ({:at 14.5})" :x "eruption time [min]"}}
                {:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                 :charts [(chart/density) (chart/rug {:place :bottom :width 1.0})]
                 :labels {:title "rug below (:bottom)" :x "eruption time [min]"}}
                {:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                 :charts [(chart/density) (chart/stripplot {:place :bottom :rng (r/rng :mersenne 2) :size 6})]
                 :labels {:title "jittered points below" :x "eruption time [min]"}}
                {:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions}
                 :charts [(chart/histogram {:bins 20}) (chart/beeswarm {:place :bottom :size 4 :bottom-share 0.3})]
                 :labels {:title "beeswarm below" :x "eruption time [min]"}}]
               {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 700})

title: 30  Distribution
text:
30.4 Boxplot
A Tukey box per group: quartiles, whiskers to the most extreme values within 1.5 IQR, outliers beyond.

30.4.1 Basic boxplot
Source: R Graph Gallery - Boxplot. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data mtcars
  :mapping {:x :mpg :y :cyl}
  :scales {:y {:type :categorical}}
  :charts [(chart/box)]
  :labels {:title "Fuel economy by number of cylinders" :x "miles per gallon" :y "cylinders"}}
 {:width 800 :height 400})




The cylinder count is a number, so it is declared categorical - one band per value instead of a numeric axis - with :scales {:y {:type :categorical}}; strings and keywords are categorical by themselves.


30.4.2 Boxplot with jittered points
Source: R Graph Gallery - Boxplot with jitter. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data mtcars
  :mapping {:x :mpg :y :cyl}
  :scales {:y {:type :categorical}}
  :charts [(chart/box {:outliers false :color [210 210 225]})
           (chart/stripplot {:rng (r/rng :mersenne 7) :jitter 0.2 :size 8 :color [215 48 39 160]})]
  :labels {:title "Box with every car" :x "miles per gallon" :y "cylinders"}}
 {:width 800 :height 400})






30.4.3 Group order
The band scale’s :order-by orders the levels by a function of each level’s rows, from the bottom up; :descending true reverses it.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Reorder boxplot. Data: Barley yields, Minnesota 1931-1932, R lattice package barley (Immer et al. 1934; Fisher 1971; Cleveland 1993); licence: GPL (>= 2) (lattice).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange [{:data barley :mapping {:x :yield :y :variety}
                 :scales {:y {:order-by #(stats/median (map :yield %))}}
                 :charts [(chart/box)]
                 :labels {:title "by median (largest on top)" :x "yield" :y nil}}
                {:data barley :mapping {:x :yield :y :variety}
                 :scales {:y {:order-by #(stats/mean (map :yield %)) :descending true}}
                 :charts [(chart/box)]
                 :labels {:title "by mean, :descending (largest at the bottom)" :x "yield" :y nil}}]
               {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 500})






30.4.4 Highlight a group
A derived column and an explicit colour scale: grey for the rest, red for the group in focus. Each band holds one colour group, so every box stays on its band’s centre line.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Highlight a group in boxplot. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data (map #(assoc % :focus (if (= 6 (:cyl %)) "6 cylinders" "other")) mtcars)
  :mapping {:x :hp :y :cyl :color :focus}
  :scales {:y {:type :categorical}
           :color {:domain ["other" "6 cylinders"] :range [[190 190 190] [215 48 39]]}}
  :charts [(chart/box)]
  :labels {:title "Horse power, 6 cylinders highlighted" :x "horse power" :y "cylinders"}}
 {:width 800 :height 400})






30.4.5 Grouped boxplot
Source: R Graph Gallery - Grouped boxplot. Data: Barley yields, Minnesota 1931-1932, R lattice package barley (Immer et al. 1934; Fisher 1971; Cleveland 1993); licence: GPL (>= 2) (lattice).

(plot/render-image
 {:data barley
  :mapping {:x :yield :y :site :color :year}
  :scales {:color {:type :categorical}}
  :charts [(chart/box)]
  :labels {:title "Barley yield by site and year" :x "yield [bushels/acre]" :y nil}}
 {:width 800 :height 500})






30.4.6 Faceted boxplot
Source: R Graph Gallery - Boxplot small multiples. Data: Barley yields, Minnesota 1931-1932, R lattice package barley (Immer et al. 1934; Fisher 1971; Cleveland 1993); licence: GPL (>= 2) (lattice).

(plot/render-image
 {:data barley
  :mapping {:x :yield :y :year :facet :site}
  :scales {:y {:type :categorical}}
  :charts [(chart/box)]
  :labels {:title "Yield by year, one panel per site" :x "yield" :y nil}}
 {:width 900 :height 500})






30.4.7 Variable width
:varwidth makes each box’s width proportional to the square root of its count.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Boxplot with variable width. Data: A-level chemistry scores, England 1997, R mlmRev package Chem97 (Yang et al. 2002); licence: GPL (>= 2) (mlmRev).

(plot/render-image
 {:data chem97
  :mapping {:x :gcsescore :y :score}
  :scales {:y {:type :categorical}}
  :charts [(chart/box {:varwidth true :n-label true})]
  :labels {:title "GCSE score by A-level score" :x "GCSE score" :y "A-level score"}}
 {:width 800 :height 550})






30.4.8 Binned continuous variable
levels/bin cuts a numeric column into half-open interval bins; the bins are ordered levels for the boxes.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Boxplot from continuous variable. Data: Prices and attributes of round cut diamonds, R ggplot2 package diamonds (Wickham et al.); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 {:data (levels/bin diamonds :carat {:as :carat-bin :bins [0 0.5 1 1.5 2 2.5 5.01]})
  :mapping {:x :price :y :carat-bin}
  :charts [(chart/box {:outliers false :n-label true})]
  :labels {:title "Diamond price by carat" :x "price [USD]" :y "carat"}}
 {:width 800 :height 500})






30.4.9 Mean marker
The categorical declaration can also sit on the mapping: (levels/categorical :gear) reads :gear as usual and makes its dimension categorical, here instead of a :scales entry.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Boxplot with mean. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data mtcars
  :mapping {:x :qsec :y (levels/categorical :gear)}
  :charts [(chart/box {:mean true})]
  :labels {:title "Quarter mile time by gears, mean marked" :x "quarter mile [s]" :y "gears"}}
 {:width 800 :height 400})






30.4.10 Sample size
:n-label with :n-format (a format string for the count).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Boxplot with sample size. Data: Barley yields, Minnesota 1931-1932, R lattice package barley (Immer et al. 1934; Fisher 1971; Cleveland 1993); licence: GPL (>= 2) (lattice).

(plot/render-image
 {:data barley
  :mapping {:x :yield :y :variety :color :year}
  :scales {:color {:type :categorical}}
  :charts [(chart/box {:n-label true :n-format "%d obs"})]
  :labels {:title "Yield by variety and year" :x "yield" :y nil}}
 {:width 900 :height 650})






30.4.11 Horizontal and vertical
Source: R Graph Gallery - Horizontal boxplot. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [p {:data mtcars :mapping {:x :wt :y :am} :scales {:y {:type :categorical}} :charts [(chart/box)]
         :labels {:x "weight [1000 lbs]" :y "manual transmission"}}]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(assoc-in p [:labels :title] "horizontal")
                  (-> p (assoc :flip true) (assoc-in [:labels :title] ":flip true"))]
                 {:columns 2})
   {:width 900 :height 400}))






30.4.12 Intervals
chart/extent draws an interval per group from fastmath.stats: here the 95% confidence interval of the mean, mean ± standard deviation and a bootstrap percentile interval.
Source: seaborn - pointplot (confidence intervals); cljplot - extents (1, 2). Data: Barley yields, Minnesota 1931-1932, R lattice package barley (Immer et al. 1934; Fisher 1971; Cleveland 1993); licence: GPL (>= 2) (lattice).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange (for [[title opts] [[":ci" {:method :ci}]
                                   [":stddev" {:method :stddev}]
                                   [":bootstrap-percentile" {:method :bootstrap-percentile :rng (r/rng :mersenne 1)}]]]
                 {:data barley :mapping {:x :yield :y :site}
                  :charts [(chart/extent opts)]
                  :labels {:title title :x "yield" :y nil}})
               {:columns 3})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})

title: 30  Distribution
text:
30.5 Ridgeline
Histograms and densities with a categorical :y become ridgelines: one profile per level, growing toward the next level, all on one height scale (:overlap - the tallest profile in band steps).

30.5.1 Basic ridgeline

(def months ["January" "February" "March" "April" "May" "June" "July" "August" "September" "October" "November"
             "December"])

Source: R Graph Gallery - Ridgeline chart. Data: Weather in Lincoln, Nebraska, 2016, R ggridges package lincoln_weather (Weather Underground, via Wilke); licence: GPL-2 (ggridges).

(plot/render-image
 {:data lincoln
  :mapping {:x :mean-temp :y :month}
  :scales {:y {:domain months :reverse true}}
  :charts [(chart/density {:overlap 1.5})]
  :labels {:title "Mean temperature in Lincoln, 2016" :x "mean temperature [F]" :y nil}}
 {:width 800 :height 650})






30.5.2 Ridge shapes
Histograms make ridgelines too; any strip chart can share the bands.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Ridgeline chart. Data: Prices and attributes of round cut diamonds, R ggplot2 package diamonds (Wickham et al.); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(let [p {:data diamonds
         :mapping {:x :price :y :cut}
         :scales {:y {:domain ["Fair" "Good" "Very Good" "Premium" "Ideal"]}}}]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(assoc p :charts [(chart/histogram {:bins 40})] :labels {:title "histogram ridges" :x "price" :y nil})
                  (assoc p :data (take-nth 25 diamonds)
                         :charts [(chart/density {:overlap 0.7}) (chart/stripplot {:rng (r/rng :mersenne 4) :size 3 :jitter 0.2})]
                         :labels {:title "density ridges with points (4% sample)" :x "price" :y nil})]
                 {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 550}))






30.5.3 Gradient fill
:fill-gradient colours the area along :x with a clojure2d gradient.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Ridgeline with gradient. Data: Weather in Lincoln, Nebraska, 2016, R ggridges package lincoln_weather (Weather Underground, via Wilke); licence: GPL-2 (ggridges).

(plot/render-image
 {:data lincoln
  :mapping {:x :max-temp :y :month}
  :scales {:y {:domain months :reverse true}}
  :charts [(chart/density {:overlap 1.5 :fill-gradient :mpl/plasma})]
  :labels {:title "Daily maximum temperature" :x "max temperature [F]" :y nil}}
 {:width 800 :height 650})






30.5.4 Double ridgeline
With two groups, :position :mirror grows the second group away from the next level.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Ridgeline (two groups). Data: A-level chemistry scores, England 1997, R mlmRev package Chem97 (Yang et al. 2002); licence: GPL (>= 2) (mlmRev).

(plot/render-image
 {:data chem97
  :mapping {:x :gcsescore :y :score :color :gender}
  :scales {:y {:type :categorical}}
  :charts [(chart/density {:position :mirror :overlap 0.45})]
  :labels {:title "GCSE score: F up, M down, by A-level score" :x "GCSE score" :y "A-level score"}}
 {:width 800 :height 650})

title: 30  Distribution
30  Distribution
text:
30.7 Strip plot and rug

30.7.1 Strip plot
Jittered points; :rng makes the jitter reproducible.
Source: lattice stripplot; seaborn stripplot (1, 2). Data: Barley yields, Minnesota 1931-1932, R lattice package barley (Immer et al. 1934; Fisher 1971; Cleveland 1993); licence: GPL (>= 2) (lattice).

(plot/render-image
 {:data barley
  :mapping {:x :yield :y :variety :color :year}
  :scales {:color {:type :categorical}}
  :charts [(chart/stripplot {:rng (r/rng :mersenne 1) :size 8 :jitter 0.1})]
  :labels {:title "Barley yield by variety, dodged by year" :x "yield" :y nil}}
 {:width 800 :height 550})






30.7.2 Rug
One line per value along the panel edge (:edge, the default without :y) or below y = 0 (:bottom).
Source: seaborn rugplot; lattice densityplot (1, 2). Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange [{:data faithful :mapping {:x :waiting} :charts [(chart/density) (chart/rug)]
                 :labels {:title "rug on the edge" :x "waiting [min]"}}
                {:data faithful :mapping {:x :waiting} :charts [(chart/density) (chart/rug {:place :bottom :width 1.0})]
                 :labels {:title "rug below zero (:bottom)" :x "waiting [min]"}}]
               {:columns 2})
 {:width 900 :height 400})

title: 30  Distribution
text:
30.8 1d strips
Every strip chart also works on one variable alone: without :y it is placed in the middle of the panel (the rug, on the panel’s edge by default, takes :place :center) and the plot has no y axis.
Source: seaborn boxplot, swarmplot (1d) (1, 2). Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange (for [[title c] [["box" (chart/box)]
                                ["violin" (chart/violin)]
                                ["stripplot" (chart/stripplot {:rng (r/rng :mersenne 5) :jitter 0.3 :size 6})]
                                ["beeswarm" (chart/beeswarm {:size 5})]
                                ["rug" (chart/rug {:place :center :width 0.6})]
                                ["extent :stddev" (chart/extent {:method :stddev})]]]
                 {:data faithful
                  :mapping {:x :waiting}
                  :charts [c]
                  :labels {:title title :x "waiting [min]"}})
               {:columns 2})
 {:width 900 :height 650})

title: 30  Distribution
text:
30.9 Empirical cumulative distribution
Source: lattice ecdfplot; seaborn ecdfplot (1, 2). Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data iris
  :mapping {:x :petal-length :color :species}
  :charts [(chart/ecdf {:line-width 2})]
  :labels {:title "ECDF of petal length by species" :x "petal length [cm]"}}
 {:width 800 :height 450})





source: notebooks/use_cases/distribution.clj

title: 31  Correlation
text:
31.1 Scatter
How two or more variables move together: scatter plots, heatmaps, correlograms, bubble charts, connected scatter plots, 2D densities, functions of two variables and the ways out of overplotting (the R Graph Gallery correlation pages and data-to-viz).
Labels along a trend line and labels moved apart (repel) are shown with the text chart. Not here: 3D densities and interactivity; a heatmap in clustered order with its dendrograms (plot/clustered-heatmap) is in the Flow chapter.
One point per observation at its two values; colour, shape and size carry more variables.

title: 31  Correlation
text:
31.1.1 Basic scatter, styled points
Living area against sale price of 1460 houses: the default points, then a translucent fill with an outline and another shape.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Basic scatterplot with ggplot2; data-to-viz - Scatter (1, 2). Data: House prices: living area and sale price, data-to-viz example dataset 2_TwoNum (Yan Holtz; Kaggle House Prices competition); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data houses :mapping {:x :living-area :y :price} :charts [(chart/scatter)]
    :labels {:title "default" :x "living area, sq ft" :y "price, USD"}}
   {:data houses :mapping {:x :living-area :y :price}
    :charts [(chart/scatter {:shape \A :size 6 :color [70 130 180 90] :stroke-color [20 60 100] :stroke-width 0.5})]
    :labels {:title "translucent triangles with outlines" :x "living area, sq ft" :y nil}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 450})






31.1.2 Colour and shape by group
Mapping :color and :shape to the same variable gives every species its colour and shape, and one legend.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Map a variable to a ggplot2 scatterplot. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width :color :species :shape :species}
  :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 7})]
  :labels {:title "Iris sepals by species" :x "sepal length, cm" :y "sepal width, cm"}}
 {:width 700 :height 500})






31.1.3 Text labels in boxes
A text chart names some cars; :background puts each label on a semi-transparent box, so the points it covers stay visible and the text stays readable over them.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Add text labels with ggplot2. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [label-box {:size 9 :background [255 255 255 200] :inset 2 :mapping {:x :wt :y :mpg :label :model}}]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data mtcars :mapping {:x :wt :y :mpg}
    :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 8 :color [200 60 40]})
             (chart/text (merge label-box {:data (filterv #(> (double (:mpg %)) 31.0) mtcars)
                                           :anchor [:left :middle] :offset [6 0]}))
             (chart/text (merge label-box {:data (filterv #(or (> (double (:wt %)) 5.3) (> (double (:hp %)) 250.0)) mtcars)
                                           :anchor [:right :middle] :offset [-6 0]}))]
    :labels {:title "Cars by weight and fuel use" :x "weight, 1000 lbs" :y "miles per gallon"}}
   {:width 750 :height 500}))






31.1.4 Rugs and marginal distributions
Margins share the panel’s axes: rugs (one line per value) beside both axes, or the densities of both variables.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Marginal distribution with ggplot2. Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting} :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 4})]
  :margins {:top {:charts (chart/rug) :size 25} :right {:charts (chart/rug) :size 25}}
  :labels {:title "Old Faithful with rugs" :x "eruption, min" :y "waiting, min"}}
 {:width 650 :height 480})





(plot/render-image
 {:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting} :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 4})]
  :margins {:top (chart/density {:fill [70 130 180 120]}) :right (chart/density {:fill [70 130 180 120]})}
  :labels {:title "Old Faithful with marginal densities" :x "eruption, min" :y "waiting, min"}}
 {:width 650 :height 520})






31.1.5 Linear fit with a confidence band
chart/smooth {:method :lm} adds the least-squares line and its 95 % confidence band.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Scatterplot with a regression line. Data: House prices: living area and sale price, data-to-viz example dataset 2_TwoNum (Yan Holtz; Kaggle House Prices competition); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 {:data houses :mapping {:x :living-area :y :price}
  :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 3 :color [0 0 0 70]}) (chart/smooth {:method :lm})]
  :labels {:title "Price grows with living area" :x "living area, sq ft" :y "price, USD"}}
 {:width 700 :height 480})






31.1.6 A scatter per group
A facet mapping draws one panel per species on shared scales.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Faceting with ggplot2. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width :facet :species}
  :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 5})]
  :labels {:title "Iris sepals, a panel per species" :x "sepal length, cm" :y "sepal width, cm"}}
 {:width 1000 :height 400})






31.1.7 Size by overlap count
Integer data puts many cars on one point; counting the cars per point and mapping the count to the point’s area (:area true on the size scale) shows how many sit there.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Scatterplot. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [counts (mapv (fn [[[cyl gear] cars]] {:cyl cyl :gear gear :cars (count cars)})
                   (group-by (juxt :cyl :gear) mtcars))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data counts :mapping {:x :cyl :y :gear :size :cars}
    :charts [(chart/scatter {:color [70 130 180 200]})]
    :scales {:size {:area true :range [4 36] :title "cars"}}
    :labels {:title "Cars per cylinder and gear count" :x "cylinders" :y "forward gears"}}
   {:width 650 :height 450}))






31.1.8 Manhattan plot
A genome-wide association plot (seeded data): one point per marker at its position along the chromosomes and its −log10 p-value, chromosomes in alternating colours and numbered at their centres (explicit :ticks with a :formatter), the significance threshold 5·10⁻⁸ as a rule.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Manhattan plot.

(def markers
  "Seeded association results: 22 chromosomes of 200-400 markers, uniform p-values with three peaks."
  (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 101)
        peaks {3 0.4 9 0.7 16 0.3}]
    (loop [chromosome 1 offset 0.0 rows []]
      (if (> chromosome 22)
        rows
        (let [n (r/irandom rng 200 400)
              chromosome-rows (for [i (range n)
                                    :let [t (/ (double i) n)
                                          peak (get peaks chromosome)
                                          strength (if peak (* 9.0 (m/exp (- (m/sq (/ (- t peak) 0.03))))) 0.0)
                                          p (* (r/drandom rng) (m/pow 10.0 (- strength)))]]
                                {:chromosome chromosome :position (+ offset i) :log-p (- (m/log10 (max p 1.0e-12)))})]
          (recur (inc chromosome) (+ offset n) (into rows chromosome-rows)))))))

31.1.9 Simpson’s paradox
Three groups (seeded): within each group y grows with x, across all of them it falls. One fit for everything points the wrong way; a fit per group shows the relation inside the groups.
Source: data-to-viz - Simpson’s paradox.

(def simpson
  (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 33)]
    (vec (for [[g cx cy] [["A" 2.0 9.0] ["B" 5.0 6.0] ["C" 8.0 3.0]]
               _ (range 40)
               :let [dx (r/grandom rng 0.0 1.0)]]
           {:group g :x (+ cx dx) :y (+ cy (* 0.8 dx) (r/grandom rng 0.0 0.5))}))))

31.2.2 Palettes, normalized columns
Raw values put every indicator on one colour scale, so life expectancy (around 80) drowns the rates (0-20); standardizing each column first gives every indicator the full palette. Any palette or gradient works: viridis on the left, a diverging RdBu around 0 on the right.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Heatmap with the levelplot function. Data: Countries: demographic indicators, data-to-viz example dataset multivariate (Yan Holtz; original source not documented); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(let [rows (z-scores (take 25 europe))
      base {:data rows :theme {:axis {:x {:label-rotation 90}}} :labels {:x nil :y nil}}]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange
    [(merge base {:mapping {:x :country :y :indicator :color :value} :charts [(chart/tile)]
                  :scales {:color {:range :viridis :title "value"}}
                  :labels {:title "raw values (viridis)" :x nil :y nil}})
     (merge base {:mapping {:x :country :y :indicator :color :z} :charts [(chart/tile)]
                  :scales {:color {:range :RColorBrewer/RdBu :midpoint 0 :reverse true :title "z-score"}}
                  :labels {:title "standardized per indicator (RdBu)" :x nil :y nil}})]
    {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 520}))






31.2.3 Side colour bar
A category of the columns as a strip of colours above the heatmap: plot/clustered-heatmap orders the rows and columns by clustering and draws :col-annotations ([accessor colour-scale-spec] pairs over the long rows) between the columns’ tree and the tiles, with its own legend (:row-annotations likewise along the rows). Here: up to six of the most populous countries of each continent (the dataset has two in North America), the continent as the side colour.
Source: R Graph Gallery - The heatmap function (side colours). Data: Countries: demographic indicators, data-to-viz example dataset multivariate (Yan Holtz; original source not documented); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(let [picked (vec (mapcat (fn [[_ rows]] (take 6 (sort-by #(- (double (:pop %))) rows)))
                          (sort-by key (group-by :continent countries))))]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/clustered-heatmap (z-scores picked)
                           {:row :indicator :col :country :value :z :tree-size [0.12 0.2]
                            :col-annotations [[:continent {:range :set2}]]
                            :scales {:color {:range :RColorBrewer/RdBu :midpoint 0 :reverse true :title "z-score"}}
                            :title "Indicators of the largest countries per continent"})
   {:width 1000 :height 600}))






31.2.4 Values in cells: the correlation matrix
pairwise/matrix-rows gives r of every pair of variables, here the lower triangle with the diagonal, each pair once; one tile per pair, coloured on a diverging scale over [-1 1] and labelled with its value (:value-label, text in a contrasting colour). The y scale’s :reverse puts the first variable on top.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Correlation matrix with ggally (heatmap). Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data (pairwise/matrix-rows mtcars {:variables [:mpg :cyl :disp :hp :drat :wt :qsec :gear :carb]
                                      :triangle :lower :self-pairs true})
  :mapping {:x (comp name :x) :y (comp name :y) :color :value}
  :scales {:y {:reverse true} :color {:range :RColorBrewer/RdBu :domain [-1 1] :title "r"}}
  :charts [(chart/tile {:stroke-color :white :value-label true})]
  :labels {:title "mtcars: correlation of every pair" :x nil :y nil}}
 {:width 700 :height 600})






31.2.5 Calendar heatmap
Daily bitcoin price changes on a calendar: ISO week across, weekday down, a row of panels per year; the colour is the day’s change, capped at ±10 % so a few extreme days don’t flatten the rest.
Source: R Graph Gallery - The hourly heatmap (calendar layout). Data: Bitcoin daily price, 2013-2018, data-to-viz example dataset 3_TwoNumOrdered (Yan Holtz; CoinMarketCap via JesseVent/crypto); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(let [weekdays ["Mon" "Tue" "Wed" "Thu" "Fri" "Sat" "Sun"]
      days (vec (for [[prev day] (partition 2 1 bitcoin)
                      :let [^LocalDate d (:date day)]]
                  {:week (.get d IsoFields/WEEK_OF_WEEK_BASED_YEAR)
                   :year (.get d IsoFields/WEEK_BASED_YEAR)
                   :weekday (weekdays (dec (.getValue ^DayOfWeek (.getDayOfWeek d))))
                   :change (m/constrain (- (/ (double (:value day)) (double (:value prev))) 1.0) -0.1 0.1)}))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data days :mapping {:x :week :y :weekday :color :change :facet-row :year}
    :scales {:y {:domain weekdays :reverse true}
             :color {:range :RColorBrewer/RdYlGn :midpoint 0 :domain [-0.1 0.1] :title "daily change"
                     :formatter #(format "%+.0f%%" (* 100.0 (double %)))}}
    :charts [(chart/tile {:stroke-color :white})]
    :labels {:title "Bitcoin: daily price change, 2013-2018" :x "ISO week" :y nil}}
   {:width 1000 :height 800}))






31.2.6 Row and column order
Categories come in data order by default (here the dataset’s subregions), which hides structure that a meaningful order shows: the band scale’s :order-by sorts the countries by a function of each one’s rows - its life expectancy.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Heatmap. Data: Countries: demographic indicators, data-to-viz example dataset multivariate (Yan Holtz; original source not documented); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(let [rows (z-scores europe)
      life-expectancy (fn [country-rows] (some #(when (= "life-expectancy" (:indicator %)) (:value %)) country-rows))
      heatmap (fn [order-by title legend?]
                {:data rows :mapping {:x :country :y :indicator :color :z} :legend legend?
                 :scales (cond-> {:color {:range :RColorBrewer/RdBu :midpoint 0 :reverse true :title "z-score"}}
                           order-by (assoc :x {:order-by order-by}))
                 :theme {:axis {:x {:label-rotation 90}}}
                 :charts [(chart/tile)]
                 :labels {:title title :x nil :y nil}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(heatmap nil "data order" false) (heatmap life-expectancy "by life expectancy (:order-by)" true)] {:columns 1})
   {:width 1000 :height 800}))






31.2.7 Smoothed heatmap
Measurements on a coarse lattice (seeded: two bumps and noise) as tiles, and the same values interpolated bicubically into a smooth field with contour lines.
Source: R Graph Gallery - 2D density chart (raster smoothing).

(def lattice
  (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 21)]
    (vec (for [x (range 12) y (range 9)]
           {:x x :y y :z (+ (* 8 (m/exp (- (/ (+ (m/sq (- x 3)) (m/sq (- y 6))) 6.0))))
                            (* 5 (m/exp (- (/ (+ (m/sq (- x 8)) (m/sq (- y 2))) 8.0))))
                            (* 0.6 (r/drandom rng)))}))))

title: 31  Correlation
text:
31.3 Correlogram
All pairs of several variables at once: plot/pairs lays out a matrix of cells sharing the variables’ scales.

31.3.1 Scatter-plot matrix by group
Scatter plots below the diagonal, densities on it, the correlation per species above it, coloured by species.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Correlogram; data-to-viz - Correlogram (1, 2). Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/pairs iris {:variables [:sepal-length :sepal-width :petal-length :petal-width] :mapping {:color :species}
                   :theme {:palette {:color :set1}} :title "Iris measurements by species"})
 {:width 950 :height 800})






31.3.2 Correlation glyphs
chart/correlation draws r of its cell as a glyph: ellipses (the shape of a bivariate normal with that r) below, pies (|r| as a filled angle) above, the variable names on the diagonal; the r colour bar on the side.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Correlation ellipses. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/pairs mtcars {:variables [:mpg :disp :hp :drat :wt :qsec]
                     :lower (chart/correlation {:glyph :ellipse}) :upper (chart/correlation {:glyph :pie})
                     :diagonal :names :title "mtcars correlogram"})
 {:width 800 :height 750})

title: 31  Correlation
text:
31.4 Bubble
A scatter plot with a third variable as the point’s size - by area, so a point twice the value has twice the ink.

31.4.1 Bubble chart: area, size range, colours and legend
Gapminder 2007: income (log axis) against life expectancy, population as the bubble’s area (:area true, size range 1-40 px), continent as colour; the :order mapping with :descending true draws the largest bubbles first, so the small ones stay on top. The left panel maps population linearly to the diameter: large countries look far larger than they are.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Bubble chart; data-to-viz - Bubble (1, 2). Data: Gapminder 2007: life expectancy, population and GDP per capita, data-to-viz example dataset 4_ThreeNum (Yan Holtz; Gapminder via the R gapminder package); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(let [bubbles (fn [area? title legend?]
                {:data gapminder :legend legend?
                 :mapping {:x :gdp-per-cap :y :life-exp :size #(/ (double (:pop %)) 1.0e6) :color :continent :order :pop}
                 :scales {:x {:kind :log} :size (cond-> {:range [1 40] :title "population, M"} area? (assoc :area true))}
                 :charts [(chart/scatter {:stroke-color :white :stroke-width 0.5 :descending true})]
                 :theme {:palette {:color :set2}}
                 :labels {:title title :x "GDP per capita, USD" :y "life expectancy, years"}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(bubbles false "diameter linear in population" false) (bubbles true "area linear in population" true)]
                 {:columns 2 :widths [1 1.25]})
   {:width 1000 :height 480}))

title: 31  Correlation
text:
31.5 Connected scatter
Two variables over time: the points in time order joined by a path, dates written next to some of them.

31.5.1 Connected scatter with dates
Yearly means of US unemployment duration and savings rate, 1990-2014, joined in time order (:order :data) by a smooth path (:curve :bezier) ending in an arrowhead (:arrow, see line); labels on boxes keep the years readable where the path crosses itself.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Connected scatterplot with ggplot2; data-to-viz - Connected scatter (1, 2). Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(let [yearly (vec (for [[year rows] (sort-by key (group-by #(.getYear ^LocalDate (:date %)) economics))
                        :when (<= 1990 year 2014)]
                    {:year year :uempmed (stats/mean (map :uempmed rows)) :psavert (stats/mean (map :psavert rows))}))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data yearly :mapping {:x :uempmed :y :psavert}
    :charts [(chart/line {:order :data :curve :bezier :color [33 102 172] :arrow {:end true :size 12} :end-gap 4})
             (chart/scatter {:size 6 :color [33 102 172]})
             (chart/text {:data (filterv #(zero? (mod (long (:year %)) 4)) yearly)
                          :mapping {:x :uempmed :y :psavert :label :year}
                          :background [255 255 255 210] :inset 2 :anchor [:left :bottom] :offset [5 5]})]
    :labels {:title "Unemployment duration vs savings rate, 1990-2014" :x "median unemployment, weeks" :y "savings rate, %"}}
   {:width 800 :height 550}))

title: 31  Correlation
text:
31.6 2D density
Where the points concentrate: counts in cells, a smooth density estimate, its contour lines.

31.6.1 2D histogram and hexbin
chart/bin2d counts points in cells: squares, or hexagons (the default) - regular on screen for the panel’s shape.
Source: R Graph Gallery - 2D density chart; data-to-viz - 2D density (1, 2). Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting} :charts [(chart/bin2d {:cell :square :bins 20})]
    :legend false :labels {:title "2D histogram" :x "eruption, min" :y "waiting, min"}}
   {:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting} :charts [(chart/bin2d {:bins 20})]
    :labels {:title "hexbin" :x "eruption, min" :y nil}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 450})






31.6.2 2D kernel density and contours
chart/field estimates the density (Gaussian kernel, a bandwidth per axis) and draws it as a raster; chart/contour draws its level lines, or with :filled true the bands between them.
Source: R Graph Gallery - 2D density plot with ggplot2. Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting}
    :charts [(chart/field) (chart/contour {:color :white :line-width 0.8})] :legend false
    :labels {:title "density raster and contour lines" :x "eruption, min" :y "waiting, min"}}
   {:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting}
    :charts [(chart/contour {:filled true :levels 8})]
    :labels {:title "filled contour bands" :x "eruption, min" :y nil}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 450})






31.6.3 Points over a density
The density as a backdrop for the points themselves.
Source: R Graph Gallery - 2D density chart. Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data faithful :mapping {:x :eruptions :y :waiting}
  :charts [(chart/field {:alpha-factor 0.8}) (chart/scatter {:size 3 :color [255 255 255 200]})]
  :labels {:title "Old Faithful eruptions over their density" :x "eruption, min" :y "waiting, min"}}
 {:width 700 :height 500})

title: 31  Correlation
text:
31.7 Functions
chart/field {:f f} samples a function of a point [x y] on a grid over a given domain (:n samples per axis) - no data needed. These examples have no gallery counterpart.

31.7.1 A function as a raster
MATLAB’s “peaks” surface - a maximum above the centre, a minimum below it and smaller lobes - on [−3, 3]², white to black, 300 × 300 samples, square pixels (:aspect :iso).

(defn peaks
  "The peaks function of a point `[x y]`: 3(1 − x)² e^(−x² − (y + 1)²) − 10(x/5 − x³ − y⁵) e^(−x² − y²) −
  e^(−(x + 1)² − y²) / 3."
  [[^double x ^double y]]
  (- (* 3.0 (m/sq (- 1.0 x)) (m/exp (- (- (* x x)) (m/sq (+ y 1.0)))))
     (* 10.0 (- (/ x 5.0) (* x x x) (m/pow y 5.0)) (m/exp (- (- (* x x)) (* y y))))
     (/ (m/exp (- (- (m/sq (+ x 1.0))) (* y y))) 3.0)))


(plot/render-image
 {:charts [(chart/field {:f peaks :domain {:x [-3 3] :y [-3 3]} :n 300})]
  :scales {:color {:range [:white :black]}}
  :aspect :iso
  :labels {:title "peaks(x, y)"}}
 {:width 650 :height 600})






31.7.2 A function with contour lines
sin x · cos y on a diverging palette centred at 0, with contour lines at fixed levels.

(let [wave (fn [[x y]] (* (m/sin x) (m/cos y)))
      domain {:x [0 (* 2 m/PI)] :y [0 4]}]
  (plot/render-image
   {:charts [(chart/field {:f wave :domain domain})
             (chart/contour {:f wave :domain domain :color :black :levels [-0.75 -0.5 -0.25 0 0.25 0.5 0.75]})]
    :scales {:color {:range :RColorBrewer/RdBu :midpoint 0 :title "sin x cos y"}}
    :labels {:title "sin x cos y with contour lines"}}
   {:width 700 :height 450}))

title: 31  Correlation
text:
31.8 Overplotting
With thousands of points a scatter plot turns into a blot. The usual ways out, on 53 940 diamonds.

31.8.1 Size, transparency, sampling, binning, facets, margins
Smaller points and transparency let density show; a sample keeps the shape with fewer points; hexagon counts replace points by numbers; facets split the cloud by a category; marginal densities show where it is thick.
Source: data-to-viz - Overplotting. Data: Prices and attributes of round cut diamonds, R ggplot2 package diamonds (Wickham et al.); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(let [base {:data diamonds :mapping {:x :carat :y :price} :scales {:x {:domain [0 5.5] :nice false :expand [0 0]} :y {:domain [0 20000] :nice false :expand [0 0]}}}
      sample (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 9)] (filterv (fn [_] (< (r/drandom rng) 0.04)) diamonds))]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange
    [(merge base {:charts [(chart/scatter)] :labels {:title "all points" :x "carat" :y "price, USD"}})
     (merge base {:charts [(chart/scatter {:size 1})] :labels {:title "small points" :x "carat" :y nil}})
     (merge base {:charts [(chart/scatter {:size 3 :color [30 60 120 12]})] :labels {:title "transparency" :x "carat" :y nil}})
     (merge base {:data sample :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 3 :color [30 60 120 120]})]
                  :labels {:title "4 % sample" :x "carat" :y "price, USD"}})
     (merge base {:charts [(chart/bin2d {:bins 30})] :legend false :labels {:title "hexbin" :x "carat" :y nil}})
     (merge base {:charts [(chart/scatter {:size 2 :color [30 60 120 20]})]
                  :margins {:top (chart/density {:fill [30 60 120 100]}) :right (chart/density {:fill [30 60 120 100]})}
                  :labels {:title "marginal densities" :x "carat" :y nil}})]
    {:columns 3})
   {:width 1000 :height 700}))




Source: data-to-viz - Overplotting (facets). Data: Prices and attributes of round cut diamonds, R ggplot2 package diamonds (Wickham et al.); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 {:data diamonds :mapping {:x :carat :y :price :facet :cut}
  :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 2 :color [30 60 120 25]})]
  :scales {:facet {:domain ["Fair" "Good" "Very Good" "Premium" "Ideal"]}}
  :labels {:title "Diamonds: a panel per cut, worst to best" :x "carat" :y "price, USD"}}
 {:width 1000 :height 400})






31.8.2 Jitter
Integer values pile up on a few positions; :jitter [dx dy] moves every point by a random offset within ±dx, ±dy (data units) so the piles spread - :rng with a seed makes it the same in every rendering.
Source: data-to-viz - Overplotting (jitter). Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [gears (fn [title jitter]
              {:data mtcars :mapping {:x :cyl :y :gear}
               :charts [(chart/scatter (cond-> {:size 7 :color [40 40 40 120]}
                                         jitter (assoc :jitter jitter :rng (r/rng :mersenne 7))))]
               :labels {:title title :x "cylinders" :y "forward gears"}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(gears "32 cars on 8 positions" nil) (gears ":jitter [0.25 0.15]" [0.25 0.15])] {:columns 2})
   {:width 900 :height 420}))

title: 31  Correlation
text:
31.9 Caveats

31.9.1 Anscombe’s quartet
Four datasets with the same means, variances, linear fit and r ≈ 0.82 - and four different relations: a line, a curve, a line with an outlier, a single far point making the correlation. Always look at the scatter plot. The same mean and spread of x and the same residual variance give the same line and confidence band; drawn over the whole x domain (:full-range with an explicit :domain, shared by the panels) they coincide.
Source: Anscombe (1973), Graphs in Statistical Analysis. Data: Anscombe’s quartet: similar statistics, different patterns, vega-datasets 3.3.1 anscombe.json (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/vega-datasets@3.3.1/data/anscombe.json); original: Anscombe’s quartet (Wikipedia), Anscombe, F. J. (1973). Graphs in Statistical Analysis. The American Statistician, 27(1):17-21.; licence: none listed - see vega-datasets (cite Vega as the source).

    :charts [(chart/smooth {:method :lm :full-range true})
             (chart/scatter {:size 7 :color [200 60 40]})
             (chart/text {:data (vec (for [[series rows] (group-by :series anscombe)] {:series series :x 4 :y 13 :label (r-label rows)}))
                          :mapping {:x :x :y :y :label :label} :anchor [:left :top]
                          :background [255 255 255 210] :inset 3})]
    :labels {:title "Anscombe's quartet: one r, four relations"}}
   {:width 1000 :height 330}))






31.9.2 Other caveats

Correlation is not causation: two variables can move together because a third one drives both.
Pearson’s r measures only a linear relation: very different clouds (Anscombe’s quartet) share one r; look at the scatter plot, and use Spearman or Kendall (chart/correlation {:method :spearman}) for monotone relations.
Bubbles: map the value to the area (:area true), not the diameter, or large values look far larger.
2D histograms and densities depend on the cell size or bandwidth: try a few before reading shapes into them.

title: 32  Ranking
text:
32.1 Barplot
Values of categories, compared and ordered: bars, lollipops, circular bars, parallel coordinates and radar charts (the R Graph Gallery ranking pages - barplot, lollipop, circular barplot, spider, parallel - and the data-to-viz caveats).
Bars are a strip chart: the levels sit on the categorical axis - {:x :country :y :value} draws vertical bars, {:x :value :y :country} horizontal ones (:level-axis decides when both or neither axis is categorical). Order comes from the data (levels in first-appearance order: left to right, bottom to top), the band scale’s :order-by (a statistic of each level’s rows, :descending reverses it; see Order and direction) or an explicit :domain.
A bar per category: its length is the value (:stat :sum of the rows of a level - one row gives its value), a mean, a median, or a count of rows.

title: 32  Ranking
text:
32.1.1 Basic barplot
Twenty long country names read best on horizontal bars: the countries on :y.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Basic barplot with ggplot2; data-to-viz - Barplot (1, 2). Data: Weapon exports by country, data-to-viz example dataset 7_OneCatOneNum (Yan Holtz); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 {:data (rseq top-20)
  :mapping {:x :value :y :country}
  :charts [(chart/bar)]
  :labels {:title "Weapon exports, top 20 countries" :x "exports" :y nil}}
 {:width 800 :height 500})






32.1.2 Colour, outline and width
:color fills, :stroke-color / :stroke-width outline (default: the fill darkened), :width - the share of the band a bar takes.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Basic barplot with ggplot2; Custom barplot layout (1, 2). Data: Weapon exports by country, data-to-viz example dataset 7_OneCatOneNum (Yan Holtz); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (vec (for [[title opts] [[":color" {:color [215 48 39]}]
                           [":stroke-color, :stroke-width" {:color :white :stroke-color [33 102 172] :stroke-width 2}]
                           [":width 0.4" {:width 0.4}]]]
         {:data top-10
          :mapping {:x :country :y :value}
          :theme {:axis {:x {:label-rotation -90}}}
          :charts [(chart/bar opts)]
          :labels {:title title :x nil :y nil}}))
  {:columns 3})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})






32.1.3 Horizontal and vertical bars
The mapping orients the bars: the countries on :x - vertical bars (tick labels turned -45°), on :y - horizontal ones, which keep long labels readable.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Barplot; data-to-viz - Barplot (1, 2). Data: Weapon exports by country, data-to-viz example dataset 7_OneCatOneNum (Yan Holtz); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data top-10 :mapping {:x :country :y :value}
    :theme {:axis {:x {:label-rotation -45}}}
    :charts [(chart/bar)]
    :labels {:title "{:x :country :y :value}" :x nil :y "exports"}}
   {:data (rseq top-10) :mapping {:x :value :y :country}
    :charts [(chart/bar)]
    :labels {:title "{:x :value :y :country}" :x "exports" :y nil}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 450})






32.1.4 Order by value
Levels follow the data (the first level at the bottom of horizontal bars - :reverse true turns the axis, so the alphabetical data reads from the top); :order-by orders them by value, so the ranking reads from the top.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Reorder a variable with ggplot2. Data: Weapon exports by country, data-to-viz example dataset 7_OneCatOneNum (Yan Holtz); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data (sort-by :country top-20) :mapping {:x :value :y :country}
    :scales {:y {:reverse true}}
    :charts [(chart/bar)]
    :labels {:title "Alphabetical (data order, :reverse)" :x "exports" :y nil}}
   {:data top-20 :mapping {:x :value :y :country}
    :scales {:y {:order-by level-value}}
    :charts [(chart/bar)]
    :labels {:title "By value (:order-by)" :x "exports" :y nil}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 500})






32.1.5 Variable width
:varwidth true - bar widths by the square root of the number of rows (as box plots), :n-label writes the counts: mean fuel economy per number of cylinders, 11, 7 and 14 cars. The cylinder counts are numbers, declared categorical with levels/categorical.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Barplot with variable width. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data mtcars
  :mapping {:x (levels/categorical :cyl) :y :mpg}
  :charts [(chart/bar {:stat :mean :varwidth true :n-label true})]
  :labels {:title "Mean fuel economy, widths by the number of cars" :x "cylinders" :y "mean miles per gallon"}}
 {:width 800 :height 400})






32.1.6 Error bars
chart/extent with the bars’ mapping takes the same slots: mean bars with ± one standard deviation.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Barplot with error bars. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (vec (for [k [:sepal-length :petal-length]]
         {:data iris :mapping {:x :species :y k}
          :charts [(chart/bar {:stat :mean :color [120 160 200]})
                   (chart/extent {:method :stddev :center :none :color [40 40 40] :line-width 1.5})]
          :labels {:title (str "Mean " (name k) " ± sd") :x nil :y "cm"}}))
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 900 :height 400})






32.1.7 Black-and-white bars
Patterns tell groups apart without colour: :pattern maps a variable to the theme’s pattern set (a legend included); a literal :pattern textures every bar. Histograms, densities, areas, ribbons, smooth bands, rects, boxes, violins, candlesticks, treemaps, partitions, packs, waffles and radar fills take patterns too.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Black and white barchart. Data: Prices and attributes of round cut diamonds, R ggplot2 package diamonds (Wickham et al.); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data (filter #(#{"Fair" "Good" "Ideal"} (:cut %)) diamonds)
    :mapping {:x :clarity :pattern :cut}
    :scales {:x {:domain clarities} :pattern {:domain ["Fair" "Good" "Ideal"]}}
    :charts [(chart/bar {:stat :count :color :white :stroke-color :black :pattern-color :black})]
    :labels {:title "Diamonds per clarity, :pattern by cut" :x nil :y "count"}}
   {:data top-10 :mapping {:x :country :y :value}
    :theme {:axis {:x {:label-rotation -90}}}
    :charts [(chart/bar {:color :white :stroke-color :black :pattern :hatch :pattern-color :black})]
    :labels {:title "A literal :pattern :hatch" :x nil :y "exports"}}]
  {:columns 2 :widths [3 2]})
 {:width 1000 :height 450})






32.1.8 Value labels
:value-label true writes each bar’s length past its end - above vertical bars, beside horizontal ones.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Barplot with number of observations. Data: Weapon exports by country, data-to-viz example dataset 7_OneCatOneNum (Yan Holtz); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data top-10 :mapping {:x :country :y :value}
    :theme {:axis {:x {:label-rotation -45}}}
    :charts [(chart/bar {:value-label true})]
    :labels {:title "Vertical" :x nil :y "exports"}}
   {:data (rseq top-10) :mapping {:x :value :y :country}
    :charts [(chart/bar {:value-label true})]
    :labels {:title "Horizontal" :x "exports" :y nil}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 450})






32.1.9 Grouped bars
A second categorical variable on :color dodges the bars inside each band (the default with two or more groups per level).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Grouped, stacked and percent stacked barplot. Data: Prices and attributes of round cut diamonds, R ggplot2 package diamonds (Wickham et al.); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 {:data diamonds
  :mapping {:x :clarity :color :cut}
  :scales {:x {:domain clarities} :color {:domain cuts}}
  :charts [(chart/bar {:stat :count})]
  :labels {:title "Diamonds per clarity and cut" :x "clarity" :y "count"}}
 {:width 900 :height 450})






32.1.10 Stacked bars
:position :stack piles the groups up, :normalize scales every stack to 1 (shares).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Grouped, stacked and percent stacked barplot. Data: Prices and attributes of round cut diamonds, R ggplot2 package diamonds (Wickham et al.); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (vec (for [p [:stack :normalize]]
         {:data diamonds
          :mapping {:x :clarity :color :cut}
          :scales {:x {:domain clarities} :color {:domain cuts}}
          :charts [(chart/bar {:stat :count :position p})]
          :labels {:title (str ":position " p) :x "clarity"}}))
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 450})






32.1.11 Mirrored bars
The bar :mirror turns the second level of a two-level variable the other way: back-to-back bars, with value tick labels as magnitudes. Answers for and against eight proposals, stacked by how sure people were: the mirror on :group (for / against), four colours - two blues, two reds - on :color.

32.1.12 Economist-style labelled bars
No axes - the labels carry the values: name and value inside the bar at its base when they fit (a text chart at x = 0, in white), else just past the bar’s end. Whether a label fits is estimated here: about 7 pixels per character against the bar’s share of a 700 pixel panel.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Horizontal barplot with labels (The Economist style). Data: Weapon exports by country, data-to-viz example dataset 7_OneCatOneNum (Yan Holtz); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(let [rows (mapv #(assoc % :label (str (:country %) "  " (:value %))) top-10)
      longest (double (reduce max (map :value rows)))
      fits? (fn [{:keys [value label]}] (> (* 700.0 (/ (double value) longest)) (+ 12.0 (* 7.0 (count label)))))
      text (fn [rows x anchor color] (chart/text {:data rows :mapping {:x x :y :country :label :label}
                                                  :anchor anchor :offset [6 0] :color color}))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data rows
    :mapping {:x :value :y :country}
    :scales {:y {:order-by level-value :axis false} :x {:axis false}}
    :theme {:panel {:grid {:x :none :y :none :bands-fill :none}}}
    :charts [(chart/bar {:color [0 104 139] :stroke-color :none :width 0.7})
             (text (filterv fits? rows) (constantly 0) [:left :middle] :white)
             (text (filterv (complement fits?) rows) :value [:left :middle] [0 104 139])]
    :labels {:title {:text "Weapon exports\nTop 10 countries, value of exports" :align [:left :middle]} :x nil :y nil}}
   {:width 800 :height 450}))

title: 32  Ranking
text:
32.2 Lollipop and dot plots
A thin stem and a point carry the value with less ink than a bar: chart/segment from the baseline under a chart/scatter.

32.2.1 Lollipop
Stems from 0 ((chart/segment {:xend 0})), styled stems and markers, and a baseline at the mean - stems grow both ways.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Basic lollipop plot; Custom lollipop chart; data-to-viz - Lollipop (1, 2, 3). Data: Weapon exports by country, data-to-viz example dataset 7_OneCatOneNum (Yan Holtz); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(let [mean (stats/mean (map :value top-20))
      base {:data top-20 :mapping {:x :value :y :country} :scales {:y {:order-by level-value}}}]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange
    [(assoc base :charts [(chart/segment {:xend 0}) (chart/scatter)]
            :labels {:title "Basic" :x "exports" :y nil})
     (assoc base :charts [(chart/segment {:xend 0 :color [150 150 150] :line-width 2})
                          (chart/scatter {:size 9 :color [215 48 39] :shape \s})]
            :labels {:title "Styled stems and markers" :x "exports" :y nil})
     (assoc base :charts [(chart/rule {:x mean :dash :dashed})
                          (chart/segment {:xend mean :color [150 150 150]})
                          (chart/scatter {:size 7 :color [33 102 172]})]
            :labels {:title "Baseline at the mean" :x "exports" :y nil})]
    {:columns 3})
   {:width 1000 :height 500}))

Two values per item: dots alone (Cleveland), or joined by a segment from one to the other (dumbbell), ordered by the second value.

      dots (fn [k color] (chart/scatter {:mapping {:x k :y :team} :size 8 :color color}))]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange
    [{:data scores :scales by-season-2
      :charts [(dots :season-2 [33 102 172])]
      :labels {:title "Cleveland dot plot: season 2" :x "score" :y nil}}

      :charts [(chart/segment {:mapping {:x :season-1 :xend :season-2 :y :team} :color [170 170 170] :line-width 2})
               (dots :season-1 [150 150 150]) (dots :season-2 [33 102 172])]
      :labels {:title "Dumbbell: season 1 (grey) to season 2 (blue)" :x "score" :y nil}}]
    {:columns 2})

32.2.3 Conditional colour and highlight
A derived column colours the lollipops above and below a threshold; a level map keeps one country in colour and greys the rest.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Lollipop chart with conditional color. Data: Weapon exports by country, data-to-viz example dataset 7_OneCatOneNum (Yan Holtz); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(let [mean (stats/mean (map :value top-20))
      rows (mapv #(assoc % :side (if (> (double (:value %)) mean) "above the mean" "below the mean")
                         :highlight (if (= "Germany (FRG)" (:country %)) "Germany (FRG)" "others"))
                 top-20)
      base {:data rows :scales {:y {:order-by level-value}}}]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange
    [(assoc base :mapping {:x :value :y :country :color :side}
            :charts [(chart/segment {:xend mean}) (chart/scatter {:size 7})]
            :labels {:title "Above / below the mean" :x "exports" :y nil})
     (assoc base :mapping {:x :value :y :country :color :highlight}
            :scales (assoc (:scales base) :color {:range {"Germany (FRG)" [215 48 39] "others" [190 190 190]}})
            :charts [(chart/segment {:xend 0}) (chart/scatter {:size 7})]
            :labels {:title "One country highlighted" :x "exports" :y nil})]
    {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 500}))

          :labels {:title (str ":position " p) :x nil :y nil}}))
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 500})






32.3.3 Circular lollipop
Segments and points in polar coordinates: the levels on the angle (:x), the values on the radius - on a log scale (stems from 50), so the small values don’t crowd the centre.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Circular barplot. Data: Weapon exports by country, data-to-viz example dataset 7_OneCatOneNum (Yan Holtz); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 {:data top-20 :mapping {:x :country :y :value}
  :coord {:kind :polar :start -9}
  :scales {:x {:order-by level-value :descending true} :y {:kind :log}}
  :charts [(chart/segment {:yend 50 :color [150 150 150]}) (chart/scatter {:size 8 :color [215 48 39]})]
  :labels {:title "Weapon exports, top 20" :x nil :y nil}}
 {:width 600 :height 600})

title: 32  Ranking
text:
32.4 Parallel coordinates
Each row a line across one axis per variable (chart/parallel over :variables); every axis has its own scale in the variable’s units, drawn by the chart.

(def iris-variables [:sepal-length :sepal-width :petal-length :petal-width])


32.4.1 Parallel coordinates: groups, highlight, vertical
Lines coloured by species; a level map greys all but one species; :flip true stacks the axes vertically.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Parallel coordinates chart with ggally; data-to-viz - Parallel coordinates (1, 2). Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data iris :mapping {:color :species}
    :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables iris-variables})]
    :labels {:title "By species" :x nil}}
   {:data iris :mapping {:color :species}
    :scales {:color {:range {"setosa" [190 190 190 120] "versicolor" [190 190 190 120] "virginica" [215 48 39 220]}}}
    :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables iris-variables})]
    :labels {:title "Virginica highlighted" :x nil}}
   {:data iris :mapping {:color :species} :flip true
    :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables iris-variables})]
    :labels {:title "Vertical (:flip true)" :x nil}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 800})






32.4.2 Smooth connections
:curve :smooth joins the axes with curves that meet every axis flat, at its value, and never overshoot; :smoothness (0..1) moves the bend toward the axes.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Parallel plot. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (vec (for [[title opts] [["Straight" {}] [":curve :smooth" {:curve :smooth}]]]
         {:data (take-nth 3 iris) :mapping {:color :species} :legend false
          :charts [(chart/parallel (merge {:variables iris-variables} opts))]
          :labels {:title title :x nil}}))
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})






32.4.3 Scaling
:scaling - per variable (v - offset) / scale: :std (mean, sd), :robust (median, R’s mad), :uniminmax (every axis 0..1, the default), :globalminmax (the values as they are, one scale).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Parallel coordinates chart with ggally (scaling). Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (vec (for [scaling [:std :robust :uniminmax :globalminmax]]
         {:data iris :mapping {:color :species} :legend false
          :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables iris-variables :scaling scaling :line-width 0.5})]
          :labels {:title (str ":scaling " scaling) :x nil}}))
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 700})






32.4.4 Axis order
The axes follow :variables: neighbours are compared, so the order changes what the chart shows.
Source: data-to-viz - Parallel coordinates (axis order). Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (vec (for [[title vs] [["Measured order" iris-variables]
                          ["Sepal width beside the petals" [:sepal-width :petal-length :sepal-length :petal-width]]]]
         {:data iris :mapping {:color :species} :legend false
          :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables vs})]
          :labels {:title title :x nil}}))
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})

32.5.1 Radar: groups and limits
Four cars filled; the same cars on axes fixed to the range of all cars (:limits); all cars by cylinders on standardized axes.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Basic radar chart; Radar chart with several individuals (1, 2). Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [(plot/arrange
    [{:data four-cars :mapping {:color :model} :coord {:kind :polar} :legend false
      :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables car-variables :fill :color :line-width 2})]
      :labels {:title "Four cars, their own ranges" :x nil}}
     {:data four-cars :mapping {:color :model} :coord {:kind :polar}
      :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables car-variables :fill :color :line-width 2 :limits car-limits})]
      :labels {:title "Ranges of all 32 cars (:limits)" :x nil}}]
    {:columns 2 :widths [2 3]})
   {:data (map #(assoc % :cylinders (str (long (:cyl %)))) mtcars) :mapping {:color :cylinders} :coord {:kind :polar}
    :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables car-variables :scaling :std})]
    :labels {:title "All cars by cylinders (:std)" :x nil}}]
  {:columns 1 :heights [1 1]})
 {:width 1000 :height 800})






32.5.2 Variables as rings
With :flip true the variables become rings and the values angles: every flower is a line from ring to ring - the species separate on the petal rings and mix on sepal width.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Spider / radar chart. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data iris :mapping {:color :species}
  :coord {:kind :polar :inner 0.25} :flip true
  :scales {:color {:range {"setosa" [27 158 119 110] "versicolor" [217 95 2 110] "virginica" [117 112 179 110]}}}
  :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables iris-variables :line-width 0.8})]
  :labels {:title "150 iris flowers across four rings" :x nil}}
 {:width 750 :height 700})

title: 32  Ranking
text:
32.6 Bump
A bump chart shows ranks over time - see Evolution - Bump chart (levels/rank-rows, monotone lines, end labels).

title: 32  Ranking
text:
32.7 Caveats

32.7.1 Order the data
Unordered categories make the reader sort them; ordered by value, the ranking is read at a glance - here all 38 rows with a value (36 countries, “Others” and “Unknown supplier(s)”), as lollipops on a log scale (exports from 2 to 12394; the stems start at 1, as log 0 is undefined).
Source: data-to-viz - Order your data. Data: Weapon exports by country, data-to-viz example dataset 7_OneCatOneNum (Yan Holtz); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (vec (for [[title y-scale] [["Alphabetical" {:reverse true}] ["Ordered by value" {:order-by level-value}]]]
         {:data (sort-by :country weapons) :mapping {:x :value :y :country}
          :scales {:x {:kind :log} :y y-scale}
          :theme {:axis {:y {:label-gap 1}}}
          :charts [(chart/segment {:xend 1 :color [150 150 150]}) (chart/scatter {:size 5 :color [33 102 172]})]
          :labels {:title title :x "exports (log scale)" :y nil}}))
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 800})






32.7.2 Barplot or histogram
A barplot shows a value per category; a histogram shows how one numeric variable is distributed - bins of a continuous axis, no gaps.
Source: data-to-viz - Barplot; Histogram (1, 2). Data: Prices and attributes of round cut diamonds, R ggplot2 package diamonds (Wickham et al.); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data diamonds :mapping {:x :cut} :scales {:x {:domain cuts}}
    :charts [(chart/bar {:stat :count})] :labels {:title "Barplot: diamonds per cut" :x nil :y "count"}}
   {:data diamonds :mapping {:x :price}
    :charts [(chart/histogram)] :labels {:title "Histogram: diamond prices" :x "price, USD"}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})






32.7.3 Radar: the order of the axes
The same car in two axis orders: the polygon’s shape and area change with the order, though the values don’t.
Source: data-to-viz - Spider chart caveats. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (vec (for [vs [car-variables [:mpg :wt :hp :drat :qsec :disp]]]
         {:data (filter #(= "Mazda RX4" (:model %)) mtcars) :coord {:kind :polar}
          :charts [(chart/parallel {:variables vs :fill :color :line-width 2 :limits car-limits})]
          :labels {:title (str "Mazda RX4: " (str/join " " (map name vs))) :x nil}}))
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 500})






32.7.4 Circular bars exaggerate the outer ones
Around a circle an outer bar is longer than an inner bar of the same value, and the angle of each bar hides its length: the straight bars compare honestly.
Source: data-to-viz - Circular barplot y axis. Data: Weapon exports by country, data-to-viz example dataset 7_OneCatOneNum (Yan Holtz); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data top-10 :mapping {:x :country :y :value} :scales {:x {:order-by level-value}}
    :coord {:kind :polar :inner 0.2}
    :charts [(chart/bar)] :labels {:title "Circular" :x nil :y nil}}
   {:data top-10 :mapping {:x :country :y :value} :scales {:x {:order-by level-value}}
    :theme {:axis {:x {:label-rotation -45}}}
    :charts [(chart/bar)] :labels {:title "Straight" :x nil :y "exports"}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 500})

title: 33  Part of a whole
text:
33.1 Grouped and stacked bars
How a whole splits into parts: grouped and stacked bars, treemaps, donuts and pies, circle packing, sunbursts, waffles, Venn diagrams and UpSet plots (the R Graph Gallery part-of-a-whole pages, the data-to-viz sunburst and the pie caveat).
Not here: dendrograms (plot/dendrogram) and the sunburst of flows belong to the Flow chapter.
Bars of groups within categories: side by side, on top of each other, scaled to the whole, or one panel per category.
