33.1.2 Likert scale
Survey answers as diverging stacked bars (seeded counts): disagreement to the left of 0, agreement to the right, the neutral answers split half to each side (two :groups of one colour). :negative-order :reverse stacks the negative side from the last answer, so the answers in their natural order diverge from the middle.

(def answers ["Strongly disagree" "Disagree" "Neutral" "Agree" "Strongly agree"])


(def likert
  (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 3)]
    (vec (for [q (range 1 6)
               [i answer] (map-indexed vector answers)
               :let [n (+ 5 (r/irandom rng 40))
                     sign ({0 -1.0 1 -1.0 3 1.0 4 1.0} i)]
               row (if sign
                     [{:question (str "Q" q) :answer answer :side "" :count (* sign n)}]
                     ;; the neutral answer: half on each side, two groups of one colour
                     [{:question (str "Q" q) :answer answer :side "-" :count (* -0.5 n)}
                      {:question (str "Q" q) :answer answer :side "+" :count (* 0.5 n)}])]
           row))))

title: 33  Part of a whole
text:
33.2 Treemap
Nested rectangles, areas proportional to the value: the world’s population by region, subregion and country.

33.2.1 Basic, groups and subgroups
One level (regions) and three (regions → subregions → countries); treemap :gap frames the groups, :stroke-color outlines the cells, a theme palette recolours the regions.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Treemap; data-to-viz - Treemap (1, 2). Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data world :mapping {:value :population :hierarchy [:region]} :charts [(chart/treemap)]
    :labels {:title "regions"}}
   {:data world :mapping {:value :population :hierarchy [:region :subregion :country]}
    :theme {:palette {:color :set2}}
    :charts [(chart/treemap {:gap 4 :stroke-color [60 60 60]})]
    :labels {:title "regions, subregions, countries (:set2, :gap 4)"}}]
  {:columns 2 :widths [1 2]})
 {:width 1000 :height 520})






33.2.2 Annotated treemap
Label functions (:leaf-labels, :group-labels) get the node’s name, value, depth and shares: the countries with their population in millions.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Treemap (annotations, labels and colors). Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 {:data world :mapping {:value :population :hierarchy [:region :country]}
  :charts [(chart/treemap {:leaf-labels #(format "%s\n%.0f M" (:name %) (/ (double (:value %)) 1e6))
                           :group-labels #(format "%s - %.1f%%" (:name %) (* 100.0 (double (:share %))))})]
  :labels {:title "World population (millions)"}}
 {:width 1000 :height 700})

title: 33  Part of a whole
text:
33.3 Donut
A ring of stacked shares: the regions’ populations around a hole (:inner - the hole’s radius as a fraction).

33.3.1 Basic, labels, ring thickness
Source: R Graph Gallery - Donut chart; data-to-viz - Donut (1, 2). Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (vec (for [inner [0.3 0.7]]
         (assoc pie-base
                :coord {:kind :polar :inner inner}
                :scales {:x {:axis false}}
                :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack :width 1.0 :value-label percent-label})]
                :labels {:title (str ":inner " inner) :x nil :y nil})))
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 450})






33.3.2 Half donut
:span 180 from :start -90: the circle shrinks to a half and fits its panel; outer labels name the parts.
Source: data-to-viz - Donut (variations). Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (assoc pie-base
        :coord {:kind :polar :inner 0.5 :span 180 :start -90}
        :legend false
        :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack :width 1.0 :value-label share-label :label-position :outer})]
        :labels {:title "World population by region" :x nil :y nil})
 {:width 800 :height 420})

title: 33  Part of a whole
text:
33.4 Pie
A donut without its hole. data-to-viz: angles are hard to compare - see the caveat at the end.

33.4.1 Basic, colours, a clean pie
The default pie shows its value axis around the circle - the cumulative population, here in billions; a palette recolours it; :axis false cleans it up.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Pie chart. Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [(assoc pie-base :legend false :scales {:x {:formatter #(format "%.0fB" (/ (double %) 1e9))}}
          :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack :width 1.0})] :labels {:title "default (axis in billions)" :x nil :y nil})
   (assoc pie-base :theme {:palette {:color :MetBrewer/Archambault}} :legend false
          :scales {:x {:formatter #(format "%.0fB" (/ (double %) 1e9))}}
          :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack :width 1.0})] :labels {:title ":MetBrewer/Archambault" :x nil :y nil})
   (assoc pie-base :scales {:x {:axis false}} :legend false
          :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack :width 1.0 :stroke-color :white :stroke-width 1})]
          :labels {:title "clean" :x nil :y nil})]
  {:columns 3})
 {:width 1000 :height 380})






33.4.2 Slice labels
Label functions get each slice’s value, count and share: shares inside the slices, or names and shares outside with leader lines (:label-position :outer - the angle axis gives way, the circle makes room).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Pie chart (labels). Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [(assoc pie-base :scales {:x {:axis false}}
          :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack :width 1.0 :value-label percent-label})]
          :labels {:title "inside" :x nil :y nil})
   (assoc pie-base :legend false
          :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack :width 1.0 :value-label share-label :label-position :outer
                               :label-leader true})]
          :labels {:title "outside, with leaders" :x nil :y nil})]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 480})

title: 33  Part of a whole
text:
33.5 Circle packing
Circles with areas proportional to the value, nested in their groups’ enclosing circles - a group’s area isn’t proportional to its value (packing leaves gaps), compare circles within a group.

33.5.1 One level
Europe’s countries: a circle each (the palette’s colours repeat - they only tell neighbours apart); leaves coloured by their subregion; wider gaps (pack :gap, pixels; :leaf-labels false hides the names).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Circular packing; data-to-viz - Circular packing (1, 2). Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data europe :mapping {:value :population :hierarchy [:country]} :legend false
    :charts [(chart/pack)] :labels {:title "basic"}}
   {:data europe :mapping {:value :population :hierarchy [:country] :color :subregion}
    :charts [(chart/pack {:gap 6 :leaf-labels false})] :labels {:title "by subregion, :gap 6"}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 480})






33.5.2 Several levels
Regions → subregions → countries: the regions’ colours lighter at every level, group names under their circles’ tops.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Circular packing (several levels). Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 {:data world :mapping {:value :population :hierarchy [:region :subregion :country]}
  :charts [(chart/pack)] :labels {:title "Regions, subregions, countries"}}
 {:width 1000 :height 800})




Hiding the regions (:hidden-levels #{1}) leaves the subregions floating - the layout stays the same.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Circular packing (hide some levels). Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 {:data world :mapping {:value :population :hierarchy [:region :subregion :country]}
  :charts [(chart/pack {:hidden-levels #{1}})] :labels {:title "Regions hidden"}}
 {:width 1000 :height 800})

title: 33  Part of a whole
text:
33.6 Sunburst
The hierarchy as rings: a partition (an icicle in cartesian coordinates) under polar coordinates - regions inside, subregions, then countries outward.
Source: data-to-viz - Sunburst. Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data world :mapping {:value :population :hierarchy [:region :subregion :country]} :coord {:kind :polar :inner 0.15}
    :charts [(chart/partition)] :labels {:title "sunburst"}}
   {:data world :mapping {:value :population :hierarchy [:region :subregion]}
    :charts [(chart/partition)] :labels {:title "icicle (two levels)"}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 520})

title: 33  Part of a whole
text:
33.7 Waffle
A grid of cells: by default 10 × 10, a cell per percent of the whole (largest-remainder rounding keeps the total at 100).

33.7.1 Basic, shapes, colours, groups
The regions’ shares; circle cells (waffle :cell-shape, :gap - a fraction of a cell); a palette; subregions within each region (a facet per region, each region’s subregions in shades of one colour - 22 subregions are more than a palette’s 20 colours).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Waffle chart. Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data world :mapping {:color :region :value :population} :charts [(chart/waffle)] :labels {:title "regions"}}
   {:data world :mapping {:color :region :value :population} :theme {:palette {:color :dark2}}
    :charts [(chart/waffle {:cell-shape :circle :gap 0.15})] :labels {:title "circles, :dark2"}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})




Source: R Graph Gallery - Waffle chart (groups and subgroups). Data: World population by region, subregion and country, data-to-viz example dataset 11_SevCatOneNumNestedOneObsPerGroup (Yan Holtz; Wikipedia); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(def subregion-colors
  "Each region's subregions in shades of the region's colour (darker to lighter)."
  (into {} (for [[base [_ subregions]] (map vector (plot/palette :category10)
                                             (sort-by key (group-by :region world)))
                 :let [names (sort (distinct (map :subregion subregions)))]
                 [i subregion] (map-indexed vector names)]
             [subregion (c/brighten base (- (* 0.7 (double i)) 1.0))])))


(plot/render-image
 {:data world :mapping {:color :subregion :value :population :facet :region}
  :scales {:color {:range subregion-colors}}
  :charts [(chart/waffle {:gap 0.15})]
  :labels {:title "Subregions within each region"}}
 {:width 1000 :height 520})

title: 33  Part of a whole
33  Part of a whole
text:
33.9 Caveats

33.9.1 The issue with pie charts
data-to-viz: three sets of five nearly equal values. As pies the differences hide in the angles; as bars they read at once. (3D pies, exploded slices and legends far from the slices make it worse - not drawn here.)

(def caveat-data
  {"data 1" [17 18 20 22 24] "data 2" [20 18 21 20 20] "data 3" [24 23 21 19 18]})

(defn- caveat-rows [values] (mapv (fn [part v] {:part part :value v}) ["a" "b" "c" "d" "e"] values))


#'use-cases.part-of-a-whole/caveat-rows

Source: data-to-viz - The issue with pie chart.

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (vec (concat
        (for [[title values] caveat-data]
          {:data (caveat-rows values) :mapping {:x :value :color :part} :coord {:kind :polar} :scales {:x {:axis false}}
           :legend false :charts [(chart/bar {:position :stack :width 1.0})] :labels {:title title :x nil :y nil}})
        (for [[title values] caveat-data]
          {:data (caveat-rows values) :mapping {:x :part :y :value :color :part} :legend false
           :charts [(chart/bar)] :labels {:title title :x nil :y nil}})))
  {:columns 3})
 {:width 1000 :height 650})






33.9.2 Other caveats

Circle packing: only leaf areas follow the values - a group’s circle also holds the gaps between its children.
Treemaps: label at most three levels; deeper ones get too small to read (data-to-viz).
Sunbursts and donuts compare angles, as pies do; outer rings exaggerate the deeper levels (their arcs are longer for the same share).

title: 34  Evolution
text:
34.1 Lines
Values over time and other ordered variables: lines, time axes, smoothing and uncertainty, many lines, areas and marks for evolution (the R Graph Gallery evolution pages and the data-to-viz caveats).
Dates are java.time values: a datetime scale places LocalDate, LocalDateTime, Instant and the other temporal types; curves and fits work in epoch milliseconds.
A line joins points in x order; dates on x give a datetime axis.

title: 34  Evolution
text:
34.1.1 Basic line with dates
Source: R Graph Gallery - Line chart with ggplot2; Time series (1, 2). Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 {:data economics
  :mapping {:x :date :y :unemploy}
  :charts [(chart/line)]
  :labels {:title "Unemployed persons in the US" :x nil :y "thousands"}}
 {:width 800 :height 400})






34.1.2 Line styling
Width, colour and points are chart options; :dash mapped to a variable takes the named dash styles in order (:solid, :dashed, :dotted, …), so lines read apart without colour.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Line chart with ggplot2 (customization). Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(let [recent (filter #(.isAfter ^LocalDate (:date %) (LocalDate/of 2010 1 1)) economics)
      recent-long (filter #(and (.isAfter ^LocalDate (:date %) (LocalDate/of 2010 1 1))
                                (#{"psavert" "uempmed" "unemploy"} (:variable %)))
                          economics-long)]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange
    [{:data recent :mapping {:x :date :y :psavert}
      :charts [(chart/line {:line-width 2 :color [215 48 39]}) (chart/scatter {:size 5 :color [215 48 39]})]
      :labels {:title "width, colour, points" :x nil :y "savings rate, %"}}
     {:data recent-long :mapping {:x :date :y :value01 :dash :variable}
      :charts [(chart/line {:line-width 1.5 :color :black})]
      :labels {:title ":dash by variable" :x nil :y "rescaled"}}]
    {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 400}))






34.1.3 Log scale
Growth at a steady rate is a straight line on a log axis; :pow, :symlog and :radial (square-root like) are the other continuous transforms (scale kinds).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Line plot with log scale. Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data economics :mapping {:x :date :y :pce} :charts [(chart/line)]
    :labels {:title "linear" :x nil :y "consumption, billions USD"}}
   {:data economics :mapping {:x :date :y :pce} :scales {:y {:kind :log}} :charts [(chart/line)]
    :labels {:title ":log" :x nil :y "consumption, billions USD"}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})






34.1.4 Several groups
One line per level of :color; values on different units are rescaled to 0..1 to share an axis.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Line chart with several groups. Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 {:data economics-long
  :mapping {:x :date :y :value01 :color :variable}
  :charts [(chart/line)]
  :labels {:title "Five economic series, rescaled" :x nil :y "value (0..1)"}}
 {:width 900 :height 450})






34.1.5 Steps and interpolated lines
:interpolator takes any fastmath one-dimensional method: steps, monotone (no overshoot) or cubic curves through the points.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Line plot; data-to-viz - Line plot (1, 2). Data: Monthly airline passengers, 1949-1960, R datasets package AirPassengers (Box & Jenkins 1976); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [year (filter #(= 1955 (:year %)) air)
      panel (fn [title opts] {:data year :mapping {:x :date :y :passengers}
                              :charts [(chart/line opts) (chart/scatter {:size 5})]
                              :labels {:title title :x nil :y "passengers, thousands"}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(panel ":step-after" {:interpolator :step-after})
                  (panel ":monotone" {:interpolator :monotone})
                  (panel ":cubic" {:interpolator :cubic})]
                 {:columns 3})
   {:width 1000 :height 350}))






34.1.6 Sampling step
An interpolated line is evaluated every :sample-step pixels (default 1) or at {:count n} positions per run - a coarse count shows the polyline behind a curve.
Data: Monthly airline passengers, 1949-1960, R datasets package AirPassengers (Box & Jenkins 1976); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [years (filter #(<= 1958 (:year %)) air)
      panel (fn [title step] {:data years :mapping {:x :date :y :passengers}
                              :charts [(chart/line {:interpolator :cubic :sample-step step}) (chart/scatter {:size 4})]
                              :labels {:title title :x nil :y "passengers, thousands"}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(panel "every pixel (default)" 1) (panel "{:count 12} per run" {:count 12})] {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 380}))






34.1.7 Missing values
A missing (nil) value breaks the line (:gaps :break, default); :gaps :bridge joins the ends with a dimmed segment, so the gap stays visible.
Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(let [gappy (map (fn [row] (if (<= 1990 (.getYear ^LocalDate (:date row)) 1992) (assoc row :psavert nil) row))
                 (filter #(<= 1985 (.getYear ^LocalDate (:date %)) 1997) economics))
      panel (fn [title gaps] {:data gappy :mapping {:x :date :y :psavert}
                              :charts [(chart/line {:gaps gaps :line-width 1.5})]
                              :labels {:title title :x nil :y "savings rate, %"}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(panel ":gaps :break" :break) (panel ":gaps :bridge" :bridge)] {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 380}))

title: 34  Evolution
text:
34.2 Time axes
Datetime ticks fall on calendar units; the formatter is a function or a java.time pattern string.

34.2.1 Date format and breaks
Source: R Graph Gallery - Time series with ggplot2; Manage dates (1, 2). Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data economics :mapping {:x :date :y :uempmed}
    :scales {:x {:ticks-params {:unit :years :step 5} :formatter "yyyy"}}
    :charts [(chart/line)] :labels {:title "every 5 years, \"yyyy\"" :x nil :y "weeks"}}
   {:data (filter #(= 2008 (.getYear ^LocalDate (:date %))) economics) :mapping {:x :date :y :uempmed}
    :scales {:x {:ticks-params {:unit :months :step 2} :formatter "MMM"}}
    :charts [(chart/line) (chart/scatter {:size 5})] :labels {:title "2008, every 2 months, \"MMM\"" :x nil :y "weeks"}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})






34.2.2 Time window
An explicit :domain of dates shows one window of a long series; the data outside is clipped by the panel.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Time series with ggplot2 (select a time frame). Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 {:data economics
  :mapping {:x :date :y :unemploy}
  :scales {:x {:domain [(LocalDate/of 2000 1 1) (LocalDate/of 2010 1 1)]} :y {:domain [4000 16000]}}
  :charts [(chart/line {:line-width 1.5})]
  :labels {:title "Unemployment, 2000-2010" :x nil :y "thousands"}}
 {:width 800 :height 400})






34.2.3 Annotations
Literal rects, rules and texts take dates as positions: recessions shaded behind the line, a rule and a label.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Line chart annotation. Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(let [d (fn [y mo] (LocalDate/of (int y) (int mo) 1))
      recessions [[(d 1969 12) (d 1970 11)] [(d 1973 11) (d 1975 3)] [(d 1980 1) (d 1980 7)] [(d 1981 7) (d 1982 11)]
                  [(d 1990 7) (d 1991 3)] [(d 2001 3) (d 2001 11)] [(d 2007 12) (d 2009 6)]]]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data economics
    :mapping {:x :date :y :unemploy}
    :charts [(chart/rect {:x recessions :fill [0 0 0 35]})
             (chart/line {:line-width 1.5})
             (chart/rule {:x (d 2008 9) :dash :dashed :color [215 48 39]})
             (chart/text {:x (d 2008 9) :y 14500 :text "Lehman Brothers" :anchor [:right :middle] :offset [-5 0]
                          :color [215 48 39]})]
    :labels {:title "Unemployment and US recessions (NBER)" :x nil :y "thousands"}}
   {:width 900 :height 450}))






34.2.4 Time heatmap
Year × month as two categorical axes, the value as a linear colour: seasonality and growth at once - a tile per month (categories in data order: January to December, the years upward).
Source: R Graph Gallery - The hourly heatmap. Data: Monthly airline passengers, 1949-1960, R datasets package AirPassengers (Box & Jenkins 1976); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data air
  :mapping {:x :month :y #(str (:year %)) :color :passengers}
  :scales {:color {:range :viridis/viridis :title "passengers"}}
  :charts [(chart/tile {:stroke-color :white})]
  :labels {:title "Airline passengers by month (thousands)" :x nil :y nil}}
 {:width 800 :height 500})

title: 34  Evolution
text:
34.3 Smoothing and uncertainty
chart/smooth fits a curve per group with a band; chart/ribbon draws any band given as :ymin / :ymax.

34.3.1 Smoothers with confidence bands
Loess (default) with nested 50% / 95% bands; a linear model per diet; a Gaussian process (mean ± z·σ). The loess defaults are ggplot2’s geom_smooth ones - 75% of the points, local quadratic fits - with fastmath’s two robustness iterations (:method-params {:iters 0} is ggplot2’s plain fit; the robust bands are a little wider). The bands of the plain fit (:iters 0) equal R’s predict(se = TRUE); with 144 or 220 points they are narrow. On a date axis the fit works in epoch milliseconds - a kernel’s scale too (here three months).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Scatterplot with ggplot2 (smoothing); Polynomial curve fitting (1, 2). Data: Monthly airline passengers, 1949-1960, R datasets package AirPassengers (Box & Jenkins 1976); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [year-ms (* 365.25 86400000.0)]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange
    [{:data air :mapping {:x :date :y :passengers}
      :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 3}) (chart/smooth {:level [0.5 0.95]})]
      :labels {:title "loess, 50% / 95%" :x nil :y "passengers"}}
     {:data chicks :mapping {:x :time :y :weight :color :diet}
      :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 3}) (chart/smooth {:method :lm})]
      :labels {:title "lm per diet" :x "days" :y "weight, g"}}
     {:data (filter #(<= 1956 (:year %)) air) :mapping {:x :date :y :passengers}
      :charts [(chart/smooth {:method :gp :level [0.5 0.95]
                              :method-params {:kernel (kernel/kernel :gaussian {:sigma (* 0.25 year-ms)})
                                              :noise 0.05 :normalize? true}})
               (chart/scatter {:size 4})]
      :labels {:title "Gaussian process" :x nil :y "passengers"}}]
    {:columns 3})
   {:width 1000 :height 380}))






34.3.2 Ribbon
Daily minimum and maximum temperatures as a band, the mean as a line.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Lines with error envelopes. Data: Weather in Lincoln, Nebraska, 2016, R ggridges package lincoln_weather (Weather Underground, via Wilke); licence: GPL-2 (ggridges).

(plot/render-image
 {:data lincoln
  :mapping {:x :date}
  :scales {:x {:formatter "MMM"}}
  :charts [(chart/ribbon {:mapping {:ymin :min-temp :ymax :max-temp} :color [215 48 39]})
           (chart/line {:mapping {:y :mean-temp} :color [150 30 20]})]
  :labels {:title "Lincoln, Nebraska, 2016: daily min-max and mean" :x nil :y "temperature, F"}}
 {:width 900 :height 420})

title: 34  Evolution
text:
34.4 Many lines
Fifty chicks are a spaghetti plot; highlighting, small multiples and labels make it readable.

34.4.1 Highlighting one line
All lines in grey (:group, no colour), then the one of interest from its own :data in colour.
Source: data-to-viz - Spaghetti plot; R Graph Gallery - Highlight elements in a line chart (1, 2). Data: Weight versus age of chicks on four diets, R datasets package ChickWeight (Crowder & Hand 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data chicks
  :mapping {:x :time :y :weight}
  :charts [(chart/line {:mapping {:group :chick} :color [190 190 190]})
           (chart/line {:data (filter #(= "21" (:chick %)) chicks) :line-width 2.5 :color [215 48 39]})
           (chart/text {:data (filter #(= "21" (:chick %)) chicks) :mapping {:x :time :y :weight :label :chick}
                        :select :last :color [215 48 39]})]
  :labels {:title "Chick 21 among all fifty" :x "days" :y "weight, g"}}
 {:width 800 :height 450})






34.4.2 Small multiples with the others greyed
A chart whose mapping sets the facet key to nil is drawn in every panel: all chicks in grey behind each diet’s own.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Small multiple line chart, all groups greyed out. Data: Weight versus age of chicks on four diets, R datasets package ChickWeight (Crowder & Hand 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data chicks
  :mapping {:x :time :y :weight :group :chick :facet :diet}
  :charts [(chart/line {:mapping {:facet nil} :color [175 175 175]})
           (chart/line {:color [33 102 172]})]
  :labels {:title "Chicks per diet, all chicks in grey" :x "days" :y "weight, g"}}
 {:width 900 :height 600})






34.4.3 Labels at line ends
chart/text with :select :last keeps one label per series at its last point and makes room for it.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Line chart with labels at end of lines. Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(let [recent (filter #(and (.isAfter ^LocalDate (:date %) (LocalDate/of 2005 1 1))
                            (#{"pce" "psavert" "unemploy"} (:variable %)))
                      economics-long)]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data recent
    :mapping {:x :date :y :value01 :color :variable}
    :charts [(chart/line {:line-width 1.5})
             (chart/text {:mapping {:x :date :y :value01 :label :variable :color :variable} :select :last})]
    :legend false
    :labels {:title "Three economic series since 2005, labelled at the end" :x nil :y "value (0..1)"}}
   {:width 900 :height 450}))






34.4.4 Bump chart
Ranks instead of values: levels/rank-rows ranks the chicks at every weighing (1 - the heaviest; ties by data order with :ties :first), a monotone line joins the ranks on a reversed axis.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Basic bump plot. Data: Weight versus age of chicks on four diets, R datasets package ChickWeight (Crowder & Hand 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [eight (set (map str (range 1 9)))
      ranked (levels/rank-rows (filter #(and (eight (:chick %)) (zero? (mod (:time %) 4))) chicks) :time :weight
                              {:ties :first})]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data ranked
    :mapping {:x :time :y :rank :color :chick}
    :scales {:y {:domain [8.5 0.5] :nice false :ticks (vec (range 1 9))}}
    :charts [(chart/line {:interpolator :monotone :line-width 3})
             (chart/scatter {:size 9})
             (chart/text {:mapping {:x :time :y :rank :label :chick :color :chick} :select :last})]
    :legend false
    :labels {:title "Weight rank of chicks 1-8 on diet 1" :x "days" :y "rank"}}
   {:width 800 :height 450}))

title: 34  Evolution
text:
34.5 Areas
An area fills between a line and zero, or between stacked lines.

34.5.1 Area chart
Source: R Graph Gallery - Area chart with ggplot2; data-to-viz - Area chart (1, 2). Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 {:data economics
  :mapping {:x :date :y :psavert}
  :charts [(chart/line {:fill :color :alpha 0.4 :line-width 1.5})]
  :labels {:title "Personal savings rate" :x nil :y "%"}}
 {:width 800 :height 400})






34.5.2 Gradient area
:fill-gradient colours the area along the y (or x) scale’s range.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Area chart with gradient. Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(plot/render-image
 {:data economics
  :mapping {:x :date :y :psavert}
  :charts [(chart/line {:fill-gradient [[255 255 255 0] [33 102 172 200]] :fill-gradient-axis :y :line-width 1.5
                        :color [33 102 172]})]
  :labels {:title "Savings rate, gradient along y" :x nil :y "%"}}
 {:width 800 :height 400})





(def diet-means

  (vec (for [[[diet day] rows] (sort-by key (group-by (juxt :diet :time) chicks))]
         {:diet diet :time day :weight (stats/mean (map :weight rows))})))

34.5.3 Stacked area
:position :stack aligns the groups on the union of their x values and stacks them; every band is filled.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Stacked area chart; data-to-viz - Stacked area (1, 2). Data: Weight versus age of chicks on four diets, R datasets package ChickWeight (Crowder & Hand 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data diet-means
  :mapping {:x :time :y :weight :color :diet}
  :charts [(chart/line {:position :stack})]
  :labels {:title "Mean chick weight per diet, stacked" :x "days" :y "weight, g"}}
 {:width 800 :height 420})






34.5.4 Percent stacked area
Source: R Graph Gallery - Stacked area chart (proportion). Data: Weight versus age of chicks on four diets, R datasets package ChickWeight (Crowder & Hand 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data diet-means
  :mapping {:x :time :y :weight :color :diet}
  :charts [(chart/line {:position :normalize})]
  :labels {:title "Share of each diet in the summed mean weight" :x "days"}}
 {:width 800 :height 420})






34.5.5 Stacking order
Groups stack in the colour scale’s order: an explicit :domain reorders the bands (and the legend).
Source: data-to-viz - Stacking caveat; R Graph Gallery - Reorder a variable (1, 2). Data: Weight versus age of chicks on four diets, R datasets package ChickWeight (Crowder & Hand 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

title: 34  Evolution
text:
34.6 Other marks
Segments, candlesticks, colour along a line and paths through time.

34.6.1 Lollipop
A segment from zero to each value ((chart/segment {:yend 0})) under a point, on any x: car models (flipped for readable labels, ordered by the band scale’s :order-by - each model’s mpg) or dates.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Basic lollipop plot; data-to-viz - Lollipop (1, 2). Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:data mtcars
    :mapping {:x :model :y :mpg}
    :scales {:x {:order-by #(:mpg (first %))}}
    :flip true
    :charts [(chart/segment {:yend 0 :color [150 150 150]}) (chart/scatter {:size 7 :color [33 102 172]})]
    :labels {:title "Fuel economy of 32 cars" :x nil :y "miles per gallon"}}
   {:data (filter #(= 1959 (:year %)) air)
    :mapping {:x :date :y :passengers}
    :charts [(chart/segment {:yend 0 :color [150 150 150]}) (chart/scatter {:size 7 :color [33 102 172]})]
    :labels {:title "Passengers in 1959" :x nil :y "thousands"}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 700})






34.6.2 Candlestick
Open-high-low-close per day: the wick from low to high, the body from open to close, green up and red down; OHLC bars as the alternative. The prices are a seeded random walk.
Source: Wikipedia - Candlestick chart.

(def prices
  "Daily open / high / low / close of a random walk over 40 trading days."
  (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 21)
        start (LocalDate/of 2024 3 1)]
    (vec (map-indexed (fn [i close]
                        (let [open (+ close (* 1.2 (r/grandom rng)))
                              spread (m/abs (* 0.8 (double (r/grandom rng))))]
                          {:date (.plusDays start i) :open open :close close
                           :high (+ (max open close) spread) :low (- (min open close) spread)}))
                      (take 40 (reductions + 50.0 (repeatedly #(r/grandom rng))))))))

title: 34  Evolution
text:
34.7 Functions
chart/function samples functions across the panel. Several functions - a vector, [label f] pairs or a map - are one group each: {:mapping {:color :function}} colours them and gives the legend, labels in the given order. :y-limits keeps asymptotes from flattening the curve: samples outside the limits don’t count for the y extent; a jump between opposite panel edges cuts the curve.

34.7.1 Many functions with a legend

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  [{:charts [(chart/function {:f (mapv (fn [k] [(str "sin " k "x") (fn [x] (m/sin (* k (double x))))]) (range 1 11))
                              :domain [0 m/PI] :mapping {:color :function}})]
    :scales {:color {:title nil}}
    :labels {:title "ten [label f] pairs" :x "x" :y "y"}}
   {:charts [(chart/function {:f m/tan :domain [(- m/PI) m/PI] :y-limits [-5 5]})]
    :labels {:title "tan with :y-limits [-5 5]" :x "x" :y "y"}}]
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 400})






34.7.2 Parametric curves
:parametric - (fn [t] [x y]) over :t [lo hi], sampled by count; Lissajous figures on an isometric aspect.
Source: Wikipedia - Lissajous curve.

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (vec (for [[a b] [[1 2] [3 2] [3 4] [5 4]]]
         {:aspect :iso
          :charts [(chart/function {:parametric (fn [t] [(m/sin (* a (double t))) (m/sin (* b (double t)))])
                                    :t [0 m/TWO_PI] :sample-step {:count 1000}})]
          :labels {:title (str "a = " a ", b = " b) :x nil :y nil}}))
  {:columns 4})
 {:width 1000 :height 300})

title: 34  Evolution
text:
34.8 Caveats

34.8.1 Cutting the y axis; aspect ratio
Starting y at zero shows changes against the whole; a cut axis magnifies them. A wide panel flattens slopes, a narrow one steepens them - the same data.
Source: data-to-viz - Cut y axis; Aspect ratio (1, 2). Data: US economic time series, 1967-2015, R ggplot2 package economics (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(let [recent (filter #(.isAfter ^LocalDate (:date %) (LocalDate/of 2012 1 1)) economics)
      plot-of (fn [title y] {:data recent :mapping {:x :date :y :pop} :scales {:y y}
                             :charts [(chart/line {:line-width 1.5})] :labels {:title title :x nil :y "population, thousands"}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(plot/arrange [(plot-of "y from 0" {:domain [0 330000]}) (plot-of "y cut" {})] {:columns 2})
                  (plot/arrange [(plot-of "wide" {}) (plot-of "narrow" {})] {:columns 2 :widths [4 1]})]
                 {:columns 1})
   {:width 1000 :height 700}))

title: 35  Flow
text:
35.1 Chord diagram
Connections and flows between entities: chord diagrams, networks, sankey and alluvial diagrams, bump charts, arc diagrams, hierarchical edge bundling, dendrograms, clustered heatmaps, circular plots and flow sunbursts (the R Graph Gallery flow pages and data-to-viz). Every layout is a function returning rows, drawn by ordinary charts; the plot/... builders return plain plot maps.
Not here: interactivity, multi-track circular plots, gradient ribbons and links, cyclic sankeys, crossing minimization beyond clustering, arcs below the line and label repel.
Flows between groups around a circle: a ring sector per group, sized by its flow, and a ribbon per link.

title: 35  Flow
text:
35.1.1 Chord diagram from an edge list
Migration between ten world regions: directed - a ribbon per flow, as wide as the flow at both ends, the sectors holding the flows out and in - and undirected, a ribbon per pair of regions, as wide as their exchange.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Chord diagram; data-to-viz - Chord diagram (1, 2). Data: Migration flows between world regions, data-to-viz example dataset 13_AdjacencyDirectedWeighted (long form; Yan Holtz, after Abel & Sander 2014); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange [(plot/chord migration {:directed true :min-value 0.1 :title "directed flows"})
                (plot/chord migration {:min-value 0.1 :title "exchange between regions"})]
               {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 520})






35.1.2 Colours, gaps, order and weak links
:min-value drops the weak flows that clutter the middle, :gap-angle widens the gaps, :order :cluster puts regions with similar partners side by side, and the palette is a plot scale like any other.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Advanced chord diagram with circlize; data-to-viz - Chord diagram (1, 2). Data: Migration flows between world regions, data-to-viz example dataset 13_AdjacencyDirectedWeighted (long form; Yan Holtz, after Abel & Sander 2014); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/chord migration {:directed true :min-value 0.5 :gap-angle 4 :order :cluster
                        :scales {:color {:range :category10}}
                        :title "Flows of at least 0.5 million, clustered order"})
 {:width 700 :height 700})

title: 35  Flow
text:
35.2 Network
Nodes and the edges between them, placed by a layout; colour, size and width carry node and edge variables.

35.2.1 From an adjacency table
Co-authorships between researchers come as a table - a row per author, a column per author, 1 for a joint paper. The table isn’t square, so its cells become edge rows directly (graph/adjacency->edges reads square matrices, see the correlation network below); the force layout places them, seeded for a stable picture. Groups of authors without joint papers between them are laid out apart and packed in rows, the largest first.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Input formats for network charts; data-to-viz - Network (1, 2). Data: Co-authorships between researchers, data-to-viz example dataset 13_AdjacencyUndirectedUnweighted (Yan Holtz); licence: MIT (data_to_viz repository).

(def coauthor-edges
  "One edge per co-author pair (the table lists some pairs both ways)."
  (->> (nu/dataset :coauthors)
       (mapcat (fn [{:keys [from] :as row}]
                 (for [[k v] (dissoc row :from) :when (= 1 v)] (vec (sort [from (name k)])))))
       (remove (fn [[a b]] (= a b)))
       (distinct)
       (mapv (fn [[a b]] {:from a :to b}))))

Nodes coloured by their group and sized by their number of links (:degree, computed with the graph); labels for the main characters. One size scale serves one variable, so edge widths (below, for migration flows) and node sizes don’t go together.

                               :mapping {:color :group :size :degree}

35.2.4 Correlation network
Variables linked when their correlation is strong (|r| > 0.7): the matrix becomes edges with graph/adjacency->edges, the weight is |r| and the colour its sign.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Correlation network with igraph. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(def correlation-edges
  (let [names (mapv name mtcars-variables)
        r (stats/correlation-matrix (mapv (fn [k] (mapv k mtcars)) mtcars-variables))
        strong (mapv (fn [row] (mapv #(if (> (m/abs (double %)) 0.7) % 0) row)) r)]
    (mapv #(assoc % :r (:value %) :value (m/abs (double (:value %))))
          (graph/adjacency->edges strong names {:whole-matrix false}))))

title: 35  Flow
text:
35.9 Flow sunburst
Sequences of steps (website visits, here 2000 synthetic sessions) as rings from the centre: every step coloured by its page wherever it occurs, end where a session stops.
Source: data-to-viz - Sunburst.

(def pages ["home" "search" "product" "account" "cart" "help"])


(def visits
  "2000 sessions starting at home: each step to another page or the end (more likely the longer the session), at
  most 6 pages; a seeded random walk."
  (let [g (r/rng :mersenne 7)
        weights {"home" [0 5 3 2 0 1] "search" [1 2 6 0 1 1] "product" [1 2 2 1 4 1]
                 "account" [2 0 1 1 1 2] "cart" [0 0 2 2 0 1] "help" [2 2 0 2 0 1]}
        pick (fn [ws] (let [total (double (reduce + ws)) u (* total (r/drandom g))]
                        (loop [i 0 acc 0.0]
                          (let [acc (+ acc (double (ws i)))]
                            (if (or (< u acc) (= i (dec (count ws)))) i (recur (inc i) acc))))))]
    (vec (for [_ (range 2000)]
           {:sequence (str/join "-" (loop [path ["home"]]
                                      (if (or (= 6 (count path)) (< (r/drandom g) (* 0.12 (count path))))
                                        (conj path "end")
                                        (recur (conj path (pages (pick (weights (peek path)))))))))}))))

title: 35  Flow
text:
35.10 Caveats

A network of many nodes and links becomes a hairball: filter weak links, or show the graph as an arc diagram or an adjacency heatmap instead.
Order changes the reading of chord and arc diagrams: :order :cluster puts nodes with the same partners together; input order may scatter them.
Weak links clutter chord and sankey diagrams; :min-value leaves them out (and the layout says how many).
Sankey diagrams show flows that go one way: a flow back to an earlier node is a cycle the layout refuses.
Widths and areas encode values: a band twice as wide is twice the flow, a sector twice as long twice the total.

Source: data-to-viz - Caveats: spaghetti plot, order your data (1, 2).

source: notebooks/use_cases/flow.clj

title: 36  Colours
text:
36.1 Specifying colours
How cljplot2 picks colours: specifying a colour, palettes, discrete and continuous colour scales, colour in practice and accessibility (the R Graph Gallery colour pages and the data-to-viz colour caveats).
Colours come from clojure2d: any colour name, hex string or RGB(A) vector, about 7,300 named palettes and 5,000 gradients.
A colour is a clojure2d colour: a name keyword, a hex string, an RGB vector, or RGBA with alpha in 0-255.

title: 36  Colours
text:
36.1.1 Calling a colour
Literal rects take a vector of fills, one per interval; the labels are a text chart. :axis false on both scales leaves out axes and grid lines that would mean nothing here.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Dealing with color in base R; colour names (1, 2).

(let [colors [:steelblue :tomato "#2ca25f" "#fdae6b" [102 51 153] [255 0 0 90]]
      labels [":steelblue" ":tomato" "\"#2ca25f\"" "\"#fdae6b\"" "[102 51 153]" "[255 0 0 90]"]
      xs (mapv (fn [i] [i (+ i 0.9)]) (range (count colors)))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:scales {:x {:axis false} :y {:axis false}}
    :charts [(chart/rect {:x xs :y [0 1] :fill colors})
             (chart/text {:x (mapv #(+ % 0.45) (range (count colors))) :y -0.15 :text labels :size 11})]
    :labels {:title "Names, hex strings, RGB and RGBA vectors" :x nil :y nil}}
   {:width 900 :height 300}))

title: 36  Colours
text:
36.2 Palettes
Palettes are named lists of colours (plot/palette gives one, plot/find-palette lists the names); gradients are functions of t in [0 1] (plot/gradient, names from plot/find-gradient). A scale’s :range takes either name.

36.2.1 Palette types
Qualitative palettes for categories, sequential for ordered values, diverging around a meaningful middle (here the mean mpg, :midpoint). The lightest end of a sequential palette is almost white and nearly disappears against the grey panel - a property of the palette worth knowing when choosing one.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Dealing with color in ggplot2. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [mean-mpg (stats/mean (map :mpg mtcars))]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange
    [{:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width :color :species}
      :scales {:color {:range :RColorBrewer/Set2}}
      :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 7})] :labels {:title "qualitative" :x "sepal length" :y "sepal width"}}
     {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width :color :petal-length}
      :scales {:color {:range :blues-9}}
      :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 7})] :labels {:title "sequential" :x "sepal length" :y "sepal width"}}
     {:data mtcars :mapping {:x :wt :y :hp :color #(- (:mpg %) mean-mpg)}
      :scales {:color {:range :RColorBrewer/RdBu :midpoint 0 :title "mpg - mean"}}
      :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 8})] :labels {:title "diverging" :x "weight" :y "horse power"}}]
    {:columns 3})
   {:width 1000 :height 360}))






36.2.2 Palette families
The same scatter with a ColorBrewer, viridis, MetBrewer and Tableau palette; plot/find-palette lists palettes by name:
Source: R Graph Gallery - paletteer, viridis, RColorBrewer (1, 2, 3). Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/find-palette #"(?i)tableau")


(:tableau-10
 :tableau-10-2
 :tableau-10-light
 :tableau-10-medium
 :tableau-20
 :tableau-20-2
 :tableau-classic-20
 :tableau-classic-medium
 :ggthemes/Tableau_10
 :ggthemes/Tableau_20)


(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (for [[title palette] [["RColorBrewer Dark2" :RColorBrewer/Dark2] ["viridis" :viridis]
                         ["MetBrewer Klimt" :MetBrewer/Klimt] ["Tableau 10" :tableau-10]]]
    {:data iris :mapping {:x :petal-length :y :petal-width :color :species}
     :scales {:color {:range palette :spread (= palette :viridis)}}
     :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 7})]
     :labels {:title title :x "petal length" :y "petal width"}})
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 900 :height 650})




:viridis has 256 colours, so its scale uses :spread true - three colours across the whole palette instead of its first three.


36.2.3 Palette swatches
A palette shown as colours: rects with an identity colour scale (the data values are the colours). Every row is resampled to nine colours with (plot/palette p 9), which also samples a gradient (given as (plot/gradient name)).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Color palette finder.

(let [palettes [[":RColorBrewer/Set2" :RColorBrewer/Set2] [":tableau-10" :tableau-10]
                [":MetBrewer/Hiroshige" :MetBrewer/Hiroshige] [":blues-9" :blues-9] [":viridis" :viridis]
                ["gradient :viridis/magma" (plot/gradient :viridis/magma)] [":RColorBrewer/RdBu" :RColorBrewer/RdBu]]
      rows (for [[row [_ p]] (map-indexed vector palettes)
                 [i col] (map-indexed vector (plot/palette p 9))]
             {:x0 i :x1 (+ i 0.92) :y0 (- row) :y1 (- 0.85 row) :c col})
      names (for [[row [label]] (map-indexed vector palettes)] {:x -0.2 :y (- 0.42 row) :label label})]
  (plot/render-image
   {:scales {:color {:kind :identity} :x {:domain [-3.6 9] :axis false} :y {:axis false}}
    :charts [(chart/rect {:data rows :mapping {:x0 :x0 :x1 :x1 :y0 :y0 :y1 :y1 :color :c}})
             (chart/text {:data names :mapping {:x :x :y :y :label :label} :anchor [:right :middle] :size 11})]
    :labels {:title "Seven palettes and gradients, nine colours each" :x nil :y nil}}
   {:width 900 :height 500}))

title: 36  Colours
text:
36.3 Discrete colour scales
Categories take palette colours in level order, unless a scale says otherwise.

36.3.1 Manual colours
A level map as :range gives every level its own colour; a level without one is an error.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Dealing with color in ggplot2. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width :color :species}
  :scales {:color {:range {"setosa" :darkorange "versicolor" :purple "virginica" :teal}}}
  :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 8})]
  :labels {:title "Manual colours per species" :x "sepal length" :y "sepal width"}}
 {:width 800 :height 500})






36.3.2 Highlighting a group
One group in colour, the others grey. Cylinder counts are numbers, so the scale is declared categorical.
Source: data-to-viz - The spaghetti plot; don’t use color if it communicates nothing (1, 2). Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 {:data mtcars :mapping {:x :hp :y :mpg :color :cyl}
  :scales {:color {:type :categorical :range {4 :lightgrey 6 :firebrick 8 :lightgrey} :title "cylinders"}}
  :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 9})]
  :labels {:title "Six-cylinder cars" :x "horse power" :y "miles per gallon"}}
 {:width 800 :height 500})






36.3.3 Sequential palettes on categories
A sequential palette has more colours than there are levels: by default the levels take its first colours (all light here, the first nearly invisible on the grey panel); :spread true resamples it across its whole range.
Source: R Graph Gallery - RColorBrewer palettes. Data: Barley yields, Minnesota 1931-1932, R lattice package barley (Immer et al. 1934; Fisher 1971; Cleveland 1993); licence: GPL (>= 2) (lattice).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (for [spread [false true]]
    {:data barley :mapping {:x :yield :y :variety :color :site}
     :scales {:color {:range :blues-9 :spread spread}}
     :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 8})]
     :labels {:title (if spread ":spread true" "first colours (default)") :x "yield" :y nil}})
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 1000 :height 450})

title: 36  Colours
text:
36.4 Continuous colour scales
Numbers on :color get a gradient and a colour bar.

36.4.1 Gradients
:range takes two colours, several colours, a gradient name or any function of t in [0 1].
Source: R Graph Gallery - Dealing with color in ggplot2; viridis (1, 2). Data: Earthquakes off Fiji since 1964, R datasets package quakes (Harvard PRIM-H project); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (for [[title color-range] [["two colours" [:lightyellow :darkred]]
                             ["four colours" [:lightyellow :orange :red :darkred]]
                             ["gradient name :viridis/magma" :viridis/magma]
                             ["a function: lerp navy to gold" (fn [t] (c/lerp :navy :gold t))]]]
    {:data quakes :mapping {:x :long :y :lat :color :depth}
     :scales {:color {:range color-range}}
     :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 5})]
     :labels {:title title :x "longitude" :y "latitude"}})
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 900 :height 700})






36.4.2 Diverging gradient with a midpoint
:midpoint puts a value at the middle of the gradient and scales both sides by the larger distance to it; the colour bar ticks the midpoint. :reverse true turns RdBu around, so high horse power is red.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Dealing with color in ggplot2. Data: Motor Trend car road tests (1974), R datasets package mtcars (Henderson & Velleman 1981); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [mean-hp (stats/mean (map :hp mtcars))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data mtcars :mapping {:x :wt :y :mpg :color :hp}
    :scales {:color {:range :RColorBrewer/RdBu :midpoint mean-hp :reverse true}}
    :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 10})]
    :labels {:title (format "Horse power around its mean (%.1f)" mean-hp) :x "weight" :y "miles per gallon"}}
   {:width 800 :height 500}))






36.4.3 Reversing
:reverse true turns the colours around: categories keep their order with the colours reversed, a gradient runs the other way.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Dealing with color in ggplot2. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(plot/render-image
 (plot/arrange
  (for [[title color scale] [["categories" :species {:range :RColorBrewer/Set1}]
                             ["categories, reversed" :species {:range :RColorBrewer/Set1 :reverse true}]
                             ["gradient" :petal-length {:range :viridis/viridis}]
                             ["gradient, reversed" :petal-length {:range :viridis/viridis :reverse true}]]]
    {:data iris :mapping {:x :sepal-length :y :sepal-width :color color}
     :scales {:color scale}
     :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 7})]
     :labels {:title title :x "sepal length" :y "sepal width"}})
  {:columns 2})
 {:width 900 :height 650})






36.4.4 Binned colours
:kind :binned colours values by bin: a count of equal bins, a breaks vector, or quantile bins ({:quantiles 5}: five bins of about equal counts, an :estimation strategy optional); the colour bar has one block per bin. For a discrete legend of intervals, bin the data with levels/bin, which takes the same :bins.
Source: R Graph Gallery - Dealing with color in ggplot2. Data: Prices and attributes of round cut diamonds, R ggplot2 package diamonds (Wickham et al.); licence: MIT (ggplot2).

(def diamonds-sample
  "A fixed 5% sample of diamonds (the full data has 53,940 rows)."
  (let [rng (r/rng :mersenne 7)] (filterv (fn [_] (< (r/drandom rng) 0.05)) diamonds)))

36.5 Colour in practice

36.5.1 Missing values and the theme palette
A missing value gets the theme’s NA colour and the last legend entry; the theme :palette sets the default colours of every plot (here a MetBrewer palette and a magenta NA).
Source: R Graph Gallery - Dealing with color in ggplot2. Data: Edgar Anderson’s iris measurements, R datasets package iris (Anderson 1935; Fisher 1936); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(def iris-with-na
  "Iris with every seventh species missing."
  (map-indexed (fn [i row] (if (zero? (mod i 7)) (assoc row :species nil) row)) iris))

With 53,940 diamonds the opaque points hide where most of them are; a colour with a low alpha shows the density.

title: 36  Colours
37  cljplot extras
text:
37.1 Statistics
The examples of the original cljplot - its sketches and the showcase images of its README - rebuilt with cljplot2. Styling differs from the originals; the chart types and what they show are the same. Data are the originals’ where available (Old Faithful, Seattle weather), otherwise synthetic and seeded.
Not here: the image mosaics, the animation, and the lattice and Vega examples (their own galleries).

title: 37  cljplot extras
text:
37.1.1 Q-Q plot
Quantiles against quantiles: a sample against a distribution (:x-distribution), per group with a quartile line each; then two distributions against each other, no data at all, labelled for the legend.
Source: cljplot - qqplot.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 1)
      sample (vec (concat (for [_ (range 300)] {:v (r/grandom g) :group "normal"})
                          (for [_ (range 300)] {:v (r/sample (r/distribution :t {:degrees-of-freedom 3 :rng g})) :group "t(3)"})))]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [{:data sample :mapping {:y :v :color :group}
                   :charts [(chart/qq {:x-distribution [:normal]})]
                   :labels {:title "samples against the normal" :y "sample quantiles"}}
                  {:charts [(chart/qq {:x-distribution [:normal] :y-distribution [:t {:degrees-of-freedom 3}]
                                       :label "t(3)" :mapping {:color :label}})
                            (chart/qq {:x-distribution [:normal] :y-distribution [:t {:degrees-of-freedom 30}]
                                       :label "t(30)" :mapping {:color :label} :line false})]
                   :labels {:title "t distributions against the normal"}}]
                 {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 450}))




Two groups against each other: one column per group (the shorter padded with nils, which the chart drops), the longer one interpolated.
Source: cljplot - qqplot. Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [faithful (nu/dataset :faithful)
      short-wait (map :eruptions (filter #(< (double (:waiting %)) 70.0) faithful))

  (plot/render-image

37.1.2 P-P plot
Probabilities against probabilities: a t sample’s empirical CDF against the normal CDF, y = x for reference.
Source: cljplot - ppplot.

(let [d (r/distribution :t {:rng (r/rng :mersenne 2)})]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data (repeatedly 2000 (fn [] {:v (r/sample d)}))
    :mapping {:y :v}
    :charts [(chart/pp {:x-distribution [:normal] :size 2})]
    :labels {:title "P-P: a t sample against the normal" :y "sample probabilities"}}
   {:width 550 :height 500}))






37.1.3 Kernel densities
One sample, a density per fastmath KDE kernel; chart/function takes the map kernel -> density.
Source: cljplot - kernel densities.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 3)
      data (concat (repeatedly 500 #(r/grandom g 4.5 0.1))
                   (take 10000 (remove #(== (m/round (* (double %) 10.0)) 30.0)
                                       (repeatedly #(+ (r/grandom g 2.0 0.1) (* (r/drandom g) (r/drandom g 1.0 3.0)))))))
      kernels (:kde k/kernel-list)]
  (plot/render-image
   {:charts [(chart/function {:f (mapv (fn [kernel] [(name kernel) (k/kernel-density kernel data)]) kernels)
                              :domain [1.0 6.0] :line-width 1.5 :mapping {:color :function}})]
    :scales {:color {:title "kernel"}}
    :labels {:title "Kernel densities of one sample"}}
   {:width 800 :height 550}))






37.1.4 Gaussian process
A Gaussian process through ten noisy samples of a sine: the mean, 50 % and 95 % bands, the true function.
Source: cljplot - Gaussian process prediction.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 4)
      truth (fn [x] (+ 10.0 (m/sin (* -0.7 (double x)))))
      xs (repeatedly 10 #(r/drandom g -5 5))
      ys (map #(+ (truth %) (r/grandom g 0.0 0.0005)) xs)
      process (gp/gaussian-process xs ys {:normalize? true :kernel (k/kernel :gaussian {:sigma 0.8}) :noise 0.0005})
      xtest (m/slice-range -5.0 5.0 200)
      band (mapv (fn [x [mu sd]] {:x x :mu mu :lo95 (- mu (* 1.96 sd)) :hi95 (+ mu (* 1.96 sd))
                                  :lo50 (- mu (* 0.67 sd)) :hi50 (+ mu (* 0.67 sd))})
                 xtest (gp/predict-all process xtest true))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data band :mapping {:x :x}
    :charts [(chart/ribbon {:mapping {:ymin :lo95 :ymax :hi95} :color [130 170 230]})
             (chart/ribbon {:mapping {:ymin :lo50 :ymax :hi50} :color [70 120 200]})
             (chart/function {:f truth :color [215 48 39] :line-width 1.5})
             (chart/line {:mapping {:y :mu} :color :black :line-width 2})
             (chart/scatter {:data (map (fn [x y] {:x x :y y}) xs ys) :mapping {:y :y} :size 9 :color :black})]
    :labels {:title "Gaussian process: mean, 50 % and 95 % bands, the true function (red)" :y nil}}
   {:width 800 :height 500}))




A posterior sample through three points, with its 95 % band (the posterior standard deviation).
Source: cljplot - Gaussian process posterior sample.

(let [xs [-4 1 2] ys [-5 1 2]
      process (gp/gaussian-process xs ys {:kernel (k/kernel :gaussian {:sigma 0.8}) :noise 0.005})
      xtest (m/slice-range -5.0 5.0 60)
      rows (mapv (fn [x [y sd]] {:x x :y y :lo (- y (* 1.96 sd)) :hi (+ y (* 1.96 sd))})
                 xtest (gp/posterior-samples process xtest true (r/rng :mersenne 5)))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data rows :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
    :charts [(chart/ribbon {:mapping {:ymin :lo :ymax :hi} :color [130 170 230] :interpolator :cubic})
             (chart/line {:color :black :line-width 2 :interpolator :cubic})
             (chart/scatter {:data (map (fn [x y] {:x x :y y}) xs ys) :size 9 :color :black})]
    :labels {:title "Gaussian process: a posterior sample with its 95 % band"}}
   {:width 800 :height 500}))




Many samples: 30 posterior curves of a periodic kernel through the three points, 20 prior curves of a Gaussian one.
Source: cljplot - Gaussian process posterior and prior samples.

(let [xs [-4 1 2] ys [-5 1 2]
      xtest (m/slice-range -5.0 5.0 40)
      g (r/rng :mersenne 6)
      periodic (gp/gaussian-process xs ys {:kernel (k/kernel :periodic {:sigma 0.5 :periodicity 8.0}) :noise 0.0001})
      gaussian (gp/gaussian-process xs ys {:kernel (k/kernel :gaussian) :noise 1.0e-7})
      curves (fn [sample-fn n] (vec (for [i (range n) [x y] (map vector xtest (sample-fn))] {:x x :y y :i i})))
      panel (fn [rows title points?]
              {:data rows :mapping {:x :x :y :y :group :i}
               :charts (cond-> [(chart/line {:color [0 0 0 90] :interpolator :cubic})]
                         points? (conj (chart/scatter {:data (map (fn [x y] {:x x :y y}) xs ys) :mapping {:group nil}
                                                       :size 9 :color [215 48 39]})))
               :labels {:title title}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(panel (curves #(gp/posterior-samples periodic xtest false g) 30) "30 posterior samples (periodic kernel)" true)

(let [xtest (m/slice-range -2.0 10.0 200)
      step-plot (fn [i]
                  (let [{:keys [xs ys gp util-best]} (nth bo-1d i)
                        band (mapv (fn [x [mu sd]] {:x x :mu mu :lo (- mu (* 1.96 sd)) :hi (+ mu (* 1.96 sd))})
                                   xtest (gp/predict-all gp (map vector xtest) true))]
                    {:data band :mapping {:x :x}
                     :charts [(chart/ribbon {:mapping {:ymin :lo :ymax :hi} :color [130 170 230]})
                              (chart/function {:f target :line-width 2 :color :black})
                              (chart/line {:mapping {:y :mu} :color [30 60 160] :dash [8 3]})
                              (chart/rule {:x (first util-best) :dash [6 4] :line-width 1.5})
                              (chart/scatter {:data (map (fn [[x] y] {:x x :y y}) xs ys) :mapping {:y :y} :size 8
                                              :color [0 140 140]})]
                     :scales {:y {:domain [-1.0 2.5]}}
                     :labels {:title (str "step " i ", " (count xs) " evaluations") :y nil}}))]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange (mapv step-plot [2 6 10]) {:columns 1})
   {:width 800 :height 750}))




A 2D black box: its contours with every evaluated point, the process mean and its standard deviation after 15 steps.
Source: cljplot - Bayesian optimisation.

(defn black-box
  [[x y]]
  (let [x (double x) y (double y)]
    (* (m/sinc (+ 2.0 x y)) (m/sin (+ x x)) (m/cos (+ y y)) (m/sin (* 2.0 x y)))))


(let [bounds {:x [-1.0 0.5] :y [-2.0 -0.5]}
      {:keys [xs gp x]} (nth (opt/bayesian-optimization black-box {:bounds [(:x bounds) (:y bounds)] :vector-arg? true
                                                                   :rng (r/rng :mersenne 8)})
                             15)
      evaluated (map (fn [[a b]] {:x a :y b}) xs)
      panel (fn [title f]
              {:charts [(chart/field {:f f :domain bounds :n 150})
                        (chart/contour {:f f :domain bounds :n 150 :color [255 255 255 120]})
                        (chart/scatter {:data evaluated :mapping {:x :x :y :y} :size 7 :color :black})
                        (chart/scatter {:data [{:x (first x) :y (second x)}] :mapping {:x :x :y :y} :size 14
                                        :shape \x :color [215 48 39]})]
               :scales {:color {:title nil}}
               :aspect :iso
               :labels {:title title}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(panel "black box and evaluations" black-box)
                  (panel "process mean" (fn [p] (gp/predict gp p)))
                  (panel "process std dev" (fn [p] (second (gp/predict gp p true))))]
                 {:columns 3})
   {:width 1000 :height 400}))

37.3 Functions and fields

(defn fn2d
  "Gives -(x^2 + y^2) sin x sin y sin xy at the point `[x y]`."
  [[^double x ^double y]]
  (* (- (+ (* x x) (* y y))) (m/sin x) (m/sin y) (m/sin (* x y))))


(def fn2d-domain {:x [(- m/PI) m/PI] :y [(- m/PI) m/PI]})


37.3.1 A function of two variables
Source: cljplot - function2d.

(plot/render-image
 {:charts [(chart/field {:f fn2d :domain fn2d-domain :n 300})]
  :aspect :iso
  :labels {:title "-(x^2 + y^2) sin x sin y sin xy"}}
 {:width 650 :height 600})






37.3.2 Its contours
Source: cljplot - contour2d.

(plot/render-image
 {:charts [(chart/contour {:f fn2d :domain fn2d-domain :n 300 :filled true :levels 12})]
  :aspect :iso
  :labels {:title "Filled contours of the same function"}}
 {:width 650 :height 600})






37.3.3 Value noise
Source: cljplot - value noise.

(plot/render-image
 {:charts [(chart/field {:f (fn [[x y]] (r/vnoise x y)) :domain {:x [-6 6] :y [-6 6]} :n 400})]
  :scales {:color {:range [:black :white]}}
  :aspect :iso
  :labels {:title "Value noise"}}
 {:width 650 :height 600})






37.3.4 A complex function
Domain colouring: the hue is the argument of f(z), the brightness its magnitude wrapped into bands (:log2 - where |f| + 1 doubles), every pixel computed (:pixel-color). The three zeros (the cube roots of 1) and the two poles (the square roots of -i) are the points every hue meets at.
Source: cljplot - complex.

(plot/render-image
 {:charts [(chart/field {:pixel-color (field/domain-color (fn [z] (cx/div (cx/sub (cx/mult z (cx/mult z z)) cx/ONE)
                                                                             (cx/add (cx/mult z z) cx/I))))
                         :domain {:x [-2 2] :y [-2 2]}})]
  :aspect :iso
  :labels {:title "(z^3 - 1) / (z^2 + i)" :x "re" :y "im"}}
 {:width 650 :height 600})






37.3.5 Field mapping
Uniform points pushed through a composition of fastmath fields (secant ∘ diamond ∘ power).
Source: cljplot - field.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 11)
      field (f/combine {:type :operation :name :comp
                        :var1 {:type :operation :name :comp
                               :var1 {:type :variation :name :secant :amount 1.0 :config {}}
                               :var2 {:type :variation :name :diamond :amount 1.0 :config {}} :amount 1.0}
                        :var2 {:type :variation :name :power :amount 1.0 :config {}} :amount 1.0})]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data (vf/mapped-points field (repeatedly 200000 #(vector (r/drandom g -4 4) (r/drandom g -4 4))))
    :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
    :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 1 :color [20 40 90 25]})]
    :labels {:title "Points mapped through secant . diamond . power"}}
   {:width 650 :height 600}))






37.3.6 Vector field
Arrows of the hyperbolic field on a shifted grid, over the sine of its heading.
Source: cljplot - vector field.

(let [hyperbolic (f/field :hyperbolic)
      heading (f/heading hyperbolic)
      domain {:x [-3 3] :y [-3 3]}]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data (vf/arrows hyperbolic {:domain domain :n 24 :grid :shifted :length-scale 1.5})
    :mapping {:x :x :y :y :xend :xend :yend :yend}
    :charts [(chart/field {:f (fn [[x y]] (m/sin (heading (v/vec2 x y)))) :domain domain :n 300})
             (chart/segment {:color [90 160 235] :line-width 1.5 :arrow {:end true :size 5}})]
    :scales {:color {:range [:black :white] :title "sin heading"}
             :x {:domain [-3 3] :expand [0 0]} :y {:domain [-3 3] :expand [0 0]}}
    :aspect :iso
    :labels {:title "Hyperbolic field"}}
   {:width 650 :height 600}))






37.3.7 Traces
Points following the exponential field from 3000 random seeds; the traces run off to the right.
Source: cljplot - field trace.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 12)
      seeds (repeatedly 3000 #(vector (r/drandom g -7 7) (r/drandom g -7 7)))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data (vf/traces (f/field :exp) seeds {:steps 200 :step 0.01})
    :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
    :charts [(chart/scatter {:size 1 :color [20 70 140 20]})]
    :scales {:x {:domain [-7 7] :nice false} :y {:domain [-7 7] :nice false}}
    :labels {:title "Traces of the exponential field"}}
   {:width 650 :height 600}))

37.4 Point density

37.4.1 Point cloud
600 000 Gaussian points as a binned density raster.
Source: cljplot - point cloud.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 13)]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data (repeatedly 600000 (fn [] {:x (r/grandom g) :y (r/grandom g)}))
    :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
    :charts [(chart/field {:binned true :n 300})]
    :scales {:color {:range [[10 10 40] [60 40 140] [220 90 120] [255 230 160]] :title "density"}}
    :aspect :iso
    :labels {:title "600 000 points"}}
   {:width 650 :height 600}))




The same kind of cloud drawn by a chart/image callback: it gets the panel’s scales and size and returns an image - here 200 000 translucent pixels.

(plot/render-image
 {:charts [(chart/image {:domain {:x [-4 4] :y [-4 4]}
                         :f (fn [{:keys [x-scale y-scale size]}]
                              (let [[w h] size
                                    g (r/rng :mersenne 14)
                                    canvas (c2d/canvas w h)]
                                (c2d/with-canvas [cv canvas]
                                  (c2d/set-color cv 230 240 255 18)
                                  (dotimes [_ 200000]
                                    (let [x (r/grandom g) y (+ (* 0.6 x) (* 0.8 (r/grandom g)))]
                                      (c2d/rect cv (x-scale x) (y-scale y) 1 1))))
                                canvas))})]
  :theme {:panel {:fill [10 15 40]}}
  :aspect :iso
  :labels {:title "A correlated cloud drawn by a callback"}}
 {:width 650 :height 600})






37.4.2 Hexbin
Two Gaussian clusters counted in flat-topped hexagons.
Source: cljplot - binned heatmap.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 15)]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data (repeatedly 10000 (fn [] (if (< (r/drandom g) 0.5)
                                     {:x (r/grandom g) :y (r/grandom g)}
                                     {:x (r/grandom g -10 1) :y (r/grandom g -10 1)})))
    :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
    :charts [(chart/bin2d {:cell :flat-hex :bins 30})]
    :scales {:color {:range :prl-9}}
    :aspect :iso
    :labels {:title "Two clusters in hexagons"}}
   {:width 650 :height 600}))






37.4.3 Density contours
Old Faithful: the 2D density at a wide and a narrow bandwidth as filled contour bands (nothing below the lowest level), with the eruptions over them.
Source: cljplot - contour. Data: Old Faithful geyser eruptions, R datasets package faithful (Härdle 1991; Azzalini & Bowman 1990); licence: Part of R (GPL-2 | GPL-3).

(let [faithful (nu/dataset :faithful)
      panel (fn [bandwidth levels title]
              {:data faithful :mapping {:x :waiting :y :eruptions}
               :charts [(chart/contour {:bandwidth bandwidth :levels levels :filled true})
                        (chart/contour {:bandwidth bandwidth :levels levels :color [0 0 0 60]})
                        (chart/scatter {:size 4 :color [20 60 120 200]})]
               :legend false
               :labels {:title title :x "waiting time [min]" :y "eruption time [min]"}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(panel [6.0 0.5] 20 "wide bandwidth, 20 levels") (panel [2.0 0.15] 10 "narrow bandwidth, 10 levels")]
                 {:columns 2})
   {:width 1000 :height 500}))

37.5 Lines and walks

37.5.1 Reference lines
Horizontal, vertical and sloped rules with dashes and widths, under a sine.
Source: cljplot - lines.

(plot/render-image
 {:charts [(chart/rule {:y 0 :color :black})
           (chart/rule {:y [1 -1]})
           (chart/rule {:x m/HALF_PI :dash [10 10] :line-width 5})
           (chart/rule {:x (* 0.75 m/TWO_PI) :dash [10 10] :line-width 5 :color [128 0 0 100]})
           (chart/rule {:slope (/ 1.0 (* 0.75 m/TWO_PI)) :intercept -1 :dash [1 2 5 2] :line-width 3})
           (chart/function {:f m/sin :domain [0 m/TWO_PI]})]
  :labels {:title "Rules and a sine"}}
 {:width 900 :height 320})






37.5.2 Wrapped random walk
A drifting 2D walk on a torus: leaving the square on one side, it comes back on the other. A row with a NaN y breaks the line at every wrap; :order :data keeps the walk’s order.
Source: cljplot - wrapped random walk.

(defn- wrap-coordinate
  "`v` wrapped into [-200, 200)."
  ^double [^double v]
  (- (m/mod (+ v 200.0) 400.0) 200.0))


#'galleries.cljplot-extras/wrap-coordinate


(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 16)
      walk (take 3000 (iterate (fn [[x y]] [(+ (double x) 2.0 (r/grandom g 0.0 2.0)) (+ (double y) 0.5 (r/grandom g 0.0 2.0))])
                               [0.0 0.0]))
      wrapped (map (fn [[x y]] [(wrap-coordinate x) (wrap-coordinate y)]) walk)
      rows (mapcat (fn [[[x0 y0] [x1 y1]]]
                     (if (or (> (m/abs (- (double x1) (double x0))) 200.0) (> (m/abs (- (double y1) (double y0))) 200.0))
                       [{:x x0 :y y0} {:x x0 :y ##NaN}]
                       [{:x x0 :y y0}]))
                   (partition 2 1 wrapped))]
  (plot/render-image
   {:data rows :mapping {:x :x :y :y}
    :charts [(chart/line {:order :data :color [0 50 255 150]})]
    :scales {:x {:domain [-200 200]} :y {:domain [-200 200]}}
    :aspect :iso
    :labels {:title "A random walk on a torus"}}
   {:width 650 :height 600}))

37.6 Composite

37.6.1 Stacked strips
One sample, many views on a shared x: jittered points, a rug, a box, a histogram and the extent (mean and range) above a violin, a density and a fine histogram below.
Source: cljplot - strips.

(let [g (r/rng :mersenne 17)
      rows (vec (repeatedly 2000 (fn [] {:v (let [u (r/drandom g)]
                                             (cond (< u 0.5) (r/grandom g)
                                                   (< u 0.65) (r/grandom g -10 2)
                                                   :else (r/grandom g 10 2)))})))
      strip (fn [charts] {:data rows :mapping {:x :v} :charts charts :scales {:x {:domain [-20 20]}} :labels {:x nil :y nil}})]
  (plot/render-image
   (plot/arrange [(strip [(chart/stripplot {:size 6 :color [215 48 39 30] :rng (r/rng :mersenne 18)})])
                  (strip [(chart/rug)])
                  (strip [(chart/box)])
                  (strip [(chart/histogram {:bins 100 :y :count})])
                  (strip [(chart/extent {:method stats/extent :color :black})])
                  (strip [(chart/violin)])
                  (strip [(chart/density {:fill :color})])
                  (strip [(chart/histogram {:bins 150})])]
                 {:columns 1 :heights [1 1 1 1.5 1 3 1.5 1.5]})
   {:width 800 :height 800}))
